en: Scientists recently examined studies on dog intelligence and compared them with research into the minds of other intelligent animals. (19 words)
cn: 科学家们最近对有关犬类智力的研究进行了梳理，并将其与其他智能动物心智方面的研究进行了比较。

en: The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores (食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not surpass other intelligent animals in any of those categories. (32 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，狗在食肉动物、群居猎手以及家养动物这几个类别中，都属于相对更聪明的一类，但它们的智力，在这几个类别中，都并未超越其他智能动物。

en: Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition previously, the authors of this new study found little to warrant the volume of work that has been devoted to the topic. (32 words)
cn: 尽管已经有大量研究此前曾对犬类认知能力进行过探讨，但这项新研究的作者们却发现，几乎没有什么理由能够证明，这一课题所投入的研究工作量是合理的。

en: Stephen Lea, lead author of the new study, argues that many researchers seem to have designed their studies to prove how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains. (31 words)
cn: 新研究的第一作者斯蒂芬·利亚认为，许多研究人员在设计研究时，似乎更倾向于证明狗有多聪明，而不是单纯地去研究狗的大脑本身。

en: Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition, comparing the studies' results with those from research into other animals. (23 words)
cn: 利亚和一位同事查阅了300多项关于犬类认知的研究，并将这些研究结果与针对其他动物的研究结果进行了比较。

en: The researchers made specific comparisons between the different species in different categories of intelligence. (14 words)
cn: 研究人员在不同的智力类别中，对不同物种进行了具体的比较。

en: These comparisons affirmed that dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as formidable as some researchers might have believed. (20 words)
cn: 这些比较证实了狗确实具备智力，但它们的智力，并不如一些研究人员此前所认为的那样强大出众。

en: In many areas, though, comparisons were not possible. (8 words)
cn: 然而，在许多领域，这种比较其实是无法进行的。

en: For example, the researchers noted that both dogs and cats are known to be able to recognize and differentiate human voices. (21 words)
cn: 举例来说，研究人员指出，狗和猫都已被证实能够识别并区分不同的人类声音。

en: But the investigators could not find any data to indicate which species can remember a greater number of distinct human voices, so it was impossible to compare the two on that front. (32 words)
cn: 但研究人员却找不到任何数据，能够表明哪个物种能够记住的不同人类声音数量更多，因此在这一点上，两者根本无法进行比较。

en: However not all researchers agree completely with the finding of this study. (12 words)
cn: 然而，并非所有研究人员都完全认同这项研究的结论。

en: Zachary Silver, an American researcher believes the authors of the new study overstated the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young and there is much to be learned about how dogs think. (45 words)
cn: 美国研究员扎卡里·西尔弗认为，这项新研究的作者们夸大了“犬类研究已投入过多”这一观点，因为犬类认知这一研究领域本身还相当年轻，关于狗究竟是如何思考的，我们还有许多需要了解的地方。

en: A) Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. (10 words)
cn: A) 感恩带来的益处，或许远比我们通常所以为的要更加显著。

en: One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel--an impact that they consistently underestimated. (29 words)
cn: 一项最近的研究要求参与者给某人写一张感谢便条，然后预估对方收到后会感到多么惊喜和快乐——结果发现，参与者对这种影响，始终存在低估的倾向。

en: Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. (10 words)
cn: 另一项研究，则评估了撰写感谢便条对健康所带来的益处。

en: The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduce symptoms of depression. (29 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，即便每周只写三张感谢便条，坚持三周，也能提升生活满意度、增加愉悦感，并减轻抑郁症状。

en: B) While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. (15 words)
cn: B) 尽管围绕感恩展开的这类研究相对较新，但其中所涉及的原理，却绝非什么新鲜事物。

en: Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year-old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. (27 words)
cn: 我在印第安纳大学教授的一门政治哲学课程上，我的学生们正在阅读丹尼尔·笛福那部已有300年历史的《鲁滨逊漂流记》——这部作品，常被视为英语世界出版的第一部小说。

en: Left alone on an unknowing island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament (悲叹). (20 words)
cn: 独自被困在一座陌生的荒岛上、看不到任何获救或逃离的希望，鲁滨逊本有无数值得悲叹的理由。

en: But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck (海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage. (43 words)
cn: 但他并没有向绝望屈服，反而列出了一份自己心怀感激的事物清单，其中就包括：自己是这场海难中唯一的幸存者，而且还能够从沉船残骸中抢救出许多有用的物资。

en: C) Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. (33 words)
cn: C) 笛福的这部杰作，常被誉为世界上最伟大的小说之一，它生动展现了“感恩”这一品质在实践中的样貌，而这幅画面，即便放到今天，依然与我们的生活息息相关。

en: It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，当代心理学和医学，也才刚刚开始追赶上这部作品所蕴含的智慧。

en: Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation. (33 words)
cn: 简而言之，对我们大多数人来说，把注意力放在生活中值得感恩的事物上，要远比放在那些容易引发怨恨和悲叹的事情上，更加有益。

en: D) When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. (27 words)
cn: D) 当我们把注意力集中在那些令人遗憾的事情上——比如失败的感情、家庭纠纷，以及事业和财务上的挫折——我们往往会变得更加懊悔。

en: Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. (22 words)
cn: 反之，当我们把注意力放在那些值得感恩的事情上时，一种更为强烈的幸福感，也往往会随之在我们的生活中蔓延开来。

en: And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health. (36 words)
cn: 尽管没有人会主张刻意培养一种虚假的幸福感，但越来越多的证据表明，“细数自己所拥有的幸福”，是我们能够养成的、有助于促进身心健康的最佳习惯之一。

en: E) Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions. (15 words)
cn: E) 长期以来，感恩在世界许多文化传统中，都占据着一席特殊而尊贵的地位。

en: For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice. (33 words)
cn: 举例来说，一些古代西方哲学家所倡导的感恩，既要持久，也要完整；而一些东方思想家，则将感恩描绘为不仅仅是一种态度，更是一种需要付诸实践的美德。

en: F) Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. (8 words)
cn: F) 近期的科学研究，也印证了这些古老的教诲。

en: Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. (28 words)
cn: 那些经常进行感恩练习的人——比如细数自己的幸福，或是向他人表达感激之情——往往表现出更高的关系满意度，身体疾病的症状也更少。

en: And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. (9 words)
cn: 而这些益处，也不仅仅局限于心理和生理层面。

en: They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy. (19 words)
cn: 它们或许还会体现在道德层面——那些践行感恩的人，看待自己生活的方式也更少物质化，遭受的嫉妒之苦也更少。

en: G) There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. (10 words)
cn: G) 关于感恩为何能带来这些益处，存在着多种解释。

en: One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. (22 words)
cn: 其中一种解释是，表达感激之情，能够鼓励对方继续保持慷慨大方的态度，从而在人际关系中，催生出一种良性循环。

en: Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate (回报) with acts of kindness of their own. (17 words)
cn: 同样地，心怀感恩的人，也更有可能以自己的善举，来回报他人。

en: Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. (30 words)
cn: 从更宏观的角度来看，一个人人彼此心怀感激的社区，往往会比一个充斥着相互猜忌与怨恨的社区，更适宜居住、更令人愉悦。

en: The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. (9 words)
cn: 感恩所带来的积极影响，或许还能延伸得更远。

en: For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. (32 words)
cn: 举例来说，当许多人因为他人为自己所做的事情而感到欣慰时，他们会体验到一种被鼓舞、被提振的感觉，同时也会相应地，加深对整个人类的美好看法。

en: Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them. (29 words)
cn: 有些人甚至会因此受到启发，努力让自己变得更好，更积极地去帮助他人发挥出最好的一面，为周围的世界带来更多的善意。

en: H) Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. (12 words)
cn: H) 感恩往往也能增强人与人之间的联结感。

en: When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. (25 words)
cn: 当人们希望做出能够激发感恩之情的善举时，人际关系中的投入程度，往往会随之提升，这段关系也似乎能够维持得更加长久。

en: And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts. (28 words)
cn: 而当人们感受到更深的联结时，他们也更倾向于选择彼此陪伴，并在日常的一举一动中，展现出自己的深厚情谊。

en: I) Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. (10 words)
cn: I) 当然，善举有时也可能引发不适之感。

en: For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior (别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. (29 words)
cn: 举例来说，如果一个人觉得自己不配得到他人的善意，或是怀疑对方的善举背后别有用心，那么，感恩本该带来的种种益处，也就无从实现了。

en: Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. (26 words)
cn: 同样地，接受他人的善意，也可能催生出一种亏欠感，让受助者觉得自己必须偿还所获得的一切好处。

en: Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. (20 words)
cn: 只有当一个人对自身足够自信、也足够信任他人时，感恩之情才能够真正蓬勃生长。

en: Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. (11 words)
cn: 阻碍感恩之情的另一大障碍，常常被称为“理所当然感”。

en: Instead of experiencing a benefaction (善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit. (31 words)
cn: 有些人不会把他人的善行，当作一种恩惠来体验，反倒将其视为一种理应偿付给自己的东西，认为对方并不因此而应获得任何道义上的赞誉。

en: J) There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude. (17 words)
cn: J) 任何人都可以采取一些切实可行的步骤，来培养自己的感恩之心。

en: One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. (29 words)
cn: 其中一种方式，是定期抽出时间，去想一想那些曾对自己产生过重要影响的人，或者写一张感谢便条，又或者当面向对方表达谢意。

en: Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. (27 words)
cn: 另一些方式，则可以在古老的宗教修行传统中找到，比如反思自己曾从他人那里获得的恩惠，或是真心实意地为施恩者的健康与幸福祈祷。

en: In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. (30 words)
cn: 除了反思自己所获得的恩惠之外，人们同样也可以把关注点，放在自己能够行善的种种机会上——无论是过去已经付诸行动的机会，还是未来所期待的机会。

en: Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. (21 words)
cn: 有些人最为感激的，并非他人为自己所做的事情，而是自己曾有幸帮助他人的机会。

en: In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage. (43 words)
cn: 笛福笔下的鲁滨逊，正是通过不断反思自己生命中值得感恩的种种事物，逐渐相信：与当初若一直留在他出发远航时所在的那个社会相比，如今的自己，已经变成了一个远远更好的人。

en: K) Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. (21 words)
cn: K) 在思考慷慨与感恩这一话题时，伟大的篮球教练约翰·伍登，曾向他的球员和学生们提出过两条忠告。

en: First, he said, 'It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you.' (26 words)
cn: 他首先说道：“除非你曾为一个永远无法回报你的人做过一些事情，否则你不可能拥有完美的一天。”

en: In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. (20 words)
cn: 通过这句话，伍登想要倡导的，是一种纯粹出于慷慨、而非期待回报的善举。

en: Second, he said, 'Give thanks for your blessings every day.' (10 words)
cn: 他的第二条忠告是：“每天都要为自己所拥有的幸福，心怀感恩。”

en: L) Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. (13 words)
cn: L) 一些信仰传统，会把这类感恩实践，融入到日常生活的节律之中。

en: For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. (22 words)
cn: 举例来说，一些宗教的信徒，会在每天清晨起床前和夜晚就寝前，做感恩祷告。

en: Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. (10 words)
cn: 另一些人，则会在一天当中的多个时刻表达谢意，比如在用餐之前。

en: Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers. (18 words)
cn: 而诸如出生、死亡和婚礼这类不那么频繁发生的特殊时刻，也同样可能伴随着这样的祈祷仪式。

en: M) When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. (32 words)
cn: M) 当笛福描绘鲁滨逊·克鲁索把感恩变成自己荒岛生活中每日不可或缺的一部分时，他其实是提前预见到了数百年后，社会科学和医学领域才会出现的相关发现。

en: Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. (18 words)
cn: 然而，与此同时，他也在呼应着可以追溯至数千年前的宗教与哲学传统中所蕴含的智慧。

en: Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them. (37 words)
cn: 感恩，是所有心理状态中最有益健康、也最滋养心灵的一种，而那些把它培养成习惯的人，不仅丰富了自己的人生，也让身边人的生活，因此而变得更加丰盈。

en: Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. (10 words)
cn: 科技，从来都不是一种用于实现人类目的的中立工具。

en: Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. (13 words)
cn: 技术创新在被人类用来掌控周遭环境的同时，也在反过来重塑着人类自身。

en: Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity. (7 words)
cn: 举例来说，人工智能，正在悄然改变着人性本身。

en: While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. (20 words)
cn: 尽管“人工智能”这个词，往往会让人联想到“杀手机器人”或“灾难性失业”这类令人焦虑的场景，但它其实还蕴含着其他更深层次的影响。

en: As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? (17 words)
cn: 随着人工智能日益塑造着人类的生活体验，这一切究竟会如何改变“身而为人”这件事的意义呢？

en: Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications. (17 words)
cn: 这一问题的核心，在于一个人做出选择的能力，尤其是那些涉及道德层面的判断能力。

en: Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them—or habit and practice. (17 words)
cn: 亚里士多德曾主张，做出实际判断的能力，依赖于人们经常性地去做出这样的判断——也就是所谓的习惯与练习。

en: We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves. (28 words)
cn: 我们看到，机器在日常生活的各种情境中，正逐渐取代人类充当“判断者”的角色，而这，对人类自身学习如何有效行使判断力，构成了一种潜在的威胁。

en: In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. (22 words)
cn: 在职场中，管理者们日常需要做出诸如“该雇用还是解雇谁”“该批准哪笔贷款”之类的决策。

en: These are areas where algorithmic (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgments, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will. (30 words)
cn: 而在这些领域，算法所给出的建议，正在逐步取代人类自身的判断——这也就意味着，那些原本有机会在这些领域培养实际判断力的人，如今再也没有了这样的机会。

en: Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. (20 words)
cn: 推荐算法，如今已日益成为人们在文化消费过程中所依赖的中介工具，但它也可能反过来限制人们的选择，并压缩“偶然发现”的空间。

en: By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. (24 words)
cn: 通过向消费者呈现出经算法筛选后的“下一步该看什么、读什么、追什么剧、去哪里”的选项，各大公司实际上是在用机器的品味，取代人类自身的品味。

en: In one sense, this is helpful. (6 words)
cn: 从某种意义上说，这确实有其便利之处。

en: After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own. (26 words)
cn: 毕竟，机器所能浏览的选项范围，远比任何个人凭一己之力、在有限的时间和精力下所能做到的，要广泛得多。

en: At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. (24 words)
cn: 但与此同时，这种筛选机制，本质上是在依据人们过去的偏好，来推算他们未来可能会喜欢的内容。

en: We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way. (21 words)
cn: 我们认为，这其中存在一种风险：人们的选择，可能会以一种全新的、始料未及的方式，被自己的过去所束缚。

en: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. (25 words)
cn: 随着机器学习算法不断改进、并在更庞大的数据集上完成训练，日常生活中越来越多的部分，都很可能变得完全可以预测。

en: The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant. (20 words)
cn: 这些预测将会变得越来越精准，最终，也将让人们日常的各种体验，变得更加高效、也更加令人愉悦。

en: Algorithms could soon—if they don't already—have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. (27 words)
cn: 算法或许很快——甚至可能已经——比你自己更清楚，你接下来想看哪部剧、又该录用哪位求职者。

en: One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display. (23 words)
cn: 有朝一日，人类甚至可能找到一种方法，让机器在做出这类决策时，避开人类通常所固有的那些偏见。

en: But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. (30 words)
cn: 但既然“不可预测性”本就是人类理解自我、乃至喜爱自我的一部分，那么，在这一过程中，人性正在逐渐失去某种至关重要的东西。

en: As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us. (21 words)
cn: 随着人类变得越来越可预测，生活在这个日益被人工智能所主导的世界中的“人类”，也将变得越来越不像我们如今所熟悉的自己。

en: Phonics, which involves sounding out words syllable (音节) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read. (19 words)
cn: “拼读法”——即按音节逐一拼读单词的方法——是教孩子学习阅读的最佳方式。

en: But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. (10 words)
cn: 但在许多课堂上，这个词却几乎成了一个“禁忌词”。

en: So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. (16 words)
cn: 情况严重到，一些教师甚至不得不偷偷地把拼读教学材料带进课堂。

en: Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong. (19 words)
cn: 而大多数美国儿童所接受的阅读教学方法，却一次又一次地被研究证明是错误的。

en: The consequences of this are striking. (6 words)
cn: 由此造成的后果，令人触目惊心。

en: Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. (12 words)
cn: 2017年，只有不到一半的美国成年人具备合格的阅读能力。

en: American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam. (15 words)
cn: 在名为“国际阅读素养进展研究”的国际测评中，美国四年级学生的排名，仅位列第15位。

en: America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. (18 words)
cn: 围绕如何教孩子学习阅读这一问题，美国已陷入了一场持续数十年之久、始终悬而未决的争论之中。

en: Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. (20 words)
cn: 一部分人主张教授“字形—音素”对应关系（比如k这个音，可以拼写成c、k、ck或ch），这种方法被称为“拼读法”。

en: Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as 'whole language'. (19 words)
cn: 另一部分人则支持一种沉浸式的教学方法（比如借助猫的图片来学习“cat”这个单词），这种方法被称为“全语言教学法”。

en: Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the EdWeek Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called 'balanced literacy'. (25 words)
cn: 根据EdWeek研究中心2019年的一项调查，如今，几乎四分之三的教师，采用的是一种被称为“平衡读写教学法”的混合方式。

en: This combination of methods is ineffective. (6 words)
cn: 而这种混合式的教学方法，其实并不奏效。

en: 'You can't sprinkle in a little phonics,' says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. (21 words)
cn: 密西西比州教育部小学教育与阅读事务执行主任特内特·史密斯表示：“你不能只是零星地掺入一点拼读教学。”

en: 'It has to be systematic and explicitly taught.' (8 words)
cn: “拼读教学必须系统化，并且要被明确、清晰地教授。”

en: Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. (11 words)
cn: 密西西比州——一个在社会政策方面常常落后于其他州的地方——却在这一领域，树立了一个值得借鉴的榜样。

en: In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. (20 words)
cn: 这个曾因阅读成绩低迷而声名狼藉的州，在2013年由州立法机构通过了新的读写能力标准。

en: Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. (7 words)
cn: 自那以来，密西西比州取得了显著的进步。

en: Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. (23 words)
cn: 在名为“全国教育进展评估”的全国性测评中，该州四年级学生的排名，从（全美50个州中的）第49位，一跃提升到了第29位。

en: In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. (11 words)
cn: 2019年，它更是全美唯一一个成绩实现提升的州。

en: For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state. (21 words)
cn: 自有相关测评记录以来，密西西比州的学生首次达到了“平均阅读水平”——对于这样一个相对贫困的州来说，这无疑是一项了不起的成就。

en: Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. (20 words)
cn: 密西西比州的成功，得益于其采用了一套建立在“阅读科学”这一研究体系之上的阅读教学方法。

en: In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the 'reading wars' and synthesize the evidence. (33 words)
cn: 1997年，美国国会要求国家儿童健康与人类发展研究所以及教育部，联合召集了一个“全国阅读专家组”，旨在终结这场“阅读教学之争”，并对现有证据进行系统梳理。

en: The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic (音位的) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best. (18 words)
cn: 该专家组的研究发现，拼读法——再辅以对音位意识、流畅性和理解能力的明确教学——才是效果最好的教学方式。

en: Yet over two decades on, 'balanced literacy' is still being taught in classrooms. (13 words)
cn: 然而，二十多年过去了，“平衡读写教学法”，却依然在课堂上被广泛使用。

en: But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. (12 words)
cn: 但统计学和脑成像技术的进步，早已证伪了“全语言教学法”的有效性。

en: To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. (26 words)
cn: 对于那些本身就是熟练阅读者的教师来说，阅读似乎是一种依靠“有根据的猜测”便能自然习得的过程，而不是拼读法所强调的那种需要刻意训练的过程。

en: Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through osmosis (潜移默化) when they were children. (15 words)
cn: 这些教师很容易认为，自己小时候，也是通过潜移默化的方式，自然而然地学会了阅读。

en: Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms. (8 words)
cn: 而在缺乏专业培训的情况下，他们也就把这种未经检验的想法，带进了自己的课堂。

en: Imagine sitting down to a big dinner; a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. (20 words)
cn: 想象一下，你正坐下来准备享用一顿丰盛的晚餐：一块厚实的牛排、满满一大份炸薯条，餐后还有蛋糕作为甜点。

en: After eating so much, you should be too full to eat another bite. (13 words)
cn: 吃下这么多东西之后，你理应已经饱得再也吃不下一口了。

en: But some people experience a powerful urge to keep eating, even after indulging in a huge meal, a behavior that makes little sense, as most adults are well-versed in the dangers of obesity, which researchers have shown correlates with innumerable health issues and is even linked to increased mortality risk. (50 words)
cn: 但有些人却会体验到一种强烈的冲动，想要在饱餐一顿之后依然继续进食——这种行为其实并不合理，因为大多数成年人都很清楚肥胖所带来的各种危害，而研究人员已经证明，肥胖与数不胜数的健康问题相关，甚至还与死亡率的上升存在关联。

en: But some people still keep eating long after they should stop, a phenomenon Dr. Susan Thompson calls 'insatiable (永不满足的) hunger.' (20 words)
cn: 但有些人，即便早已过了该停止进食的时候，依然会持续不停地吃下去——苏珊·汤普森博士将这种现象称为“永不满足的饥饿感”。

en: 'It is characterized by two main attributes: not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary (久坐不动的).' (20 words)
cn: “这种现象的特征，主要体现在两个方面：一是无论吃多少都得不到满足，二是有一种想要久坐不动的强烈倾向。”

en: This is at odds with how humans are biologically programmed. (10 words)
cn: 这与人类在生物学层面上的天生程序设定，正好相悖。

en: When there was a great deal of food available, ancient people would gorge on calories; this massive calorie intake was accompanied by an urge to get active. (27 words)
cn: 在食物充足的年代，原始人类往往会大量摄入热量；而这种大量的热量摄入，通常也会伴随着一种想要变得活跃、多加运动的冲动。

en: Humans were also programmed for something called 'compensation,' which is the brain's regulatory mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight. (21 words)
cn: 人类体内还预先设定了一种被称为“补偿机制”的程序，这是大脑用来防止体重过度堆积的一种调节机制。

en: With compensation, if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally inclined to eat less for the rest of the day. (24 words)
cn: 借助这种补偿机制，如果你在早上吃了一顿丰盛的大餐，那么在这一天接下来的时间里，你自然而然地就会倾向于少吃一些。

en: But recent studies show that 70% of American adults have lost the ability to naturally compensate for the calories they consume: worse still, a significant number of them report diminishing hunger halfway through an eating session, but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down. (57 words)
cn: 但最近的研究表明，70%的美国成年人已经丧失了这种自然补偿摄入热量的能力：更糟糕的是，其中相当一部分人报告说，自己在一顿饭吃到一半时，饥饿感就已经开始减退，但等到这顿饭吃完时，他们所感受到的饥饿程度，却与刚开始吃饭时相同、甚至更为强烈。

en: Dr. Thompson argues that the main cause of this phenomenon is the modern diet, which is comprise of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories. (25 words)
cn: 汤普森博士认为，造成这一现象的主要原因，在于现代饮食结构——它主要由高糖、高碳水化合物、高热量的食物所构成。

en: A) When psychologist Jessica Pryor lived near an internationally renowned university, she once saw a student walking into a library holding a sleeping bag and a coffee maker. (28 words)
cn: A) 心理学家杰西卡·普赖尔曾住在一所享誉国际的大学附近，她曾亲眼看到一名学生抱着睡袋和咖啡机走进图书馆。

en: She has heard of graduate students spending 12 to 18 hours at a time in the lab. (17 words)
cn: 她也曾听说过，有研究生一次就要在实验室里待上12到18个小时。

en: Their schedules are meant to be literally punishing: If they are scientists-in-training, they won't allow themselves to watch Netflix until their experiments start generating results. (25 words)
cn: 他们的日程安排，几乎堪称是一种自我惩罚：如果他们是正在接受训练的科研人员，那么在实验出成果之前，他们就绝不允许自己看奈飞。

en: 'Relationships become estranged (疏远的) —people stop inviting them to social gatherings or dinner parties, which leads them to spend even more time in the lab,' Pryor told me. (28 words)
cn: 普赖尔告诉我：“人际关系会因此变得疏远——身边的人不再邀请他们参加社交聚会或晚宴，而这，又反过来促使他们把更多时间耗在实验室里。”

en: B) Along with other therapists, Pryor, who is now with the Family Institute at Northwestern University, is trying to sound the alarm about a tendency among young adults and college students to strive for perfection in their work—sometimes at any cost. (41 words)
cn: B) 如今任职于西北大学家庭研究所的普赖尔，正与其他心理治疗师一道，试图敲响警钟，提醒人们关注这样一种倾向：年轻人和大学生，往往在工作中一味追求完美——有时甚至不惜付出任何代价。

en: Though it is often portrayed as a positive trait, Pryor and others say extreme perfectionism can lead to depression, anxiety, and even suicide. (23 words)
cn: 尽管完美主义常常被描绘成一种积极的品质，但普赖尔等人却指出，极端的完美主义，可能导致抑郁、焦虑，甚至走向自杀。

en: C) What's more, perfectionism seems to be on the rise. (10 words)
cn: C) 更为严重的是，完美主义倾向似乎正呈上升趋势。

en: In a study of thousands of American, Canadian and British college students published earlier this year, Thomas Curran of the University of Bath and Andrew Hill of York St. John University found that today's college students report higher levels of perfectionism than college students did during the 1990s or early 2000s. (51 words)
cn: 在今年早些时候发表的一项针对数千名美国、加拿大和英国大学生的研究中，巴斯大学的托马斯·科伦和约克圣约翰大学的安德鲁·希尔发现，如今的大学生所报告的完美主义水平，要高于20世纪90年代或21世纪初的大学生。

en: They measured three types of perfectionism: self-oriented, or a desire to be perfect; socially prescribed, or a desire to live up to others' expectations; and other-oriented, or holding others to unrealistic standards. (32 words)
cn: 他们测量了三种类型的完美主义：一种是“自我导向型”，即追求自身完美的渴望；一种是“社会期许型”，即渴望达到他人期望的心理；还有一种是“他人导向型”，即对他人抱有不切实际的高标准。

en: From 1989 to 2016, they found, self-oriented perfectionism scores increased by 10 percent, socially prescribed scores rose by 33 percent, and other-oriented perfectionism increased by 16 percent. (27 words)
cn: 他们发现，从1989年到2016年，“自我导向型”完美主义的得分上升了10%，“社会期许型”得分上升了33%，而“他人导向型”完美主义的得分，也上升了16%。

en: D) A person living with an other-oriented perfectionist might feel criticized by the perfectionist spouse for not doing household chores exactly the 'right' way. (24 words)
cn: D) 与一个“他人导向型”完美主义者共同生活的人，可能会因为家务没有按照“正确”的方式完成，而不断受到这位完美主义伴侣的批评指责。

en: 'One of the most common things couples argue about is the proper way of loading the dishwasher,' says Amy Bach, a psychologist in Providence Rhode Island. (26 words)
cn: 罗德岛州普罗维登斯市的心理学家艾米·巴赫说：“情侣之间最常争论的事情之一，就是该如何‘正确地’摆放洗碗机里的餐具。”

en: E) Curran describes socially prescribed perfectionism as 'My self-esteem is contingent on what other people think.' (16 words)
cn: E) 科伦将“社会期许型”完美主义描述为：“我的自我价值感，完全取决于别人怎么看我。”

en: His study didn't examine the causal reasons for its rise, but he assumes that the rise of both standardized testing and social media might play a role. (27 words)
cn: 他的研究并未深入探讨这种完美主义上升背后的原因，但他推测，标准化考试和社交媒体的兴起，或许在其中起到了一定的作用。

en: These days, LinkedIn alerts us when our rival gets a new job, and Instagram can let us know how well 'liked' our lives are compared with a friend's. (28 words)
cn: 如今，当我们的竞争对手换了新工作，领英会第一时间通知我们；而Instagram也能让我们清楚地看到，与朋友相比，自己的生活获得了多少“点赞”。

en: In an opinion piece earlier this year, Curran and Hill argue that society has also become more 'dog-eat-dog.' (18 words)
cn: 在今年早些时候发表的一篇评论文章中，科伦和希尔提出，如今的社会也变得更加“弱肉强食”。

en: Over the last 50 years, public interest and civic responsibility have been progressively eroded, 'they write,' replaced by a focus on self-interest and competition in a supposedly free and open marketplace. (31 words)
cn: 他们写道，在过去的50年间，公共利益和公民责任感一直在不断被侵蚀，取而代之的，是在一个所谓“自由开放”的市场中，对自身利益和竞争的过度关注。

en: We strive for perfection, it seems, because we feel we must in order to get ahead. (16 words)
cn: 我们之所以拼命追求完美，似乎是因为我们觉得，只有这样才能在竞争中脱颖而出、取得领先。

en: Michael Brustein, a clinical psychologist in Manhattan, says when he first began practicing in 2007, he was surprised by how prevalent perfectionism was among his clients, despite how little his graduate training had focused on the phenomenon. (37 words)
cn: 曼哈顿的临床心理学家迈克尔·布鲁斯坦说，2007年他刚开始执业时，就对来访者中完美主义倾向的普遍程度感到十分惊讶——尽管他在研究生阶段所接受的训练，几乎很少涉及这一现象。

en: He sees perfectionism in, among others, clients who are entrepreneurs, artists, and tech employees. (14 words)
cn: 在他的来访者中，创业者、艺术家和科技行业从业者，都常常表现出明显的完美主义倾向。

en: 'You're in New York because you're ambitious, you have this need to strive,' he says. (15 words)
cn: 他说：“你之所以会来纽约，正是因为你有野心，内心怀揣着一种不断进取的渴望。”

en: 'But then your whole identity gets wrapped into a goal.' (10 words)
cn: “但渐渐地，你的整个身份认同，就都被裹挟进了某一个具体的目标之中。”

en: F) Perfectionism can, of course, be a positive force. (9 words)
cn: F) 当然，完美主义也可以成为一种积极的推动力量。

en: Think of professional athletes, who train aggressively for ever-higher levels of competition. (12 words)
cn: 不妨想想职业运动员，他们为了在竞技中不断突破更高水平，往往会进行极其严苛的高强度训练。

en: In well-adjusted perfectionism, someone who doesn't get the gold is able to forget the setback and move on. (18 words)
cn: 在“良性调适型”完美主义中，一个未能赢得金牌的人，能够放下这次挫折，继续向前迈进。

en: In maladaptive (不当的) perfectionism meanwhile, people make an archive of all their failures. (13 words)
cn: 与此同时，在“不当型”完美主义中，人们却会把自己所有的失败经历，全都归档保存起来。

en: They revisit these archives constantly, thinking, as Pryor puts it, 'I need to make myself feel terrible so I don't do this again.' (23 words)
cn: 正如普赖尔所说，他们会不断地回顾这些“失败档案”，反复告诉自己：“我得让自己感到痛苦难受，这样才不会再犯同样的错误。”

en: Then they double down, 'raising the expectation bar even higher, which increases the likelihood of defeat, which makes you self-critical, so you raise the bar higher, work even harder,' she says. (31 words)
cn: 她说，接下来他们会变本加厉，“不断把期望的标准调得更高，这也随之增加了失败的可能性，而失败又会让人变得更加自我苛责，于是他们又把标准调得更高，逼自己更加拼命地努力。”

en: Next comes failure, shame, and pushing yourself even harder toward even higher and more impossible goals. (16 words)
cn: 紧接着而来的，便是失败、羞愧，以及不断把自己推向更高、更加不切实际的目标。

en: Meeting them becomes an 'all or nothing' premise. (8 words)
cn: 要想真正达成这些目标，也逐渐变成了一种“要么全有、要么全无”的极端前提。

en: Pryor offered this example: 'Even if I'm an incredible attorney, if I don't make partner in the same pacing as one of my colleagues, clearly that means I'm a failure.' (30 words)
cn: 普赖尔举了这样一个例子：“即便我是一名出类拔萃的律师，只要我晋升合伙人的速度没能跟上某位同事，那显然就意味着，我是个失败者。”

en: G) Brustein says his perfectionist clients tend to devalue their accomplishments, so that every time a goal is achieved, the high lasts only a short time, like 'a gas tank with a hole in it.' (35 words)
cn: G) 布鲁斯坦说，他的完美主义来访者们，往往倾向于贬低自己所取得的成就，因此每当他们达成一个目标时，那种成就感也只能维持很短的时间，就像“一个漏了洞的油箱”，油再多也留不住。

en: 'If the boss says you did a great job, it's because he doesn't know anything.' (15 words)
cn: “如果老板夸你做得很棒，那只是因为他其实什么都不懂。”

en: 'If the audience likes your work, that's because it's too stupid to know what good art actually is.' (18 words)
cn: “如果观众喜欢你的作品，那也只是因为他们太外行，根本不懂什么才是真正的好艺术。”

en: But, therapists say, there are also different ways perfectionism manifests. (10 words)
cn: 不过，治疗师们也指出，完美主义的表现形式，其实各不相同。

en: Some perfectionists are always pushing themselves forward. (7 words)
cn: 有些完美主义者，会不断地逼迫自己向前冲。

en: But others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect. (16 words)
cn: 但另一些人，实际上却会在工作中拖延落后，除非能够做到尽善尽美，否则根本无法完成任务。

en: Or they might handicap their performance ahead of time. (9 words)
cn: 又或者，他们会提前给自己的表现设置障碍。

en: They're the ones partying until 2 a.m. the night before the final, so that when the grade C rolls in, there's a ready excuse. (24 words)
cn: 他们往往就是那种，在期末考试前一晚还party到凌晨两点的人，这样一来，等成绩单上出现C的时候，自己也就有了一个现成的借口。

en: H) While educators and parents have successfully convinced students of the need to be high performing and diligent, the experts told me, they haven't adequately prepared them for the inevitability of failure. (32 words)
cn: H) 专家们告诉我，尽管教育者和家长已经成功地让学生们相信，自己必须表现优异、勤奋刻苦，但他们却并未为学生们做好足够的准备，去坦然面对失败终将不可避免这一事实。

en: Instead of praises like 'You're so smart,' parents and educators should say things like 'You really stuck with it,' Pryor says, to emphasize the value of perseverance over intrinsic talent. (30 words)
cn: 普赖尔说，与其像“你真是太聪明了”这样的夸奖，家长和教育者更应该说“你真的很坚持”这样的话，以此来强调坚韧不拔的价值，而非天生的才华。

en: Pryor notes that many of her clients are wary she'll 'turn them into some degenerate couch potato and teach them to be okay with it.' (25 words)
cn: 普赖尔指出，她的许多来访者，都对她心存戒备，担心她会“把自己变成一个消沉懒散的‘沙发土豆’，还教他们坦然接受这种状态”。

en: Instead, she tries to help them think through the parts of their perfectionism they'd like to keep, and to lose the parts that are ruining their lives. (27 words)
cn: 但事实并非如此，她所努力做的，是帮助他们理清自己完美主义中，哪些部分值得保留，哪些部分正在毁掉他们的生活，从而学会取舍。

en: I) Bach, who sees many students from Brown University, says some of them don't even go out on weekends, let alone weekdays. (22 words)
cn: I) 巴赫接诊过许多来自布朗大学的学生，她说，其中有些学生甚至连周末都不出门，更不用说平日了。

en: She tells them, 'Aim high, but get comfortable with good enough.' (11 words)
cn: 她会告诉他们：“志向要远大，但也要学会坦然接受‘足够好’就已经很好了。”

en: When they don't get some award, she encourages them to remember that 'one outcome is not a basis or a broad conclusion about the person's intelligence, qualifications, or potential for the future.' (32 words)
cn: 每当他们未能获得某项奖项时，她都会鼓励他们记住：“一次结果，并不能构成评判一个人智力、能力，或未来潜力的依据或全面结论。”

en: J) The treatment for perfectionism might be as simple as having patients keep logs of things they can be proud of, or having them behave imperfectly in small ways, just to see how it feels. (35 words)
cn: J) 治疗完美主义的方法，有时可能简单到，只是让患者记录下那些自己值得骄傲的小事，或者让他们在一些小事上故意做得不那么完美，去亲身体会一下那是什么感觉。

en: 'We might have them hang the towels crooked (不正的) or wear some clothing inside out,' says Martin Antony, a professor in the department of psychology at Ryerson University in Toronto. (30 words)
cn: 多伦多瑞尔森大学心理学系教授马丁·安东尼说：“我们有时会让他们故意把毛巾挂得歪歪扭扭，或者把衣服反着穿。”

en: K) Brustein likes to get his perfectionist clients to create values that are important to them, then try to shift their focus to living according to those values rather than achieving specific goals. (33 words)
cn: K) 布鲁斯坦喜欢引导他的完美主义来访者，去梳理出那些对自己真正重要的价值观，然后试着把关注的重心，从“达成具体目标”，转向“按照这些价值观去生活”。

en: It's a play on the 'You really stuck with it' message for kids. (13 words)
cn: 这其实是对前文提到的、鼓励孩子“你真的很坚持”这一理念的一种延伸运用。

en: In other words, it isn't about doing a headstand in yoga class; it's about going to yoga class in the first place, because you like to be the kind of person who takes care of herself. (36 words)
cn: 换句话说，重点并不在于你能否在瑜伽课上完成一个倒立动作，而在于你首先愿意去上这堂瑜伽课——因为你希望自己成为那种懂得照顾自己的人。

en: But he warns that some people go into therapy expecting too much—an instant transformation of themselves from a pathological (病态的) perfectionist to a (still high achieving) non-perfectionist. (27 words)
cn: 但他也提醒道，有些人在接受治疗时，期望值往往过高——他们希望自己能立刻从一个病态的完美主义者，摇身一变，成为一个（依然表现优异、但）不再是完美主义者的人。

en: They try to be perfect, in other words, at no longer being perfect. (13 words)
cn: 换句话说，他们其实是在拼尽全力，追求“完美地不再追求完美”这件事本身。

en: How on earth did we come to this? (8 words)
cn: 我们究竟是怎么走到这一步的？

en: We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. (21 words)
cn: 我们对孩子的保护近乎痴迷，不放过任何潜在的伤害；我们仔细审视孩子所接触到的每一位照护者、教师或医生。

en: Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access. (20 words)
cn: 然而，尽管如此，却有这样一个群体——它们丝毫没有真正把孩子的最大利益放在心上——却几乎能够毫无阻碍地接触到孩子。

en: We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. (19 words)
cn: 我们似乎理所当然地默许了广告商和营销人员，去对哪怕是年龄最小的孩子，进行心理层面的塑造和影响。

en: Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. (39 words)
cn: 甚至在孩子们尚未建立起健全的自我认知、也还没学会如何管理金钱之前，他们就已经被诱导着，把身份地位和自我价值，与物质商品捆绑在一起，并转而向名气和财富这类外在的事物，去寻求自我认可。

en: We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live. (24 words)
cn: 我们正在培养出的，是一群小小的“消费者”，而不是那些懂得从自己对所处社会所做出的贡献中，去获得自我价值感的年轻公民。

en: We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it. (14 words)
cn: 我们是如此循序渐进地走到今天这一步的，以至于我们当中的许多人，甚至从未对此产生过任何质疑。

en: It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents. (30 words)
cn: 自广告商开始将目标对准年轻一代、并发现他们可以被“招募”来对父母展开商业攻势以来，这一趋势就已经在长达60年的时间里，悄无声息地渗透进了我们的生活。

en: We've come to know it as 'pester power' or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases. (20 words)
cn: 我们如今把这种现象，称为“软磨硬泡的力量”——即孩子通过不断纠缠，向父母施压，迫使他们购买特定商品的能力。

en: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness. (31 words)
cn: 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育工作者，都援引研究指出，这种正在形成的、从摇篮到坟墓贯穿一生的消费主义倾向，正在导致低自尊、抑郁以及其他各类心理疾病发生率的不断攀升。

en: Not all psychologists agree. (4 words)
cn: 但并非所有心理学家都认同这一观点。

en: There are plenty working hand in glove with a £12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form—often literally. (26 words)
cn: 有相当一部分心理学家，其实是在与这个年产值高达120亿英镑的产业密切合作——而这个产业，早已把操纵成年人的情绪与欲望，发展成了一门艺术，而且往往是名副其实的艺术。

en: It's also one that forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. (33 words)
cn: 这个产业还在不断开发新的手段，来诱使孩子们渴望拥有各种物质商品；而由于广告本身具有“病毒式传播”的效应，它们往往只需要“感染”少数几个孩子，便能借由孩子之间的相互影响，波及到更广泛的群体。

en: Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children. (10 words)
cn: 广告和营销，对孩子而言，其实也能发挥一些有益的作用。

en: Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood. (22 words)
cn: 营销活动或许有助于让孩子学会以消费者的身份融入社会，向他们介绍相关产品信息，并在他们步入成年之际，帮助他们塑造出属于自己的独特身份。

en: Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children? (10 words)
cn: 那么，我们是否应该全面禁止一切针对幼童的广告呢？

en: I say yes. (3 words)
cn: 我的答案是：应该。

en: Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s. (16 words)
cn: 当然，针对全面禁止面向11岁以下儿童投放广告这一提议，反对的声音必定不会少。

en: There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products. (28 words)
cn: 会有人辩称，这样做会侵犯言论自由，也会侵害企业向孩子们进行“洗脑”、诱使他们索求其产品的权利。

en: Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions. (41 words)
cn: 大多数家长，都厌恶广告对自己孩子所造成的影响，但我们其实是拥有能力去终止这一切的——让孩子们在真正有能力自主做决定之前，能够摆脱许多消费主义所带来的压力，健康成长。

en: And though advertising is only part of an all-pervasive (无处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere. (19 words)
cn: 尽管广告，只是这种无处不在的营销文化的一部分，但我们终究需要找一个起点，先行动起来。

en: Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now. (13 words)
cn: 那就让我们从现在开始，全面禁止一切针对小学及以下年龄段儿童的广告吧。

en: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. (18 words)
cn: 许多人反对职场监控，因为它天生就带有一种非人性化的影响，也会给员工带来持续不断的压力。

en: But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. (22 words)
cn: 但随着各大企业都希望通过压榨员工的生产效率，来实现更高的运营效率，职场监控在全球范围内，正呈现出不断上升的趋势。

en: More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used 'non-traditional' monitoring techniques on staff last year. (19 words)
cn: 去年，年营收超过7.5亿美元的公司中，有超过一半都对员工采用了“非传统”的监控手段。

en: Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. (27 words)
cn: 对员工绩效进行监控，能让企业有能力评估员工的工作表现和相互协作的情况，而这，对企业和员工双方而言，都可能是有益的。

en: A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. (9 words)
cn: 越来越多的数据分析公司，开始提供这类服务。

en: They gather 'data exhaust' left by employees' email and instant messaging apps; and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. (23 words)
cn: 它们会收集员工使用邮件和即时通讯软件时所留下的“数据痕迹”，并使用配备了射频识别装置和麦克风的员工工牌。

en: These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. (22 words)
cn: 借助这些设备，企业可以监测你说话的时长、音量和语气，即便你在对话中并没有占据主导地位。

en: While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment. (18 words)
cn: 尽管这听起来颇具侵入性，但支持者却认为，这也能够保护员工，免受欺凌和性骚扰之害。

en: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. (9 words)
cn: 这类数据分析，有时也会产生一些出人意料的结果。

en: For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis. (41 words)
cn: 举例来说，研究发现，坐在12人餐桌就餐的员工，往往比经常坐在4人餐桌就餐的员工，有更多的互动交流、更频繁地分享想法，工作表现也更为出色——如果没有这类数据分析，这一事实很可能永远都不会被人发现。

en: Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular 'chipping parties', where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. (29 words)
cn: 过去几年间，斯德哥尔摩一家名为“Epicenter”的联合办公空间，做得更加“出格”——它举办了颇受欢迎的“植入芯片派对”，人们可以在这里把微芯片植入自己的手部。

en: They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. (18 words)
cn: 他们可以利用这些植入的芯片，来开启电子门禁，或者监测打字速度与心率之间的关联性。

en: Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices. (20 words)
cn: 体内植入芯片，听起来或许有些极端，但从身份证件和生物识别技术，发展到这类植入设备，其实只是相对较小的一步跨越。

en: As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. (31 words)
cn: 只要这类计划是完全自愿参与的，那么随着越来越多以便利为导向的应用场景不断涌现，很可能会有相当数量的员工，选择主动植入芯片。

en: But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. (19 words)
cn: 但如果植入芯片被用来压缩员工的空闲时间或休息时间，那就可能会带来负面影响。

en: And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. (13 words)
cn: 而一旦监控工具剥夺了员工的自主权，这类工具也就会变得最不受欢迎。

en: A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged. (18 words)
cn: 这在很大程度上，取决于企业如何向员工传达这类监控举措的目的和方式，而这，也可能有助于避免员工产生抵触甚至抗议的情绪。

en: If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. (9 words)
cn: 如果管理层未能有效沟通，员工往往就会往最坏的方向去揣测。

en: But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. (25 words)
cn: 但如果企业能够坦诚公开自己所收集的信息、以及这些信息的具体用途，研究表明，约有46%的员工，总体上是能够接受这种做法的。

en: Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties. (24 words)
cn: 尽管许多此类监控计划都采用了匿名化数据处理、且参与也完全出于自愿，但仍有许多员工对此心存疑虑，担心自己的公民自由权利，会因此受到侵蚀。

en: So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. (19 words)
cn: 因此，职场监控，既可能为员工赋能，也可能对那些希望提升效率和盈利能力的企业有所助益。

en: But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive. (18 words)
cn: 但如果实施方式不当，它同样也可能沦为一种不受欢迎的压迫性工具，最终反倒适得其反。

en: You might not know yourself as well as you think. (10 words)
cn: 你可能并不像自己以为的那样了解自己。

en: According to a new study, people are relatively accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. (16 words)
cn: 一项新的研究表明，人们只能相对准确地判断自己的部分行为。

en: While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study probes how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. (35 words)
cn: 以往关于人们对自我了解程度的研究，大多聚焦于长期稳定的人格特质，而这项新研究探究的，则是人们对自己每时每刻行为表现的理解程度。

en: Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically activated every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. (25 words)
cn: 研究人员要求参与者佩戴录音设备，该设备会在早上7点到凌晨2点之间，每隔9.5分钟自动启动一次，录制30秒的音频。

en: These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to recall how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. (28 words)
cn: 随后，研究人员每天会向这些参与者发送四次电子邮件问卷，要求他们回忆自己在某一特定小时内表现得有多外向、随和或尽责。

en: The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two consecutive weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks. (29 words)
cn: 这项研究使用了248名参与者的数据，他们都连续两周回答了有关自身行为的问题，并在其中一周佩戴了录音设备。

en: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's assessment of themselves. (19 words)
cn: 六名实验室助理对每位参与者的录音片段进行了评分，以观察他们的观察结果与参与者的自我评估之间存在怎样的差异。

en: The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. (18 words)
cn: 在被观察者的行为表现上，这六名助理的判断总体上是一致的。

en: Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. (19 words)
cn: 此外，在外向程度和尽责程度这两方面，参与者对自己的评价与观察者的评价也是一致的。

en: But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. (13 words)
cn: 但在随和程度这一方面，参与者与外部观察者之间的一致性则要小得多。

en: Some of this discrepancy could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read cues like body language, but there are probably other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. (44 words)
cn: 造成这种差异的部分原因，可能是观察者只能依靠音频片段，因而无法察觉肢体语言之类的线索，但恐怕还存在其他一些解释，因为人们理应能够通过声音听出，一名参与者到底是表现得友善还是粗鲁。

en: The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather deny rude behavior. (23 words)
cn: 参与者自认为的行为表现与观察者所听到的实际情况之间之所以吻合度不高，或许是因为人们更倾向于否认自己存在粗鲁的行为。

en: A) We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness. (7 words)
cn: A) 我们正在经历一场“小”的复兴。

en: Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. (13 words)
cn: 农贸市场、微型住宅和自酿啤酒馆，都体现了我们对“小”的喜爱。

en: So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. (9 words)
cn: 特许学校、咖啡馆和本地书店也是如此。

en: Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are. (35 words)
cn: “小”往往（但并非总是）意味着更实惠、更健康、也更可持续，但它最出色的特质——那个能把魅力升华为热爱的特质——在于“化小”能让我们更充分地成为真实的自己。

en: B) In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered 'mid sized'. (22 words)
cn: B) 而在高等教育领域，趋势却大多恰恰相反：拥有2万或3万名学生的大学，只能算是“中等规模”。

en: The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. (20 words)
cn: 美国规模最大的大学——亚利桑那州立大学，目前拥有8万名在校生，并计划再招收10万名在线学生。

en: At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. (40 words)
cn: 而在另一个极端，则有为数不多的几所学院，在校生不足百人，也不开设在线课程，比如斯特林学院、托马斯·摩尔文理学院和深泉学院。

en: These colleges are so small that they can only be called 'tiny.' (12 words)
cn: 这些学院规模之小，只能被称为“微型”学院。

en: C) Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person's intellect, but on the young person as a whole. (19 words)
cn: C) 微型学院所关注的，并不仅仅是年轻人的智力发展，而是他们的全面发展。

en: Equally important, tiny colleges ask, 'How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?' (18 words)
cn: 同样重要的是，微型学院会追问：“教育究竟该如何促进人类的繁荣与世界的福祉？”

en: And they shape a college experience to address that question. (10 words)
cn: 并据此塑造出一种能够回应这一问题的大学教育体验。

en: They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities. (20 words)
cn: 它们不再执着于学校自身规模的扩张，而是转而关注学生作为社区中全面发展的参与者所取得的成长。

en: D) I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career—a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. (26 words)
cn: D) 在我的职业生涯中，我有幸曾在三所不同的高等院校任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中等规模的公立大学。

en: I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. (32 words)
cn: 但我也曾对这几所院校、以及许多同事深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生、为他们承担成年后的种种责任做准备这一方面。

en: Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. (20 words)
cn: 行政管理人员专注于大学的经营运作，而大多数教师则专注于自身的学术研究和本学科的教学。

en: Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings. (14 words)
cn: 至于学生如何作为独立个体和社会成员逐渐走向成熟，却鲜有人刻意投入关注。

en: E) Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college, Flagstaff College. (26 words)
cn: E) 我刚从一所公立大学退休，如今正返回我的家乡——亚利桑那州的弗拉格斯塔夫，去创办一所名为“弗拉格斯塔夫学院”的微型学院。

en: I'm convinced there's a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. (26 words)
cn: 我坚信，社会需要另一种类型的教育——一种致力于帮助学生认识自我、并融入这个既美好又充满困扰的世界的教育。

en: Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. (21 words)
cn: 年轻人所需要的教育，不仅要传授给他们知识和技能，还应赋予他们意义感、希望、勇气与热情。

en: Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education. (12 words)
cn: 而我认为，大型院校恰恰是最不适合提供这类教育的地方。

en: F) There's no 'best of' list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. (16 words)
cn: F) 就微型学院而言，目前尚不存在什么“最佳排行榜”，至少现在还没有。

en: But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education. (24 words)
cn: 但在全国各地，人们正在创办新的学院，以此作为小型文理学院、大型公立大学和在线教育之外的另一种选择。

en: G) With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical. (20 words)
cn: G) 深泉学院仅有26名学生，是全美规模最小的学院，很可能也是最非典型的一所。

en: Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for 'a life of service to humanity.' (31 words)
cn: 深泉学院坐落在加州与内华达州交界处的一座正常运营的牧场上，是一所私立的两年制男子寄宿学院，致力于培养学生投身“服务人类的一生”。

en: Founded by the electricity tycoon L.L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs' 'curriculum' revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance. (18 words)
cn: 深泉学院由电力大亨L.L.纳恩于1917年创立，其“课程体系”围绕学术、劳动和自治三方面展开。

en: In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. (20 words)
cn: 除了修习课程之外，学生们还要负责经营这座占地155英亩的牧场，并监督学院的日常运作。

en: Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees. (9 words)
cn: 招生委员会和课程委员会，也都由学生担任主席。

en: H) 'Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person,' says William Hunt, who graduated last year. (33 words)
cn: H) 去年毕业的威廉·亨特说：“与老师和同学们紧密地生活在一个共同体中，并被迫承担起成年人的责任，这些经历促成了一个人的成长。”

en: 'To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you're sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them.' (46 words)
cn: “想要在这样一个共同体中长久地生存下去，你就必须克服‘自己是否足够有才华或有原则’这样的疑虑，转而开始思考：你能如何激发自己和同伴的潜力，又能与他们一起学到多少东西。”

en: I) Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small—fewer than 100 students. (14 words)
cn: I) 位于佛蒙特州克拉夫茨伯里康芒的斯特林学院，规模同样非常小——学生人数不足100人。

en: Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. (28 words)
cn: 与深泉学院不同，斯特林学院的课程重点是环境和社会公正议题，但与深泉学院一样，它也高度重视个人责任感和体力劳动。

en: According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines 'rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work.' (19 words)
cn: 根据该校的招生简章，斯特林学院的大学教育融合了“严谨的学术训练、撸起袖子迎接挑战的实践，以及扎扎实实的辛勤劳作”。

en: J) The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. (38 words)
cn: J) 小型文理学院的年均学费为3万至4万美元（尚不包括校内生活费用），相比之下，公立大学仅学费一项，每年就需要8000至1万美元。

en: Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn't charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. (28 words)
cn: 在这些微型学院中，只有深泉学院不收取学费和食宿费用；学生只需支付书本费以及往返学校的交通费。

en: If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable. (24 words)
cn: 如果微型学院想要在高等教育领域占据一席之地，它们就必须找到办法，让自身真正做到收费低廉、人人可负担得起。

en: K) Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. (21 words)
cn: K) 只要不过分照搬现有的办学模式，做到这一点或许并不那么困难。

en: We've come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. (29 words)
cn: 我们已经渐渐认定，一所好大学理应开设众多学术项目、配备一流的设施、豪华的宿舍、丰富的体育项目，以及世界一流的学生活动中心。

en: Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! (8 words)
cn: 试想一所连攀岩墙都没有的好大学，简直难以想象！

en: We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. (33 words)
cn: 我们同样已经接受了这样一种观念：大学校长及其众多副校长的薪酬，理应比照商界同行的水平来支付，而高等教育也需要一套精密而先进的技术基础设施。

en: All of this drives up the cost of education. (9 words)
cn: 所有这一切，都在不断推高教育的成本。

en: L) The 'trick' to making tiny colleges affordable, if that's the right word, is simplicity. (15 words)
cn: L) 使微型学院变得可负担的“诀窍”——如果“诀窍”这个说法恰当的话——其实就是简约。

en: At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. (8 words)
cn: 教育的核心，本质上是人与人之间的互动。

en: Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. (37 words)
cn: 加菲尔德总统曾在回顾自己的大学教育经历时评论道，一所理想的大学，无非就是传奇教师马克·霍普金斯坐在一根圆木的一端，一名学生坐在另一端。

en: The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. (18 words)
cn: 换句话说，微型学院的经济模式，或许与微型住宅颇为相似。

en: Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. (18 words)
cn: 正因为规模小，微型住宅在建造、装修、投保和维护方面的花费也相对更少。

en: But the economic benefits of a small house don't end there. (11 words)
cn: 但小型住宅所带来的经济效益，并不止于此。

en: Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don't need, because there's no place to put it. (19 words)
cn: 微型住宅还能让屋主打消购买自己实际上并不需要的东西的念头，因为家里根本没有地方存放。

en: M) I'm a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. (24 words)
cn: M) 我是最近才转而认同微型学院这一理念的，我完全理解社会需要多种多样、类型各异的教育机构。

en: Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren't suited for either. (14 words)
cn: 学术研究和职业培训固然重要，但微型学院对这两者都并不适合。

en: The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. (20 words)
cn: 一个复杂社会的教育需求，本身也是复杂多样的，没有任何单一模式能够满足所有这些需求。

en: But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. (24 words)
cn: 但我如今坚信，有一种教育需求，如今几乎完全未能得到满足，那就是帮助年轻人顺利过渡到成年阶段这一需求。

en: Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution. (13 words)
cn: 而在这方面，微型学院比任何其他类型的教育机构都做得更好。

en: N) The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. (43 words)
cn: N) 微型学院存在的根本理由，源于这样一种信念：我们每个人，都是通过与了解并关心我们的人进行密切互动，才得以充分成就自身的人性；而高等教育的基本目的之一，正是促进社会性的发展。

en: Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all's said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. (31 words)
cn: 尽管我们嘴上总说大学教育会让我们成为更好的人，但归根结底，我们看待高等教育的方式，主要还是从经济角度出发的。

en: We've come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. (19 words)
cn: 我们已经渐渐把高等教育，看作是谋生的手段，而不是塑造人生的途径。

en: We've also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. (16 words)
cn: 我们也已经渐渐把高等教育，视为一种私人财富，而非公共财富。

en: Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they're an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities: the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings. (34 words)
cn: 微型学院并不能解决我们所有的教育需求，但它们确实回应了我们最基本的教育需要之一：培养出有思想、积极参与社会、且富有同情心的人。

en: If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic, you're not alone. (18 words)
cn: 如果你是那种在疫情期间变得更爱吃垃圾食品当零食的人，那你并不是唯一一个。

en: Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. (20 words)
cn: 调查记者迈克尔·莫斯指出，加工食品的设计初衷，就是要让人上瘾，这与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无二致。

en: His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. (20 words)
cn: 他在2013年出版的《盐糖脂》一书中，探讨了食品公司对这类产品的激进营销手段，以及这些产品对我们健康所造成的影响。

en: In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates. (29 words)
cn: 在他的新书《上钩》中，莫斯更新了食品巨头们为让我们持续购买其产品而做出的种种努力，以及他们如何应对来自消费者和健康倡导者的种种投诉。

en: Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. (9 words)
cn: 加工食品价格低廉、合法销售，而且随处可见。

en: Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. (15 words)
cn: 食品公司的广告不断向我们发出提示，让我们记住这些产品，从而使我们持续不断地渴望这些产品。

en: So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. (20 words)
cn: 因此，食品所处的整体环境，正是让食品对许多人而言变得更加成问题的关键因素之一。

en: Memory, nostalgia in particular plays a big role in the foods we crave. (13 words)
cn: 记忆，尤其是怀旧情绪，在我们对食物的渴望中扮演着重要角色。

en: Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. (34 words)
cn: 汽水公司发现，如果在孩子和父母一起观看球赛时，把一瓶汽水递到孩子手中，那么这瓶汽水就会永远和那一刻的欢乐情绪联系在一起。

en: Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. (18 words)
cn: 长大以后，每当这个孩子想要重温那种快乐的感觉，他就会想起汽水。

en: Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood. (11 words)
cn: 许多人都会从童年记忆中的零食里寻求慰藉。

en: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking. (17 words)
cn: 莫斯探讨了食品公司是如何利用我们的记忆、渴望以及大脑化学机制，来让我们不断吃零食的。

en: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. (26 words)
cn: 我之所以认为，其中一些食品产品，其影响力甚至比毒品更强大、更令人棘手，原因之一就在于记忆。

en: What we eat is all about memory. (7 words)
cn: 我们吃什么，归根结底都与记忆有关。

en: And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. (12 words)
cn: 而我们从很小的年纪，就已经开始形成与食物有关的记忆。

en: And we keep those memories for a lifetime. (8 words)
cn: 并且，我们会将这些记忆保留一生。

en: Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. (20 words)
cn: 深知这一点的食品行业，花费了大量时间来努力塑造我们对其产品的记忆。

en: One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. (36 words)
cn: 早在20世纪90年代，研究毒品成瘾的科学家就发现了成瘾现象的一个特征：一种物质到达大脑的速度越快，我们就越容易因此表现出冲动的行为。

en: There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. (12 words)
cn: 而在到达大脑的速度上，没有什么能比食物更快了。

en: For Moss, this puts the notion of 'fast food' in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains—almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. (32 words)
cn: 在莫斯看来，这让“快餐”这一概念呈现出一种全新的意涵，因为这一现象并不局限于快餐连锁店——杂货店里近90%的食品，都是加工食品。

en: Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging. (11 words)
cn: 从生产制造到包装，这个行业的一切，都是围绕“速度”展开的。

en: Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. (18 words)
cn: 总的来说，莫斯概述了这个行业对于把产品做得廉价、极其美味、并且对消费者来说异常便利这一点的高度依赖。

en: Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods. (42 words)
cn: 如今，越来越多的人开始关心自己摄入体内的究竟是什么、也越来越想要吃得更健康，而这些公司却发现，正是由于自身早已沉迷于制造这类方便食品，它们很难真正满足消费者这一新的需求。

en: Chimpanzees, human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. (13 words)
cn: 黑猩猩是人类在动物界最亲近的近亲，与我们共享着高达98%的基因。

en: Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. (8 words)
cn: 然而，人类与黑猩猩的生活方式，却截然不同。

en: Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. (23 words)
cn: 如今，野生黑猩猩仅存不到30万只，栖息在非洲少数几片森林角落，而人类却已经在地球的每一个角落定居繁衍。

en: At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals—despite our physical weaknesses. (17 words)
cn: 尽管人类在体能上存在种种劣势，但如今人口总数已超过70亿，远远超过了几乎所有其他哺乳动物。

en: What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes? (9 words)
cn: 究竟是什么原因，造就了人类这个物种如此惊人的进化成功？

en: One obvious answer is our big brains. (7 words)
cn: 一个显而易见的答案，是我们拥有发达的大脑。

en: It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe. (28 words)
cn: 或许正是我们与生俱来的智力，赋予了我们前所未有的跳出常规思考的能力，使人类在迁徙至全球各地的过程中，能够不断创新出应对棘手难题的解决方案。

en: But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists are rejecting that explanation. (13 words)
cn: 但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家，正在摒弃这一解释。

en: They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. (21 words)
cn: 他们认为，人类之所以能够生存和繁衍，并不是因为我们靠创新来谋生，恰恰相反，正是因为我们并不独立自主地进行思考。

en: Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others. (13 words)
cn: 相反，人们是通过仔细模仿他人，来应对充满挑战的气候和生态环境的。

en: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects—children and chimpanzees—a mechanical box with a treat inside. (24 words)
cn: 在一项著名的研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀滕，向两组实验对象——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个内藏有食物奖励的机械盒子。

en: In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. (14 words)
cn: 在其中一种实验条件下，盒子是不透明的，而在另一种条件下，盒子则是透明的。

en: The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick. (27 words)
cn: 实验人员示范了如何打开盒子取出食物，但在演示过程中，还加入了一个用棍子敲打盒子的无关步骤。

en: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. (24 words)
cn: 奇怪的是，即便孩子们能够看出用棍子敲打这一步骤并没有任何实际作用，他们依然会仔细地模仿打开盒子的每一个步骤。

en: That is, they copied irrationally: instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed. (23 words)
cn: 也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：孩子们并没有只做取得奖励所必需的动作，而是机械地模仿了自己所目睹的每一个动作。

en: Of course, that study only included three- and four-year-olds. (9 words)
cn: 当然，那项研究的实验对象，仅限于三岁和四岁的儿童。

en: But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate—that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions. (33 words)
cn: 但后续研究表明，年龄更大的儿童和成年人，反而更容易不假思索地模仿他人的行为，而婴儿则不太容易出现“过度模仿”，也就是说，他们不太会去精确复制那些哪怕并不实用的动作。

en: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. (12 words)
cn: 相比之下，实验中的黑猩猩，只有在不透明条件下才会出现“过度模仿”的现象。

en: In the transparent condition—where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless—they ignored that step entirely. (16 words)
cn: 而在透明条件下，由于它们能够看出那根棍子在机械原理上毫无用处，它们便完全忽略了这一步骤。

en: Other research has since supported these findings. (7 words)
cn: 此后的其他研究，也进一步支持了这些发现。

en: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults. (14 words)
cn: 在模仿这件事上，黑猩猩要比人类的孩子或成年人更为理性。

en: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? (11 words)
cn: 那么，人类这种看似非理性的“过度模仿”偏好，究竟从何而来呢？

en: Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. (25 words)
cn: 人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们，所依赖的技术往往极其复杂，复杂到没有人能够以纯粹理性的方式将其习得。

en: Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers. (18 words)
cn: 相反，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任更有经验的长辈和同伴所拥有的智慧。

en: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. (24 words)
cn: 所以，下次当你再听到有人慷慨激昂地主张，每个人都应该拥抱特立独行、避免模仿他人时，你或许可以会心一笑。

en: We're not chimpanzees, after all. (5 words)
cn: 毕竟，我们不是黑猩猩。

en: Our brains respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility, scientists at New York University have recently found. (23 words)
cn: 纽约大学的科学家最近发现，我们的大脑在处理表达事实的语言时，与处理传达可能性的词语时，反应方式并不相同。

en: Their work offers new insights into the impact word choice has on how we differentiate between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible. (26 words)
cn: 他们的研究，为“措辞选择如何影响我们区分‘真实陈述’与‘仅仅是可能性的陈述’”这一问题，提供了全新的洞见。

en: The researchers assert their findings are important because we are presented with false information all the time. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员强调，他们的发现之所以重要，是因为我们无时无刻不在接触各种虚假信息。

en: Some of this is deliberate, as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is aggravated by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information. (26 words)
cn: 其中一些虚假信息是故意为之的，比如具有欺骗性的广告；但更棘手的问题在于，还有一些人明明自以为在分享正确的信息，却让问题变得更加严重。

en: Thus, it is more important than ever to separate the factual from the possible or merely speculative in how we communicate. (21 words)
cn: 因此，在我们的日常交流中，把事实性内容与可能性内容，或者说仅仅是推测性的内容区分开来，比以往任何时候都更为重要。

en: This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact evokes special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of uncertainty. (35 words)
cn: 这一点尤其真实，因为该研究清楚地表明，以事实形式呈现的信息，会在我们大脑中引发一种特殊的反应——这种反应，与我们处理带有明确不确定性标志的同类内容时的反应，是截然不同的。

en: In their new study, the scientists intended to ascertain how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as 'may,' 'might,' and 'if.' (24 words)
cn: 在这项新研究中，科学家们的意图，是要弄清楚大脑究竟是如何计算由诸如“可能”“也许”“如果”这类词语所表达的各种可能性的。

en: The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual scenarios and those expressing possibility. (14 words)
cn: 研究人员比较了大脑对表达事实性情境的陈述、以及表达可能性的陈述所做出的反应。

en: 'There is a monster under my bed' exemplifies a factual statement. (11 words)
cn: “我床底下有一个怪物”，就是一句典型的事实性陈述。

en: 'I will stay home,' is also factual. (7 words)
cn: “我会待在家里”，同样也是一句事实性陈述。

en: This is opposed to statements that express possibility, like 'There might be a monster under my bed,' or 'If it rains, I will stay home.' (25 words)
cn: 与此相对的，则是表达可能性的陈述，比如“我床底下可能有一个怪物”，或者“如果下雨，我就待在家里”。

en: The results of the study showed that factual language activated a rapid increase in brain activity, with the brain responding more powerfully and showing more engagement with factual phrases compared to those communicating possibility. (34 words)
cn: 研究结果显示，事实性语言会在大脑中激发出更为迅速的活动增长——面对事实性语句，大脑的反应更为强烈，参与程度也明显高于面对表达可能性的语句时的反应。

en: Thus, facts rule when it comes to the brain. (9 words)
cn: 由此可见，就大脑而言，事实占据着主导地位。

en: Brain regions involved in processing discourse rapidly distinguish facts from possibilities. (11 words)
cn: 参与语篇处理的大脑区域，能够迅速地将事实与可能性区分开来。

en: Further, these regions respond in a much more robust fashion to factual statements. (13 words)
cn: 此外，这些脑区在应对事实性陈述时，所表现出的反应也要强劲得多。

en: A) On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. (24 words)
cn: A) 在肯尼亚中部的山丘上，阳光下闪烁着点点绿意的茶树丛，让整片山坡几乎呈现出柠檬绿的色泽，而当地的农民，对气候变化早已深有体会。

en: 'The rainy season is no longer predictable,' says one. (9 words)
cn: “雨季已经变得不再可预测了，”一位农民说道。

en: 'When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once.' (14 words)
cn: “该下雨的时候不下，然后又会一股脑儿全下下来。”

en: Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. (12 words)
cn: 气候变化，是一个将影响地球上每一个人的议题。

en: For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. (34 words)
cn: 但对非洲人来说，其后果将尤为惨痛：其他地区曾靠燃烧煤炭和石油走向富裕，而非洲却要在没能享受到这些发展红利的情况下，承担起气候变化所带来的大部分人道代价。

en: 'Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts,' says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds. (35 words)
cn: “非洲的温室气体排放量仅占全球总量的2%，但它却是预计将受气候影响最为严重的大陆，”负责管理世界银行80亿美元气候投资基金的马法尔达·杜阿尔特说道。

en: B) Although there are huge uncertainties to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. (30 words)
cn: B) 尽管气候变化究竟会带来怎样的具体影响，目前仍存在巨大的不确定性，但现有的了解已经足以说明，全球变暖正是威胁非洲繁荣发展的主要因素之一。

en: Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. (30 words)
cn: 非洲部分地区的升温速度，已经远远快于全球平均水平：过去50年间，南部非洲的气温上升速度，大约是全球平均升温速度的两倍。

en: Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5°C, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. (29 words)
cn: 即便全世界能够成功削减排放、将全球升温控制在1.5摄氏度以内，非洲的热浪也将进一步加剧，疾病也会蔓延到目前尚未受到影响的地区。

en: Farming would also be hit hard. (6 words)
cn: 农业同样也将遭受重创。

en: About 40% of the land now used to grow maize (玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. (18 words)
cn: 目前用于种植玉米的土地中，约有40%将不再适宜种植玉米。

en: Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18%-22%. (11 words)
cn: 总体而言，据估计，玉米产量将因此下降18%至22%。

en: C) Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. (42 words)
cn: C) 非洲之所以显得尤为脆弱，部分原因在于，即便完全不考虑气候变化，它本身就已经难以养活自己——若要让快速增长的人口都能吃饱饭，非洲就必须大幅提高农作物产量和生产效率。

en: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. (38 words)
cn: 联合国粮食及农业组织估计，到2050年，为了满足人口数量与食欲同步增长所带来的需求，全球粮食产量必须在2009年的水平基础上，再提高约70%。

en: Much of this new demand will be in Africa. (9 words)
cn: 而这其中，很大一部分新增需求，都将来自非洲。

en: Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. (25 words)
cn: 然而，非洲大陆目前每年已经要进口约500亿美元的粮食，而这一数字预计在未来五年内还将翻上一倍以上。

en: Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement. (27 words)
cn: 粮食自给自足并非非洲的既定目标，但非洲花在进口粮食上的钱，居然比花在购买资本品上的钱还多，这一事实本身，就说明它在这方面依然大有改进的空间。

en: D) Finding out why is not hard. (7 words)
cn: D) 要弄清楚其中的原因，其实并不难。

en: Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. (11 words)
cn: 非洲大多数农场规模极小，靠人工耕作，还得完全依赖雨水灌溉。

en: More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. (11 words)
cn: 非洲有超过一半的人口，都是靠务农为生的。

en: Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. (22 words)
cn: 尽管过去几十年间，非洲的粮食总产量有所攀升，但这主要是因为耕种人口增多、耕种面积扩大了而已。

en: But in many places there is no spare land to farm. (11 words)
cn: 但在许多地方，早已没有多余的土地可供开垦耕种。

en: Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. (18 words)
cn: 卢旺达的农田规模之小，甚至可以把250块这样的地块，塞进一座普通美国农场的面积里。

en: And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. (29 words)
cn: 而且，尽管过去30年间，非洲的人均产出已经提高了超过一半，但这一增幅，依然远远落后于亚洲2.5倍的增长水平。

en: Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America. (17 words)
cn: 非洲的玉米产量通常低于每公顷两吨，仅相当于美国水平的五分之一。

en: E) The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. (23 words)
cn: E) 非洲农民生产效率低下的问题，也体现在了国家经济统计数据之中——尽管农业吸纳了大量劳动力，但它对GDP的贡献却仅占15%。

en: 'They can't even feed their families,' says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. (20 words)
cn: “他们甚至连自己的家人都养不活，”负责农业事务的非洲开发银行副行长珍妮弗·布兰克说道。

en: 'Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years.' (12 words)
cn: “在非洲许多地区，农业生产效率已经整整一百年都没有得到过改善了。”

en: F) One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. (24 words)
cn: F) 原因之一在于，在独立后的最初几十年里，许多非洲国家的政府一心专注于推动经济工业化，而忽视了农业发展。

en: Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. (25 words)
cn: 另一些国家，则通过压低国营垄断机构收购农作物的价格，来补贴城市工人的廉价食品，从而对农业造成了损害。

en: Ghana taxed cocoa (可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. (26 words)
cn: 加纳对可可粉出口征收的重税之高，导致其可可产量在20世纪60年代到80年代间腰斩了一半，尽管当时可可的全球价格正在飙升。

en: Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. (35 words)
cn: 然而，过去大约二十年间，各国政府和捐助方，已经开始重新把目光投向农业，将其视为解决每年新增1300万青年劳动力就业问题的一条出路。

en: Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. (18 words)
cn: 其中，大部分的关注重点，都放在了帮助小农户使用化肥、以及更为重要的——使用更优质种子上。

en: The results can be impressive. (5 words)
cn: 由此取得的成效，可以说相当可观。

en: Improved varieties of sorghum (高粱), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. (19 words)
cn: 举例来说，改良品种的高粱，其产量可以比普通品种高出40%。

en: Infrastructure is important. (3 words)
cn: 基础设施建设，同样至关重要。

en: A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes. (22 words)
cn: 世界银行在埃塞俄比亚开展的一项灌溉项目，帮助当地农民将马铃薯的收成，从每公顷约8吨，提高到了35吨。

en: G) Better techniques help, too. (5 words)
cn: G) 改进的种植技术，同样也大有助益。

en: Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. (33 words)
cn: 肯尼亚的小规模咖啡种植户，只需遵循几条简单的护理咖啡树的准则——比如只保留三根主枝、修剪掉其余枝条——便能将自己的收入提高40%。

en: Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. (13 words)
cn: 他们的许多邻居，却并不愿采纳这一建议，因为这在直觉上似乎说不通。

en: More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. (11 words)
cn: 他们认为，枝条越多，理应能结出越多的咖啡豆才对。

en: Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same. (21 words)
cn: 但在看到采纳了这一建议的农户，接连一两季都获得了更丰厚的收成之后，越来越多的人，也开始纷纷效仿。

en: H) One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. (16 words)
cn: H) 传播知识经验的一种方式，是把农场与其收成的大买家联系起来。

en: When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. (30 words)
cn: 英国饮料巨头帝亚吉欧在肯尼亚西部兴建了一座啤酒厂，希望利用当地作物，酿造出一款价格足够低廉、能与非法自酿酒竞争的啤酒。

en: It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. (22 words)
cn: 该公司把农户组织成小组，为他们改善了获取种子和化肥的供应链，并承诺收购他们的谷物。

en: It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. (9 words)
cn: 如今，它已经为约1.7万名农户提供了稳定的销路。

en: Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business. (26 words)
cn: 负责该公司非洲业务的约翰·奥基夫表示，在整个地区，公司使用本地原材料的比例，在五年间已经翻了一番，达到了约80%。

en: I) An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farms. (25 words)
cn: I) 一个更为重要的转变，是从传统农耕方式，转向能够以盈利方式为小农户带来技术和投资的商业模式。

en: Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. (19 words)
cn: 年轻的肯尼亚人泰塔·恩格蒂奇，在攻读工程学专业期间，曾想通过副业赚一点外快。

en: He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. (11 words)
cn: 他东拼西凑地攒了2万肯尼亚先令（约合200美元），用来种植西红柿。

en: Everything went wrong. (3 words)
cn: 结果一切都出了岔子。

en: The crop was attacked by pests. (6 words)
cn: 他种的作物遭到了虫害的侵袭。

en: 'Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital,' he says. (13 words)
cn: “后来又发生了一场大洪水，把我们所有的本钱都冲走了，”他说道。

en: Mr. Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. (17 words)
cn: 恩格蒂奇没有放弃，转而考虑购置一座温室大棚，来保护自己的作物免受虫害和风雨的侵袭。

en: The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. (17 words)
cn: 市面上最便宜的温室大棚，一座也要2500多美元，于是他索性自己设计了一款，成本只有市价的一半。
