en: Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. (27 words)
cn: 很快，周边的农户也开始向他下订单，如今，他的公司“Illuminum温室”，已经卖出了超过1400座温室大棚，为大约6000人提供了生计。

en: The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields. (18 words)
cn: 这项业务并未止步于此，他如今还提供化肥、优质种苗，以及能够提高产量的智能传感器。

en: J) Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. (14 words)
cn: J) Illuminum公司的成功案例说明了，技术如何能够帮助即便是小规模农场，也能提高生产效率。

en: Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. (26 words)
cn: 由于非洲人口中有如此之大的比例，是靠农业为生的，哪怕是生产效率上的微小提升，也能让数百万人的收入随之增加。

en: But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure. (22 words)
cn: 但从长远来看，小规模农业的发展终究有其局限，尤其是在气候变化和人口压力的双重夹击之下。

en: K) 'If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education,' says Mr. Ngetich. (41 words)
cn: K) “如果我们真的想要帮助人们摆脱贫困，就必须投资那些能让他们月收入至少达到100美元的项目，这样他们才能负担得起医疗和教育的开支，”恩格蒂奇说道。

en: 'Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there.' (20 words)
cn: “那些只能靠种豆子或玉米、每月多挣2美元的项目，是无法真正帮他们实现这一目标的。”

en: Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities. (12 words)
cn: 要实现这种大幅度的收入跃升，还需要依靠工厂和城市中更优质的就业机会。

en: One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts. (25 words)
cn: 近几十年来，共和党取得的一项重大成功，便是不遗余力地推广了一套简单的经济增长公式：减税。

en: The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. (11 words)
cn: 这套公式其实并不奏效，但这丝毫没有影响它的受欢迎程度。

en: And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals. (16 words)
cn: 尽管“减税崇拜”招致了不少批评者，但它却始终没有遇到真正有力的对手主张。

en: Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. (14 words)
cn: 民主党的政治人物，往往倾向于以“帮助那些被经济增长甩在身后的人”作为竞选主张。

en: When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans. (13 words)
cn: 而当民主党人真的谈起如何促进经济增长时，他们的论调，却常常听起来跟共和党人如出一辙。

en: This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. (18 words)
cn: 这不仅仅是民主党所面临的一个政治问题；对整个美国而言，这也是一个经济问题。

en: The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. (12 words)
cn: 这个国家，需要一套更有说服力的、关于经济增长驱动力的叙事。

en: The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages. (13 words)
cn: 近几十年来所经历的种种惨痛教训，都指向了一个颇具前景的答案：提高工资。

en: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. (14 words)
cn: 提高美国劳动者的工资，理应成为经济决策者的首要任务。

en: We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks. (30 words)
cn: 与其把注意力过多地放在每季度更新的国内生产总值（GDP）增长数据上，我们不如把关注的重点，转向劳动者薪资的增长——这样一来，大家的处境都会更好。

en: Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. (12 words)
cn: 暂且把那个人们耳熟能详的、支持提高工资的理由——公平——放到一边不谈。

en: The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth. (14 words)
cn: 这里想说的论点是，提高工资本身，就能为经济增长这台引擎提供动力。

en: Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. (30 words)
cn: 或许，最能说明这一好处的经典案例，就是亨利·福特在1914年做出的决定——把福特T型车装配线工人的日薪，提高到5美元。

en: He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. (15 words)
cn: 他这样做，是为了提高生产效率——他愿意付出高于市场行情的薪资，来维系一支稳定可靠的员工队伍。

en: The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. (12 words)
cn: 而由此带来的一个意外收获是，福特工厂的工人，也逐渐变成了福特汽车的顾客。

en: The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. (19 words)
cn: 同样的逻辑，至今依然成立：消费，驱动着美国经济的运转，而拿到更高薪水的劳动者，也能够消费得更多。

en: Mainstream economists insisted that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. (25 words)
cn: 主流经济学家一直坚持认为，人为地要求实现可持续的工资增长是不可能的，因为薪酬水平所反映的，是市场力量那种“从不出错”的判断。

en: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. (14 words)
cn: 传统观点一直认为，提高生产效率，是通往更高工资的唯一途径。

en: Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. (10 words)
cn: 按照这一逻辑，任何通过谈判争取更高工资的努力，都只会适得其反。

en: Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none. (26 words)
cn: 最低工资法只会推高失业率，因为整个工资总池的资金终归是有限的，如果有些人拿得更多，另一些人就注定拿不到任何份额。

en: It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. (20 words)
cn: 正是在这种世界观的背景下，“减税能够带来繁荣”这一论调，才开始逐渐流行开来。

en: Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise. (10 words)
cn: 其逻辑是：富人会用减税所得进行投资，生产效率随之提升，工资也就会随之上涨。

en: In the real world, things are more complicated. (8 words)
cn: 但在现实世界中，事情要复杂得多。

en: Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. (17 words)
cn: 工资水平，其实受到雇主与劳动者之间一场“拉锯战”的影响，而在这场拉锯战中，一直是雇主占据上风。

en: One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. (18 words)
cn: 一个明显的证据是，自1970年前后以来，生产效率的增长与工资增长之间的差距，一直在不断拉大。

en: Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. (10 words)
cn: 生产效率已经翻了不止一倍；而工资的增长，却远远落在了后面。

en: A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote (矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts. (24 words)
cn: 把关注的重点，转向工资增长，将为那种迷信减税具有“魔力”、看似简单诱人的观念，提供一剂矫正良方。

en: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. (23 words)
cn: 期刊编辑决定着什么样的研究能够得以发表、什么样的研究不能，这直接影响着其他学者的职业发展，也影响着整个学科领域未来的走向。

en: You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. (24 words)
cn: 因此，人们理应期待，各类学术期刊会竭尽所能，建立起一支多元化的编辑团队，从而反映出多样化的声音、经历和身份背景。

en: Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. (11 words)
cn: 然而遗憾的是，《自然·神经科学》上刊登的一项最新研究，读来却令人心情沉重。

en: The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. (43 words)
cn: 研究团队发现，顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的编辑，绝大多数都是男性，且大多身处美国——这种局面，可能正在进一步放大该领域业已存在的性别不平等，同时也影响着哪些研究成果能够得以发表。

en: Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. (13 words)
cn: 研究发现，男性占心理学期刊编辑总数的60%。

en: There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. (28 words)
cn: 在每一个资历层级上，男性编辑的数量都明显多于女性编辑，而在超过四分之三的期刊中，男性编辑都占据了多数席位。

en: Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. (17 words)
cn: 更为关键的是，女性编辑所占的比例，明显低于心理学领域女性研究人员的整体占比。

en: The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. (26 words)
cn: 在神经科学类期刊中，这种差距更为悬殊：70%的编辑为男性，在88%的期刊中，男性都占据了编辑职位的多数。

en: In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly. (32 words)
cn: 而在这种情况下，女性编辑所占的比例，与从事神经科学研究的女性学者占比相比，并没有明显偏低——这一发现，恰恰揭示出该领域更为普遍、持久存在的性别失衡问题。

en: Based on their results, the team concludes that 'the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience.' (32 words)
cn: 基于这些研究结果，研究团队总结道：“在心理学和神经科学领域最具影响力的学术期刊中，男性的观念、价值取向以及决策偏好，在编辑职位中占据着过高的比重。”

en: Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. (44 words)
cn: 科学界的性别不平等，常常被归因于资深学者中男性居多这一事实——由于科学界历史上一直由男性主导，人们据此认为，随着时间推移、更多女性晋升至资深职位，这一领域自然会变得更加平等。

en: Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty. (33 words)
cn: 然而，这项研究却显示，即便是在心理学期刊的初级编辑职位上，男性也同样占据着不成比例的多数——尽管实际上，心理学领域的初级教职人员中，女性人数其实是多于男性的。

en: This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. (12 words)
cn: 这意味着，女性学者数量不足，并不是问题的根源所在。

en: Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. (11 words)
cn: 恰恰相反，女性在科学界处于不利地位，其背后存在着结构性的原因。

en: Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. (31 words)
cn: 举例来说，女性的薪资水平往往更低，还要承担更多的育儿责任，这可能导致她们发表的论文数量更少、获得的科研经费也更少——而这些，恰恰正是期刊在决定任命人选时所看重的条件。

en: Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. (20 words)
cn: 与其简单地把编辑团队中的性别不平等归咎于传统惯例，我们更应当积极主动地去打破这些现存的障碍。

en: A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. (14 words)
cn: 期刊编辑队伍缺乏多样性，很可能也是导致心理学界“WEIRD”问题（即研究样本过度集中于西方、受过教育、工业化、富裕且民主社会人群）的原因之一。

en: If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not. (30 words)
cn: 如果期刊编辑大多是来自美国的男性，那么无论是否出于自觉，他们很可能都会更加看重那些与西方、男性群体相关的研究论文。

en: The desert is deceiving. (4 words)
cn: 沙漠总是充满迷惑性。

en: At first glance it looks lifeless, barren, and bone-dry. (9 words)
cn: 乍看之下，它显得毫无生机、荒芜贫瘠，干燥得如同枯骨一般。

en: For most passersby humming through the Mojave on their way to try their luck in Las Vegas or heading towards the Grand Canyon, it's just a flat stretch of land with some mountains in the distance and more apt to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars. (51 words)
cn: 对于大多数只是路过、正驱车穿越莫哈韦沙漠、前往拉斯维加斯碰运气或是驶向大峡谷的人来说，它不过是一片平坦的荒地，远处点缀着几座山峦，看起来更像是某部火星题材电影的取景地。

en: The desert, however, is overflowing with life, mystery, and magic. (10 words)
cn: 然而，这片沙漠，实则处处洋溢着生命、神秘与魔力。

en: The Mojave desert sees less than two inches of rain a year, and like most deserts, is a land of extremes. (21 words)
cn: 莫哈韦沙漠年降水量不足两英寸，和大多数沙漠一样，是一片充满极端反差的土地。

en: Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to burning hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day. (18 words)
cn: 这里的气温波动幅度极大，从冰点直到酷热难耐，不仅体现在季节之间的变化上，甚至同一天之内也会经历这样的剧烈起伏。

en: At the heart of this vast, 25,000-square-mile desert is Mojave National Preserve. (12 words)
cn: 在这片方圆2.5万平方英里的广袤沙漠腹地，坐落着莫哈韦国家保护区。

en: The folks managing and working there wear the wide-brimmed (宽檐的) hats that have become synonymous with places like Yosemite. (19 words)
cn: 在这里管理和工作的人们，头戴着那种如今几乎已成为约塞米蒂等地代名词的宽檐帽。

en: The preserve is rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities to stimulate your interest, especially for anyone who loves the outdoors. (22 words)
cn: 这片保护区历史底蕴深厚、文化多元、生物多样性丰富，对任何一个热爱户外活动的人来说，都蕴藏着无穷无尽、能够激发兴趣的机会。

en: For a photographer, it requires patience and probably a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved 'roads', but the rewards are plenty. (24 words)
cn: 对摄影师而言，要在这片错综复杂的未铺装“道路”网络中辗转穿行，需要极大的耐心，也很可能还需要备上几个备用轮胎，但所获得的回报，绝对物有所值。

en: Photographing here requires a good, sturdy pair of shoes and a lot of preparation. (14 words)
cn: 在这里拍摄，需要一双结实耐穿的鞋子，以及充分的准备。

en: Plenty of water, spare tires, and a full tank of gas are needed to explore this unit of the national park system, which is the third largest in the country. (30 words)
cn: 要探索这片国家公园体系中面积第三大的区域，充足的饮用水、备用轮胎和加满的油箱，都必不可少。

en: Like all deserts, though if you are patient, you will be rewarded, as they often reveal their secrets slowly. (19 words)
cn: 和所有沙漠一样，只要你有足够的耐心，就终将获得回报，因为沙漠往往是缓缓地、逐渐地才向人展露它的秘密。

en: During my last outing, I was surprised to see how much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces, much of which remains today, giving the area a unique feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs. (41 words)
cn: 在我最近一次出行中，我惊讶地发现，这片区域在很大程度上是由古老的火山活动和地质力量塑造而成的，而这些痕迹至今大多依然清晰可辨，赋予了这片土地一种独特的气质，也为绝佳的摄影作品，勾勒出了一幅色彩斑斓的背景画卷。

en: A) Most visitors come to Cape Canaveral, on the northeast coast of Florida, for the tourist attractions. (17 words)
cn: A) 大多数游客前往佛罗里达州东北海岸的卡纳维拉尔角，都是为了那里的旅游景点。

en: It's home to the second-busiest cruise ship port in the world and is a gateway to the cosmos. (18 words)
cn: 这里坐拥全球第二繁忙的邮轮港口，也是通往浩瀚宇宙的门户。

en: Nearly 1.5 million visitors flock here every year to watch rockets, spacecraft, and satellites blast off into the solar system from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex. (26 words)
cn: 每年都有近150万游客蜂拥而至，只为亲眼见证火箭、航天器和卫星，从肯尼迪航天中心游客综合体升空、驶向太阳系深处。

en: Nearly 64 kilometers of undeveloped beach and 648 square kilometers of protected refuge fan out from the cape's sandy shores. (20 words)
cn: 从这座海角的沙质海岸线向外延伸，是近64公里未经开发的海滩，以及648平方公里的自然保护区。

en: B) Yet some of Cape Canaveral's most legendary attractions lie unseen, wedged under the sea's surface in mud and sand, for this part of the world has a reputation as a deadly ship trap. (34 words)
cn: B) 然而，卡纳维拉尔角一些最富传奇色彩的景观，却深藏不露，静静地嵌在海面之下的泥沙之中——因为世界上这片区域，素有“致命沉船陷阱”的恶名。

en: Over the centuries, dozens of majestic Old World sailing ships smashed and sank on this irregular stretch of windy Florida coast. (21 words)
cn: 几个世纪以来，数十艘来自旧大陆的宏伟帆船，在这片风大浪急、地形不规则的佛罗里达海岸线上，触礁沉没。

en: They were vessels built for war and commerce, crossing the globe carrying everything from coins to cannons, boxes of silver and gold, chests of jewels and porcelain, and pearls from the Caribbean. (32 words)
cn: 这些船只，原本是为战争与商贸而建造的，它们曾满载从硬币到大炮、从成箱的金银到成箱的珠宝瓷器、乃至来自加勒比海的珍珠，穿越全球各地。

en: C) Cape Canaveral contains one of the greatest concentrations of colonial shipwrecks in the world. (15 words)
cn: C) 卡纳维拉尔角，是全世界殖民时期沉船分布最为密集的区域之一。

en: In recent years, advances in radar, diving, detection equipment, computers, and GPS have transformed the hunt. (16 words)
cn: 近年来，雷达、潜水技术、探测设备、计算机以及GPS定位技术的进步，彻底改变了这场“寻宝之旅”。

en: The naked eye might see a pile of rocks, but technology can reveal the precious artifacts (人工制品) that lie hidden on the ocean floor. (24 words)
cn: 肉眼看去，那或许只是一堆乱石，但借助科技，人们却能揭示出隐藏在海底深处的珍贵人工制品。

en: D) As technology renders the seabed more accessible, the hunt for treasure-filled ships has drawn a fresh tide of salvors (打捞者) and their investors—as well as marine archaeologists (海洋考古学家) wanting to bring to light the lost relics. (37 words)
cn: D) 随着科技让海床变得愈发触手可及，寻找满载财宝的沉船，也吸引了新一波打捞者及其投资人的加入——与此同时，也吸引了渴望重现这些失落遗物的海洋考古学家。

en: But of late, when salvors have found vessels, their rights have been challenged in court. (15 words)
cn: 但近来，每当打捞者发现沉船，他们对这些发现的权利，却往往会在法庭上遭到挑战。

en: The big question: who should have control of these treasures? (10 words)
cn: 一个关键的问题由此浮现：这些财宝，究竟应当由谁掌控？

en: E) High-stakes fights over shipwrecks pit archaeologists against treasure hunters in a vicious cycle of accusations. (16 words)
cn: E) 围绕沉船展开的、赌注极高的争斗，让考古学家与寻宝者陷入了一轮又一轮相互指责的恶性循环之中。

en: Archaeologists regard themselves as protectors of history, and they see salvors as careless destroyers. (14 words)
cn: 考古学家把自己视为历史的守护者，并将打捞者视为鲁莽的破坏者。

en: Salvors feel they do the hard work of searching for ships, only to have them stolen from under them when discovered. (21 words)
cn: 而打捞者则觉得，明明是自己历经千辛万苦找到了这些沉船，最后却眼睁睁看着成果被人从手中夺走。

en: This kind of clash inevitably takes place on a grand scale. (11 words)
cn: 这种冲突，往往不可避免地会演变成大规模的对抗。

en: Aside from the salvors, their investors, and the maritime archaeologists who serve as expert witnesses, the battles sweep in local and international governments and organizations like UNESCO that work to protect under-water heritage. (33 words)
cn: 卷入这场纷争的，除了打捞者、他们的投资人，以及担任专家证人的海洋考古学家之外，还有地方及国际政府机构，以及像联合国教科文组织这样致力于保护水下遗产的组织。

en: The court cases that ensue stretch on for years. (9 words)
cn: 由此引发的诉讼官司，往往一打就是数年之久。

en: Are finders keepers, or do the ships belong to the countries that made them and sent them sailing centuries ago? (20 words)
cn: 究竟应当遵循“先到先得”的原则，还是这些船只理应归属于几个世纪前建造并派遣它们出海的国家？

en: Where once salvors and archaeologists worked side by side, now they belong to opposing, and equally contemptuous, tribes. (18 words)
cn: 曾几何时，打捞者与考古学家还能并肩合作，如今却已分裂成彼此对立、且同样相互鄙视的两大阵营。

en: F) Nearly three million vessels lie wrecked on the Earth's ocean floor—from old canoes to the Titanic—and likely less than one percent have been explored. (25 words)
cn: F) 地球的海底，静静躺着近三百万艘沉船——从古老的独木舟到泰坦尼克号，无所不有——而其中，很可能还不到百分之一曾被探索发现。

en: Some—like an ancient Roman ship found off Antikythera, Greece, dated between 70 and 60 BC and carrying astonishingly sophisticated gears and dials for navigating by the sun—are critical to a new understanding of our past. (35 words)
cn: 其中一些沉船——比如在希腊安提基特拉岛附近发现的一艘古罗马沉船，年代可追溯至公元前70年至前60年之间，船上还载有一套复杂精密到令人惊叹的、用于依靠太阳导航的齿轮和刻度装置——对我们重新认识过去，具有至关重要的意义。

en: No wonder there is an eternal stirring among everybody from salvors to scholars to find them. (16 words)
cn: 难怪从打捞者到学者，人人都对寻找这些沉船抱有一种永不熄灭的热情。

en: G) In May 2016, a salvor named Bobby Pritchett, president of Global Marine Exploration (GME) in Tampa, Florida, announced that he had discovered scattered remains of a ship buried a kilometer off Cape Canaveral. (34 words)
cn: G) 2016年5月，一位名叫博比·普里切特的打捞者——他同时也是佛罗里达州坦帕市“全球海洋勘探公司”（GME）的总裁——宣布，他在卡纳维拉尔角外海一公里处，发现了一艘沉船散落的遗骸。

en: Over the prior three years, he and his crew had obtained 14 state permits to survey a nearly 260-square-kilometer area off the cape; they worked 250 days a year, backed by investor funds of, he claims, US $4 million. (39 words)
cn: 在此前的三年里，他和他的团队已获得了14份州政府颁发的许可证，用以勘测这片沿海约260平方公里的区域；他们据称在投资人提供的400万美元资金支持下，每年工作达250天之久。

en: It was hard work. (4 words)
cn: 这是一份异常艰辛的工作。

en: Crew members were up at dawn, dragging sensors from their expedition vessels back and forth, day in and day out, year after year, to detect metal of any kind. (29 words)
cn: 团队成员天不亮就要起床，日复一日、年复一年地拖着传感器，在勘探船上来回往返，只为探测任何一丝金属信号。

en: Using computer technology, Pritchett and his crew created intricate, color-coded maps marked with the GPS coordinates of thousands of finds, all invisible under a meter of sand. (27 words)
cn: 借助计算机技术，普里切特和他的团队绘制出了错综复杂、以颜色区分标注的地图，上面标记着数千处发现地点的GPS坐标——而这些发现，全都埋藏在一米厚的沙层之下，肉眼根本无法察觉。

en: H) One day in 2015, the magnetometer (磁力计) picked up metal that turned out to be an iron cannon; when the divers blew the sand away, they also discovered a more precious bronze cannon with markings indicating French royalty and, not far off, a famous marble column carved with the coat of arms of France, known from historical paintings. (59 words)
cn: H) 2015年的某一天，磁力计探测到了一块金属信号，结果发现是一门铁制大炮；当潜水员将周围的沙子吹开后，他们又发现了一门更为珍贵的青铜大炮，炮身上刻有代表法国王室的标记，而在不远处，还发现了一根著名的大理石柱，上面雕刻着法国的国徽——这一图案，此前只在历史画作中出现过。

en: The discovery was cause for celebration. (6 words)
cn: 这一发现，值得大肆庆祝一番。

en: The artifacts indicated the divers had likely found the wreck of La Trinity, a 16th-century French vessel that had been at the center of a bloody battle between France and Spain that changed the fate of the United States of America. (41 words)
cn: 这些文物表明，潜水员很可能找到了“三位一体号”的残骸——这是一艘16世纪的法国船只，曾是法国与西班牙之间一场惨烈战役的核心焦点，而那场战役，也彻底改写了美利坚合众国的命运。

en: I) And then the legal storm began, with GME and Pritchett pitted against Florida and France. (16 words)
cn: I) 紧接着，一场法律风暴便随之而来——GME公司和普里切特，被推上了与佛罗里达州及法国对簿公堂的境地。

en: The Sunken Military Craft Act of 2004, a US federal act, protects any vessel that was on a military mission, allowing the originating country to claim their ship even centuries later. (31 words)
cn: 根据美国2004年颁布的《沉没军用船只法》这一联邦法案，任何执行军事任务的沉船，都受到法律保护，即便时隔数百年，其所属国家仍有权主张对该船只的所有权。

en: In 2018, two long years after Pritchett's discovery, the federal district court ruled in favor of France. (17 words)
cn: 2018年，也就是普里切特发现沉船整整两年之后，联邦地区法院最终裁定，法国胜诉。

en: For Pritchett, the decision was devastating. (6 words)
cn: 对普里切特而言，这一裁决无疑是毁灭性的打击。

en: Millions of dollars of investor funding and years of labor were lost. (12 words)
cn: 数百万美元的投资资金，以及多年的辛勤付出，就此付诸东流。

en: J) But this is far from the first time a salvor has lost all rights to a discovery. (18 words)
cn: J) 但这远非打捞者第一次因某项发现，而彻底丧失所有权利。

en: In 2012, for instance, Spain won a five-year legal battle against Odyssey Marine Exploration, which had hauled 594,000 gold and silver coins from a Spanish wreck off the coast of Portugal across the Atlantic to the United States. (38 words)
cn: 举例来说，2012年，西班牙就在一场历时五年的法律诉讼中，击败了“奥德赛海洋勘探公司”——该公司曾从葡萄牙沿海一艘西班牙沉船中，打捞出59.4万枚金银币，并将其横跨大西洋运往了美国。

en: 'Treasure hunters can be naive,' says attorney David Concannon, who has had several maritime archaeologists as clients and represented two sides in the battles over the Titanic for 20 years. (30 words)
cn: “寻宝者有时未免过于天真，”律师大卫·康坎农说道。他曾代理过多名海洋考古学家客户，并在围绕泰坦尼克号展开的诉讼中，代表过双方阵营，前后长达20年之久。

en: 'Many treasure hunters don't understand they are going to have to fight for their rights against a government that has an endless supply of money for legal battles that treasure hunters are likely to lose.' (35 words)
cn: “许多寻宝者根本没有意识到，自己将不得不与一个在法律诉讼上拥有近乎无穷资金实力的政府对抗，来争取自己的权利——而这样的官司，寻宝者往往注定会输。”

en: K) Putting an inflated price on artifacts rather than viewing them as cultural and historical treasures that transcend any price is what irritates many archaeologists. (25 words)
cn: K) 让许多考古学家感到愤慨的是，人们总是给文物标上虚高的价格，而不是把它们当作超越任何金钱价值的文化历史瑰宝来看待。

en: For the archaeologist, everything in a wreck matters—hair, fabric, a fragment of a newspaper, rat bones—all things speak volumes. (19 words)
cn: 在考古学家眼中，一艘沉船中的每一样东西都至关重要——无论是一缕毛发、一片布料、一张报纸的碎片，还是几根老鼠的骨头——这些细节，都蕴含着丰富的信息。

en: Archaeologists don't want artifacts ending up in a private collection instead of taking humanity on a journey of understanding. (19 words)
cn: 考古学家不希望这些文物最终流入私人收藏，而是希望它们能够带领全人类，踏上一段理解历史的旅程。

en: L) George Bass is one of the pioneers of under-water archaeology, and a researcher at Texas A&M University. (18 words)
cn: L) 乔治·巴斯，是水下考古学领域的先驱人物之一，如今在得克萨斯农工大学从事研究工作。

en: He has testified in court against treasure hunters, but says archaeology is not without its own serious problems. (18 words)
cn: 他曾在法庭上作证、指证寻宝者，但他也坦言，考古学本身同样存在着一些严重的问题。

en: He believes archaeologists need to do a better job themselves instead of routinely criticizing treasure hunters. (16 words)
cn: 他认为，考古学家们应当反思并改进自身的工作，而不是一味地惯性批评寻宝者。

en: 'Archaeology has a terrible reputation for not publishing enough on its excavations (发掘) and finds,' he says. (17 words)
cn: “考古学界有一个相当糟糕的名声，那就是对自己的发掘工作和发现成果，发表得实在太少，”他说道。

en: Gathering data, unearthing and meticulously preserving and examining finds, verifying identity and origin, piecing together the larger story, and writing and publishing a comprehensive paper or book can take decades. (30 words)
cn: 从收集数据、发掘出土，到细致地保存和研究这些发现，再到确认文物的身份和来源、拼凑出完整的历史脉络，最终撰写并发表一篇全面的论文或专著，这整个过程，可能要耗费数十年的光阴。

en: A bit cynically, Bass describes colleagues who never published because they waited so long they became ill or died. (19 words)
cn: 巴斯还略带讽刺地描述了一些同行的境况——他们迟迟没有发表研究成果，一直拖到自己生病或去世，也始终未能完成。

en: Who is more at fault, Bass asks, the professional archaeologist who carefully excavates a site and never publishes on it or the treasure hunter who locates a submerged wreck, salvages part, conserves part, and publishes a book on the operation? (40 words)
cn: 巴斯不禁发问：究竟谁的过错更大——是那位小心翼翼地发掘了一处遗址、却始终未能发表任何成果的专业考古学家，还是那位找到了一艘沉船、打捞出部分文物、精心保存了部分文物、并就整个行动出版了一本书的寻宝者？

en: M) Pritchett concedes that his find deserves careful excavation and preservation. (11 words)
cn: M) 普里切特也承认，自己的这项发现，理应得到细致的发掘和妥善的保存。

en: 'I think what I found should go in a museum,' he says. (12 words)
cn: “我认为，我所发现的这些东西，应该被送进博物馆，”他说道。

en: 'But I also think I should get paid for what I found.' (12 words)
cn: “但我同时也认为，我应该为自己的这一发现，获得相应的报酬。”

en: Indeed, it's a bit of a mystery why governments, archaeologists, and treasure hunters can't work together—and why salvors aren't at least given a substantial finder's fee before the original owner takes possession of the vessel and its artifacts. (38 words)
cn: 事实上，政府、考古学家和寻宝者为何始终无法携手合作，以及为何在原属国收回船只及其文物之前，打捞者至少不能获得一笔可观的“发现者酬金”，这确实是个令人费解的谜团。

en: Could you get by without using the Internet for four and a half years? (14 words)
cn: 你能整整四年半不使用互联网、依然正常生活下去吗？

en: That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health. (18 words)
cn: 而这，正是歌手兼演员塞琳娜·戈麦斯为改善自己的心理健康，所做出的选择。

en: She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like 'an addict' when she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016. (30 words)
cn: 她曾多次公开谈论过社交媒体使用与自身心理健康之间的关系，并回忆道，2016年，当她成为Instagram粉丝数最多的用户时，自己曾感觉像是一名“瘾君子”。

en: 'Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health,' says she. (20 words)
cn: “暂时远离社交媒体，是我为自己的心理健康所做过的最正确的决定，”她说道。

en: 'The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down.' (13 words)
cn: “只要我一放下手机，那些无谓的恶意评论和攀比，就都随之烟消云散了。”

en: Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect. (14 words)
cn: 然而，彻底放弃使用整个互联网，却是一件远比这微妙、复杂得多的事情。

en: The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. (36 words)
cn: 我们社会日益数字化的趋势，意味着从缴纳燃气费，到规划前往朋友家的路线，乃至打一通电话，几乎一切事务，都完全受制于你的网络连接。

en: Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege. (12 words)
cn: 主动选择退出互联网，如今已成为一种唯有特权阶层才能真正拥有的奢侈选择。

en: Ms. Gomez's multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the 'social' out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the trolls (挑衅者) at bay. (31 words)
cn: 戈麦斯坐拥千万身家的地位，让她得以把“社交”这一环节，从“社交媒体”中彻底剥离出去——这样一来，她既能继续借助自己巨大的名气，又能把网络喷子拒之门外。

en: The fact that she's still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it's entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects—by way of a dedicated team—without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail and rape or death threats. (43 words)
cn: 而她至今仍是Instagram上粉丝数第二多的女性这一事实也说明，只要有专门团队打理，完全有可能在维持庞大网络影响力、推广各类项目的同时，避免自己直接暴露在恶毒评论、仇恨邮件，乃至强奸或死亡威胁之下。

en: It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital detox (数字排毒) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from. (50 words)
cn: 不用说，这与我们这些既没有美妆代言、也没有电影要宣传的普通人使用Instagram、TikTok和Twitter等平台的方式，有着本质的不同，但即便是所谓的“数字排毒”，也终究离不开一台设备和一份网络连接——你首先得拥有它们，才谈得上主动选择断开连接。

en: The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. (20 words)
cn: 过去两年间，英国的“数字鸿沟”问题进一步恶化，导致许多贫困家庭家中至今没有宽带网络连接。

en: Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the metaverse (元宇宙) as the next great frontier when schoolchildren are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating. (38 words)
cn: “数字排斥”，正是威胁英国更广泛社会公平的一大隐患，因此，当人们看到Facebook这样的公司还在大力鼓吹“元宇宙”是下一个伟大前沿领域时，而与此同时，无数学童却连完成家庭作业都举步维艰，这实在让人格外感到刺耳和不适。

en: Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed. (35 words)
cn: 因此，值得铭记的是：尽管删除所有社交媒体账号，无疑会让一部分人感觉无比轻松，但对另一些人来说，这些分享平台所孕育出的那种强烈的社群归属感，同样也让他们从中获益良多。

en: Internet access will continue to grow in importance as we edge further towards web 3.0, and greater resources and initiatives are needed to provide the underprivileged with the connectivity they desperately need to learn, work and live. (37 words)
cn: 随着我们不断迈向Web 3.0时代，互联网接入的重要性也将与日俱增，因此，我们需要投入更多资源、推出更多举措，为弱势群体提供他们在学习、工作和生活中亟需的网络连接。

en: It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off—and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place. (39 words)
cn: 至关重要的是：既要让那些认为社交媒体正在损害自己心理健康的人，能够自由选择“关闭”它；同时，也要让那些身处“数字排斥”困境中的人，首先拥有“开启”它的机会。

en: Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior. (20 words)
cn: 长期以来，心理学家们一直对“竞争究竟是后天习得的行为，还是人类与生俱来的基因组成部分”这一问题争论不休。

en: Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life. (21 words)
cn: 但无论其本质究竟为何，你都无法否认，竞争正在学术界以及当代生活的诸多领域中，发挥着切实的影响。

en: Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. (13 words)
cn: 从心理学的角度来看，竞争一直被视为人类内在驱力所导致的一种必然后果。

en: According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. (20 words)
cn: 按照西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的说法，人类天生就在渴求关注中呱呱坠地，并充满了在各个领域寻求满足的原始驱力。

en: Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. (9 words)
cn: 起初，我们争夺的是父母的关注。

en: Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence. (24 words)
cn: 此后，我们便始终受制于一场拉锯战：一方面是追求自我满足的原始冲动，另一方面则是禁止纯粹放纵行为的社会与文化规范。

en: Current work in anthropology (人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. (22 words)
cn: 然而，人类学领域的最新研究却表明，这种关于竞争在人类行为中所扮演角色的看法，或许并不正确。

en: Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the 'natural world, that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being 'nasty, brutish, and short.' (40 words)
cn: 十七世纪的伟大哲学家之一托马斯·霍布斯，或许最为人所铭记的，正是他对“自然世界”——即人类意志尚未施加于世界之前的那个状态——所做出的著名描述：“污秽、野蛮、而又短暂”。

en: This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, The Origin of Species, which established the doctrine of natural selection. (28 words)
cn: 这种对前理性世界的想象，至今依然广为流传，而查尔斯·达尔文那部影响深远的著作《物种起源》，更是进一步强化了这一观念——正是这部著作，确立了自然选择学说。

en: This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. (42 words)
cn: 这一学说，理所当然地认为，那些最能适应并掌控自身所处自然环境的物种，才能生存下来，并由此暗示：为生存而进行的斗争，是决定一个人能否成功的一种内在人性特质。

en: Darwin's theory has even been summarized as 'survival of the fittest'—a phrase Darwin himself never used—further highlighting competition's role in success. (21 words)
cn: 达尔文的理论，甚至被概括为“适者生存”——尽管这一说法其实并非达尔文本人所提出——这进一步凸显了竞争在成功中所扮演的角色。

en: As it has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for 'survival of the fittest.' (31 words)
cn: 然而，正如人们经常指出的那样，“自然选择”这一概念本身，其实并没有任何内容表明，竞争是实现“适者生存”的最成功策略。

en: Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation. (25 words)
cn: 达尔文本人在《物种起源》中就曾明确指出，他所描述的这种“斗争”，应当被视为一种隐喻，其中完全可以涵盖依存与合作的关系。

en: Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation—by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. (35 words)
cn: 许多研究都曾试图检验，不同文化究竟赋予了竞争怎样的重要性，又是如何将其与合作等其他价值相权衡的，而这些研究普遍得出的结论是：唯独美国人，格外推崇竞争，将其视为一种自然、必然且值得追求的品质。

en: In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. (39 words)
cn: 1937年，享誉世界的人类学家玛格丽特·米德出版了《原始民族的合作与竞争》一书，书中基于她对若干并不推崇竞争、甚至有时似乎对其持负面评价的社会所做的研究。

en: One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. (19 words)
cn: 亚利桑那州的祖尼印第安人，便是这样一个社会——米德发现，他们看重合作的程度，远远超过了竞争。

en: After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it. (36 words)
cn: 在研究了数十个类似的文化之后，米德最终得出的结论是：竞争性，是一种由文化塑造出来的人类行为特质，而它在某个特定社会中的盛行程度，也取决于该社会本身对它的重视和推崇程度。

en: Modern U.S. cities were designed to make exercise unnecessary. (9 words)
cn: 现代美国的城市，从设计之初，就旨在让人们无需再进行体力活动。

en: Cars and elevators once symbolized urban areas as machines for more efficient living. (13 words)
cn: 汽车和电梯，曾一度象征着城市地区正朝着更高效便捷的生活方式迈进。

en: Now it is clear that these improvements provide great benefits but also impose health costs. (15 words)
cn: 而如今，人们已经清楚地认识到，这些改进虽然带来了巨大的便利，却也让人们付出了健康上的代价。

en: Recent studies show that urban sprawl encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight. (15 words)
cn: 近期的研究表明，城市的无序扩张，会助长人们对开车出行的依赖，也与体重超标存在关联。

en: This correlation suggests that the layout and design of cities can hinder or promote healthier lifestyle choices and it is imperative that urban planners bear this in mind. (28 words)
cn: 这种相关性表明，城市的布局和设计，既可能阻碍、也可能促进人们做出更健康的生活方式选择，因此，城市规划者们务必要将这一点铭记于心。

en: Unfortunately, urban planning still centers in large part on solving the problems of the past. (15 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，如今的城市规划，在很大程度上，依然主要着眼于解决过去遗留下来的种种问题。

en: Of course cities still need to foster standard public health practices, such as separating toxic facilities from homes and restricting heavy truck traffic through dense residential areas. (27 words)
cn: 当然，城市依然需要坚持一些标准的公共卫生举措，比如将有毒设施与居民住宅区隔开，以及限制重型卡车穿行人口密集的居民区。

en: But it's also important to create healthier cities—and the discussion is already underway. (13 words)
cn: 但与此同时，打造更健康的城市，同样至关重要——而围绕这一话题的讨论，早已展开。

en: More and more city planners are paying increasing attention to encouraging physical activity by making it easier and safer for people to recreate, walk, bike and take public transportation. (29 words)
cn: 越来越多的城市规划者，正日益关注如何鼓励人们进行体力活动——让人们能够更轻松、更安全地娱乐休闲、步行、骑行，以及乘坐公共交通工具。

en: Many studies of longevity show that people live the longest in environments where physical activity is part of everyday life. (20 words)
cn: 许多关于长寿的研究表明，人们在那些将体力活动融入日常生活的环境中，往往能活得最久。

en: Providing more walkable spaces, better protected bike lanes and more recreational spaces are important steps. (15 words)
cn: 提供更多适合步行的空间、更完善的自行车道保护措施，以及更多的休闲娱乐空间，都是重要的举措。

en: But even smaller changes can be effective. (7 words)
cn: 但即便是一些较小的改变，也同样能够产生实实在在的效果。

en: Cities can close off streets on weekends to encourage communities to get out and walk. (15 words)
cn: 城市可以在周末封闭部分街道，鼓励社区居民走出家门、外出散步。

en: They also can provide more seating in public places, so that less-fit residents can rest during their journeys. (18 words)
cn: 城市也可以在公共场所增设更多座椅，让体能较弱的居民，能够在出行途中得以歇脚休息。

en: Using public spaces in cities as places where people can exercise promotes equity, rather than allowing physical activity to become restricted to private gyms with often-expensive monthly fees that deter less wealthy people from joining. (35 words)
cn: 把城市中的公共空间，用作人们锻炼身体的场所，有助于促进公平——而不是任由体育锻炼，被局限在那些收费往往不菲的私人健身房之中，从而将经济条件较差的人们挡在门外。

en: A) You may have heard that learning another language is one method for preventing or at least postponing the onset of dementia. (22 words)
cn: A) 你或许曾听说过，学习另一门语言，是预防、或者至少延缓痴呆症发病的方法之一。

en: Dementia refers to the loss of cognitive abilities, and one of its most common forms is Alzheimer's disease (阿尔茨海默病). (19 words)
cn: 痴呆症，指的是认知能力的丧失，而其中最常见的形式之一，便是阿尔茨海默病。

en: At this time, the causes of the disease are not well understood, and consequently, there are no proven steps that people can take to prevent it. (26 words)
cn: 目前，人们对这种疾病的成因，尚未有透彻的了解，因此，也没有任何经过证实、能够真正预防它的具体措施。

en: Nonetheless, some researchers have suggested that learning a foreign language might help delay the onset of dementia. (17 words)
cn: 尽管如此，一些研究人员还是提出，学习外语或许有助于延缓痴呆症的发病时间。

en: B) To explore this possibility more deeply, let's look at some of the common misconceptions about dementia and the aging brain. (21 words)
cn: B) 为了更深入地探讨这种可能性，让我们先来看看，人们对痴呆症和大脑衰老，普遍存在着哪些常见的误解。

en: First of all, dementia is not an inevitable part of the normal aging process. (14 words)
cn: 首先，痴呆症并不是正常衰老过程中不可避免的一部分。

en: Most older adults do not develop Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia. (13 words)
cn: 大多数老年人，并不会患上阿尔茨海默病或其他形式的痴呆症。

en: It is also important to remember that dementia is not the same thing as normal forgetfulness. (16 words)
cn: 同样重要的是要记住，痴呆症与日常生活中普通的健忘，完全是两码事。

en: At any age, we might experience difficulty finding the exact word we want or have trouble remembering the name of the person we just met. (25 words)
cn: 无论处于哪个年龄段，我们都可能一时想不起某个恰当的词，或是记不清刚认识的人的名字。

en: People with dementia have more serious problems, like feeling confused or getting lost in a familiar place. (17 words)
cn: 而痴呆症患者所面临的问题，则要严重得多，比如感到思维混乱，甚至在自己熟悉的地方也会迷路。

en: Think of it this way: If you forget where you parked your car at the mall, that's normal; if you forget how to drive a car, that may be a signal that something more serious is going on. (38 words)
cn: 不妨这样理解：如果你忘记了自己把车停在了商场的哪个位置，这属于正常现象；但如果你忘记了该怎样开车，那可能就意味着，有更严重的问题正在悄然发生。

en: C) The idea that dementia can be prevented is based on the comparison of the brain to a muscle. (19 words)
cn: C) “痴呆症可以被预防”这一观点，其实建立在“把大脑比作肌肉”这一类比之上。

en: When people talk about the brain, they sometimes say things like 'It is important to exercise your brain' or 'To stay mentally fit, you have to give your brain a workout.' (31 words)
cn: 当人们谈论大脑时，有时会说出诸如“锻炼你的大脑很重要”，或者“想要保持头脑敏捷，就得给大脑做做‘运动’”这样的话。

en: Although these are colorful analogies, in reality the brain is not a muscle. (13 words)
cn: 尽管这些比喻听起来颇为生动形象，但实际上，大脑并不是一块肌肉。

en: Unlike muscles, the brain is always active and works even during periods of rest and sleep. (16 words)
cn: 与肌肉不同，大脑始终处于活跃状态，即便在休息和睡眠期间，它也依然在持续运转。

en: In addition, although some muscle cells have a lifespan of only a few days, brain cells last a lifetime. (19 words)
cn: 此外，尽管有些肌肉细胞的寿命只有短短几天，但脑细胞却能伴随人的一生。

en: Not only that, but it has been shown that new brain cells are being created throughout one's lifespan. (18 words)
cn: 不仅如此，研究还表明，新的脑细胞会在人的一生中不断生成。

en: D) While it makes for a colorful analogy, comparing the brain to a muscle is inaccurate and misleading. (18 words)
cn: D) 尽管把大脑比作肌肉听起来颇为形象生动，但这种类比其实并不准确，甚至颇具误导性。

en: So, if the brain is not a muscle, can it still be exercised? (13 words)
cn: 那么，既然大脑并非肌肉，它是否依然可以被“锻炼”呢？

en: Once again, researchers don't know for sure. (7 words)
cn: 对此，研究人员同样也没有确切的答案。

en: There are now many computer, online, and mobile device applications that claim to be able to 'train your brain,' and they typically tap into a variety of cognitive abilities. (29 words)
cn: 如今，市面上有许多电脑、网络和移动设备应用程序，都宣称自己能够“训练你的大脑”，它们通常会涉及多种不同的认知能力。

en: However, research suggests that although this type of training may improve one's abilities at the tasks themselves, they don't seem to improve other abilities. (24 words)
cn: 然而，研究表明，尽管这类训练或许能够提升人们在特定任务本身上的表现，但它们似乎并不能提升其他方面的能力。

en: In other words, practicing a letter-detection task will, over time, improve your letter-detection skills, but it will not necessarily enhance your other perceptual abilities. (24 words)
cn: 换句话说，长期练习“字母辨识”这类任务，确实会提高你在字母辨识方面的技能，但却未必能增强你其他方面的感知能力。

en: E) However, there is some reason to believe that learning languages might be different. (14 words)
cn: E) 然而，也有一定理由让人相信，语言学习或许有所不同。

en: The best evidence that foreign language learning confers cognitive benefits comes from research with those who are already bilingual (双语的). (20 words)
cn: 支持“学习外语能够带来认知益处”这一观点的最有力证据，来自针对那些已经掌握双语的人群所做的研究。

en: Bilingualism most commonly occurs when children are exposed to two languages, either in the home (mom speaks Dutch, dad speaks Spanish) or more formally in early schooling. (27 words)
cn: 双语能力最常见的形成方式，是儿童在成长过程中同时接触两种语言，要么是在家庭环境中（比如妈妈说荷兰语，爸爸说西班牙语），要么是在早期学校教育中更为正式地习得。

en: But bilingualism certainly occurs in adulthood as well. (8 words)
cn: 但双语能力，同样也完全可能是在成年之后才逐渐掌握的。

en: F) Bilingualism and multilingualism are actually more common than you might think. (12 words)
cn: F) 双语和多语能力，实际上比你想象中要普遍得多。

en: In fact, it has been estimated that there are fewer monolingual speakers in the world than bilinguals and multilinguals. (19 words)
cn: 事实上，据估计，全世界只会一种语言的人，其数量反倒少于掌握两种或多种语言的人。

en: Although in many countries most inhabitants share just one language, other countries have several official languages. (16 words)
cn: 尽管在许多国家，大多数居民都只使用一种语言，但也有一些国家拥有多种官方语言。

en: Switzerland, for example, has four official languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. (12 words)
cn: 例如，瑞士就拥有四种官方语言：德语、法语、意大利语和罗曼什语。

en: Throughout large parts of Africa, Arabic, Swahili, French, and English are often known and used by individuals who speak a different, native language in their home than they do in the marketplace. (32 words)
cn: 在非洲的大片地区，人们在家中所使用的母语，往往与在集市等公共场合所使用的语言不同，而阿拉伯语、斯瓦希里语、法语和英语，都常常为人们所熟知和使用。

en: So bilingualism and multilingualism are to be found throughout the world. (11 words)
cn: 因此，双语和多语能力，其实遍布全世界各地。

en: And with regard to cognitive abilities, the research on those who speak more than one language paints an encouraging picture. (20 words)
cn: 而在认知能力方面，针对掌握不止一种语言人群的研究，也描绘出了一幅令人振奋的图景。

en: G) For one thing, bilinguals are better at multitasking. (9 words)
cn: G) 首先，双语者在多任务处理方面，表现得更为出色。

en: One explanation of this superiority is that speakers of two languages are continually inhibiting one of their languages, and this process of inhibition confers general cognitive benefits to other activities. (30 words)
cn: 对这种优势的一种解释是，掌握两种语言的人，会持续不断地抑制其中一种语言的使用，而这种“抑制”过程，也为其他各类活动带来了普遍性的认知益处。

en: In fact, bilingual individuals outperform their monolingual counterparts on a variety of cognitive tasks, such as following complex instructions, and switching to new instructions. (24 words)
cn: 事实上，在诸如遵循复杂指令、以及灵活切换到新指令等多种认知任务上，双语者的表现，都要优于只掌握一种语言的人。

en: For the sake of completeness, it should be noted that the advantages of being bilingual are not universal across all cognitive domains. (22 words)
cn: 但为了呈现全貌，也有必要指出，双语能力所带来的优势，并非在所有认知领域都普遍适用。

en: Bilingual individuals have been shown to have smaller vocabularies and to take longer in retrieving words from memory when compared to monolinguals. (22 words)
cn: 研究表明，与单语者相比，双语者的词汇量往往更小，从记忆中提取词汇所需的时间，也往往更长。

en: In the long run, however, the cognitive and linguistic advantages of being bilingual far outweigh these two drawbacks. (18 words)
cn: 然而，从长远来看，掌握双语所带来的认知和语言优势，还是远远超过了这两项劣势。

en: H) If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer's disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer's for bilinguals. (41 words)
cn: H) 如果双语能力所带来的益处，能够延伸到认知领域的其他方面，那么我们理应观察到，双语者患阿尔茨海默病的比例低于单语者，或者至少，双语者的发病时间会更晚一些。

en: In fact, there is evidence to support this claim. (9 words)
cn: 事实上，确实有证据支持这一观点。

en: The psychologist Ellen Bialystok and her colleagues obtained the histories of 184 individuals who had made use of a memory clinic in Toronto. (23 words)
cn: 心理学家艾伦·比亚利斯托克及其同事，收集了184名曾在多伦多某记忆诊所就诊者的病史资料。

en: For those who showed signs of dementia, the monolinguals in the sample had an average age of 71.4 years at time of onset. (23 words)
cn: 在那些表现出痴呆症状的样本中，单语者的平均发病年龄为71.4岁。

en: The bilinguals, in contrast, received their diagnosis at 75.5 years, on average. (12 words)
cn: 相比之下，双语者的平均确诊年龄，则为75.5岁。

en: In a study of this sort, a difference of four years is highly significant, and could not be explained by other systematic differences between the two groups. (27 words)
cn: 在这类研究中，四年的差距具有相当高的统计学意义，而且这种差异，也无法用两组之间其他系统性的差异来解释。

en: For example, the monolinguals reported, on average, a year and a half more schooling than their bilingual counterparts, so the effect was clearly not due to formal education. (28 words)
cn: 举例来说，单语者所报告的平均受教育年限，比双语者还多出一年半，因此，这种效应显然并非源于正规教育的差异。

en: I) A separate study, conducted in India, found strikingly similar results: bilingual patients developed symptoms of dementia 4.5 years later than monolinguals, even after other potential factors, such as gender and occupation, were controlled for. (35 words)
cn: I) 另一项在印度开展的独立研究，得出了惊人相似的结果：即便在控制了性别、职业等其他潜在因素之后，双语患者出现痴呆症状的时间，依然比单语患者晚4.5年。

en: In addition, researchers have reported other positive effects of bilingualism for cognitive abilities in later life, even when the person acquired the language in adulthood. (25 words)
cn: 此外，研究人员还报告了双语能力对晚年认知能力的其他积极影响，即便这门第二语言是在成年后才习得的，这种效应依然存在。

en: Crucially, Bialystok suggested that the positive benefits of being bilingual were only found in those who used both languages all the time. (22 words)
cn: 尤为关键的是，比亚利斯托克指出，只有那些始终坚持使用两种语言的人，才能真正从双语能力中获得这些积极益处。

en: J) But encouraging as these kinds of studies are, they still have not established exactly how or why differences between bilinguals and monolinguals exist. (24 words)
cn: J) 尽管这类研究结果颇为令人鼓舞，但它们至今仍未能确切揭示，双语者与单语者之间的差异，究竟是如何产生、又为何会产生的。

en: Because these studies looked back at the histories of people who were already bilingual, the results can only say that a difference between the two groups was found, but not why that difference occurred. (34 words)
cn: 由于这些研究都是回溯性地考察那些本已具备双语能力的人群的病史，因此，其研究结果只能说明两组之间确实存在差异，却无法解释这种差异究竟因何而起。

en: Further research is needed to determine what caused the differences in age of onset between the two groups. (18 words)
cn: 要弄清楚究竟是什么原因，导致了两组人群在发病年龄上的差异，还需要开展进一步的研究。

en: K) Other studies of successful aging suggest that being connected to one's community and having plenty of social interaction is also important in delaying or even preventing the onset of dementia. (31 words)
cn: K) 其他关于“成功老龄化”的研究表明，与所在社区保持紧密联系、并拥有充分的社交互动，对于延缓、乃至预防痴呆症的发病，同样具有重要意义。

en: Once again, however, the results are far less clear than the popular media might lead you to believe. (18 words)
cn: 然而，再一次地，这方面的研究结论，远不像大众媒体所渲染的那样清晰明确。

en: Older individuals who lead active social lives are, almost by definition, healthier than their counterparts who rarely leave their homes or interact with others. (24 words)
cn: 那些社交生活活跃的老年人，几乎可以说，天然地就比那些很少外出、很少与人互动的同龄人更为健康。

en: So we can't really say whether being socially active prevents the onset of dementia, or if people who don't have dementia are more likely to be socially active. (28 words)
cn: 因此，我们其实很难断定，究竟是积极的社交活动预防了痴呆症的发生，还是那些本就没有患上痴呆症的人，天生就更倾向于积极参与社交活动。

en: L) But even if studying a foreign language is not a magical cure-all, there is one thing it will do: It will make you a better speaker of a foreign language. (31 words)
cn: L) 但即便学习外语并非包治百病的灵丹妙药，它至少有一点确凿无疑的效果：它会让你的外语说得更好。

en: Doing that confers a whole host of advantages we do know about. (12 words)
cn: 而这一点本身，就已经能带来许许多多我们确实了解、且已被证实的好处。

en: Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development. (18 words)
cn: 研究的意义，本在于通过提高公众意识、创造能够推动发展的产品与创新成果，来造福整个社会。

en: For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals. (19 words)
cn: 而要让研究真正发挥其全部价值，研究成果就必须走出实验室和学术期刊的局限，被更广泛的社会所了解和运用。

en: Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public. (15 words)
cn: 得到有效传播的研究成果，能够在很大程度上，服务于公众的切身利益。

en: They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients. (12 words)
cn: 它们能够帮助解决各种社会不公问题，也能够改善患者所获得的治疗方案。

en: Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. (19 words)
cn: 许多研究人员似乎只满足于在学术期刊或学术会议上分享自己的研究成果。

en: But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. (9 words)
cn: 但很少有期刊，能够让所有人都自由阅读到这些研究发现。

en: Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader. (15 words)
cn: 即便是那些可以免费获取的文章，通常也是用普通读者难以理解的学术语言撰写的。

en: For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. (28 words)
cn: 对于身处“终身教职晋升体系”中的研究人员来说，他们的首要目标是获得终身教职，而实现这一目标的途径之一，便是在知名期刊上发表足够数量的论文。

en: Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised. (9 words)
cn: 在这样的压力之下，面向社区层面的科普推广工作，自然就很难被摆在优先位置。

en: Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. (14 words)
cn: 许多研究人员，也缺乏向普通大众清晰阐述自己研究成果所需的写作能力。

en: They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. (21 words)
cn: 他们或许还会担心，公众是否能够真正理解自己的研究发现，又或者担心，这些发现会被用来左右一些颇具争议的政策制定。

en: These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community. (16 words)
cn: 正是出于这些顾虑，一些研究人员选择回避，不愿在学术圈之外分享自己的研究成果。

en: Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. (14 words)
cn: 让研究成果的传播，突破学术出版物的边界，对于解决某些社会不平等问题而言，显得尤为关键。

en: It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society. (22 words)
cn: 它能够帮助家庭、社区、医疗服务提供者、政策制定者、政府机构以及其他相关利益方，更好地理解并应对困扰整个社会的各类危机。

en: The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. (8 words)
cn: 分享研究成果所带来的益处，其实是双向的。

en: Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research. (24 words)
cn: 与其他研究人员及公众展开交流互动，往往能够催生出意想不到的新联系和新思路，从而为未来的研究，指明富有成效的新方向。

en: To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated. (21 words)
cn: 为了让研究人员和所在社区都能从中受益，寻找既具创新性、又便于大众理解的成果分享方式，其重要性，怎么强调都不为过。

en: Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. (25 words)
cn: 各机构和资助方，应当支持更多研究人员，将成果发表在开放获取期刊上，这样公众就无需付费，也能阅读到这些研究成果。

en: Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly. (15 words)
cn: 各机构和研究人员，也应当投入资源，建立各类合作关系，以扩大研究成果更广泛传播的能力。

en: Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. (16 words)
cn: 此外，伦理委员会也应当将“与公众分享研究成果”，设定为对研究人员的一项强制性要求。

en: Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent. (20 words)
cn: 每一位研究参与者，都应当在知情同意的过程中，自主选择是否接收相关研究结果。

en: There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. (15 words)
cn: 由于专业术语的存在，公众有可能会对研究人员所呈现的研究结果产生误解。

en: But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public. (36 words)
cn: 但这一问题，可以通过研究人员聘请专业写作者或传播官员来加以解决，由他们协助，将研究内容转化为更易于理解的语言，并广泛地与媒体机构和公众分享。

en: Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. (27 words)
cn: 把研究成果，分享给那些受其影响最深的人群，不仅能让我们成为更出色的研究者，也能确保我们的工作，真正被用于改善人们的生活。

en: Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so. (10 words)
cn: 各机构和合作方，都必须真正认识到，这样做的价值所在。

en: Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. (12 words)
cn: 每年八月末到初秋时节，蜘蛛的存在感便会格外强烈。

en: This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs. (37 words)
cn: 这正是一些最常见蜘蛛品种的交配季节：雄性家蛛纷纷从藏身的角落中爬出，四处寻觅雌性配偶，而园蛛也已长成成体，开始编织出它们最为绚丽夺目的蛛网。

en: Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. (22 words)
cn: 尽管蜘蛛早已是儿歌童谣和万圣节装饰中司空见惯的形象，但它与人类之间的关系，却远比表面看起来要复杂得多。

en: Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. (14 words)
cn: 对蜘蛛的恐惧十分普遍，并对患有这种恐惧症的人的生活，带来了严重的影响。

en: Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. (10 words)
cn: 而这种恐惧的普遍程度，似乎与人们对实际风险的理性评估，并没有太大关联。

en: Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. (8 words)
cn: 英国的蜘蛛，几乎全部都对人类无害。

en: Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. (16 words)
cn: 生活在农田中的蜘蛛物种，通过捕食那些与人类争夺农作物的害虫，为生态系统提供了颇具价值的服务。

en: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages. (22 words)
cn: 但它们却始终是人类焦虑不安的一大来源——这种文化上的关联，可以追溯到中世纪，将蜘蛛与女巫和邪恶联系在一起。

en: Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? (21 words)
cn: 这，是否在一定程度上，解释了为何在当今这个生态危机的时代，我们却缺乏关于蜘蛛生存状况的相关数据呢？

en: British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. (22 words)
cn: 得益于长期以来收集和观察蝴蝶的悠久传统，英国的蝴蝶，已成为全世界研究最为深入的昆虫类群。

en: But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. (22 words)
cn: 但蜘蛛保护人士指出，直到20世纪80年代，家蛛的分类体系才真正得以厘清、完善。

en: And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders. (26 words)
cn: 而尽管人们已经通过统计撞击挡风玻璃或落入陷阱的昆虫数量等实验方式，来收集有关昆虫种群的数据，但针对蜘蛛数量的类似统计尝试，却少之又少。

en: The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. (18 words)
cn: 飞行类昆虫数量的大幅锐减，必然也意味着蜘蛛的食物来源正在随之减少。

en: A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. (32 words)
cn: 一项具有里程碑意义的最新研究发现，1989年至2016年间，昆虫种群数量下降了高达75%，而杀虫剂的使用，以及野生地区因开发而遭到破坏，被认为是造成这一现象的主要原因。

en: This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. (15 words)
cn: 这意味着，和大多数其他生物一样，蜘蛛的整体生存前景，同样令人担忧。

en: But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate. (25 words)
cn: 但保护人士最为担忧的，是那些因栖息地丧失和破碎化而受到威胁的蜘蛛品种——这种破碎化，使它们根本无法完成迁徙。

en: Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. (17 words)
cn: 在英国有规律记录在案的约650种蜘蛛中，大多数都生活在沼泽和荒地环境中，并在此茁壮繁衍。

en: Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. (19 words)
cn: 保护行动往往由一些意志坚定的个人所主导，通过将某些物种重新引入新的栖息地，帮助这些蜘蛛种群得以恢复。

en: With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving, along wildlife corridors. (32 words)
cn: 随着“生态重野化”如今已被正式纳入环境政策议程，人们所期望的是，未来蜘蛛能够沿着野生动物迁徙廊道自主迁移，从而更好地适应气候变化。

en: It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. (28 words)
cn: 尽管蜘蛛在自然界中拥有作为“纺织能手”的独特地位，但它们恐怕永远都难以像蜜蜂、鸟类或蝴蝶那样，赢得人类同等程度的喜爱与热情。

en: But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific. (30 words)
cn: 但当蜘蛛在这个秋天，尽情展露出自己华丽风采的时候，如果能有更多动物爱好者，认识到蜘蛛究竟有多么了不起，那也将是一件美好的事情。

en: A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky. (13 words)
cn: 彩虹是一种可能出现在天空中的多彩、弧形现象。

en: The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and dispersion of light through water droplets (小滴) present in the atmosphere. (22 words)
cn: 彩虹的色彩，是由大气中存在的水滴对光线进行反射和散射而产生的。

en: An observer may perceive a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot. (25 words)
cn: 观察者或许会以为彩虹位于某个或近或远的固定位置，但实际上，这一现象并不存在于任何具体的地点。

en: Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in relation to the direction of light. (21 words)
cn: 相反，彩虹的呈现方式，完全取决于观察者相对于光线方向所处的位置。

en: In essence, a rainbow is an optical illusion. (8 words)
cn: 从本质上讲，彩虹其实是一种光学幻象。

en: Rainbows present a spectrum made up of seven colors in a specific order. (13 words)
cn: 彩虹所呈现的，是一段按特定顺序排列的、由七种颜色组成的光谱。

en: In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name 'Roy G. Biv' as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order. (30 words)
cn: 事实上，在许多英语国家，学校会教孩子们记住“Roy G. Biv”这个名字，作为帮助记忆彩虹颜色及其排列顺序的口诀。

en: 'Roy G. Biv' stands for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. (13 words)
cn: “Roy G. Biv”分别代表：红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫。

en: The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet. (15 words)
cn: 彩虹弧的外缘是红色，内缘则是紫色。

en: A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets hanging in the atmosphere. (16 words)
cn: 当光线（通常是阳光）穿过悬浮在大气中的水滴时，彩虹便由此形成。

en: The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction (折射). (20 words)
cn: 光波在穿过水滴的过程中会发生方向改变，由此产生两个过程：反射和折射。

en: When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it originates. (19 words)
cn: 当光线在水滴表面发生反射时，它只是简单地从原来射来的方向、朝相反方向弹回。

en: When light refracts, it takes a different direction. (8 words)
cn: 而当光发生折射时，它会转向另一个不同的方向。

en: Some individuals refer to refracted light as 'bent light waves.' (10 words)
cn: 有人把经过折射的光称为“弯曲的光波”。

en: A rainbow is formed because white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions. (18 words)
cn: 彩虹之所以会形成，是因为白光进入水滴后，会在其中向若干个不同方向发生弯折。

en: When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of completely passing through the water. (27 words)
cn: 当这些经过弯折的光波到达水滴的另一侧时，它们会从水滴内反射回来，而不是径直穿透水滴。

en: Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye. (21 words)
cn: 由于白光在水中被分离开来，折射后的光在人眼看来，便呈现为一道道各自独立的颜色。

en: A) Phyllis Hartman knows what it's like to make one's way through the depths of office meeting hell. (18 words)
cn: A) 菲莉丝·哈特曼深知，在办公室“会议地狱”的深渊中艰难跋涉，究竟是一种怎样的体验。

en: Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. (25 words)
cn: 在她此前从事人力资源工作的一家公司里，管理层安排的会议多到令人咋舌，与会者要么在会议桌上打起瞌睡，要么干脆故意迟到。

en: With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. (21 words)
cn: 由于一天中大量时间都被不必要的会议占用，她常常不得不靠加班来补上原本该完成的工作。

en: 'I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done,' says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (30 words)
cn: “实际上，我花在工作上的时间，远比完成这些工作本该需要的时间要多得多，”哈特曼说道。她是宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡PGHR咨询公司的创始人兼总裁。

en: B) She isn't alone in her frustration. (7 words)
cn: B) 感到沮丧的，并不只有她一个人。

en: Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. (26 words)
cn: 在美国，每天举行的会议数量在1100万到5500万场之间，这让大多数机构要为此付出其人力预算7%到15%的成本。

en: Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours. (19 words)
cn: 每周，员工平均要花大约六个小时开会，而普通管理者用于开会的时间，竟高达惊人的23个小时。

en: C) And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. (31 words)
cn: C) 尽管专家们一致认为，传统会议对于做出某些决策、制定战略而言必不可少，但在一些员工看来，会议却是工作日中最没有必要的环节之一。

en: The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call 'meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)': time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. (34 words)
cn: 由此造成的后果，不仅是数千亿美元的浪费，还催生出一种组织心理学家称之为“会议恢复综合征”（MRS）的困扰——即在一场毫无意义的会议之后，人们需要花时间冷静下来、重新集中注意力。

en: If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you're likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome. (23 words)
cn: 如果你在一场令人沮丧的会议结束后，会跑去办公室茶水间跟同事吐槽、缓解一下情绪，那你很可能正经历着“会议恢复综合征”。

en: D) Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. (20 words)
cn: D) “会议恢复综合征”这一概念，对几乎所有从事过正式工作的人来说，都应该不算陌生。

en: It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. (25 words)
cn: 说员工在开完会后会感到疲惫，这算不上什么石破天惊的发现，但直到最近这几十年，科学家们才开始认为，这一现象值得进一步深入研究。

en: With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures. (27 words)
cn: 由于这种综合征与组织效率和员工福祉密切相关，它也因此引起了心理学家们的关注——他们意识到，有必要弄清楚其确切的成因与应对之策。

en: E) Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. (24 words)
cn: E) 就目前研究者所能提出的假设而言，“会议恢复综合征”最容易被理解为一种有限的心理与身体资源正在缓慢恢复的过程。

en: When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. (16 words)
cn: 当员工坐在一场毫无成效的会议中时，他们的脑力实际上正在被一点点消耗殆尽。

en: Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. (17 words)
cn: 如果会议拖得太久、无法调动员工的参与，或者变成了单方面的说教，都会消耗员工的活力。

en: The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person's resources are threatened or lost. (26 words)
cn: “资源保存理论”最早由史蒂文·霍布福尔博士在1989年提出，该理论认为，当一个人的资源受到威胁或遭受损失时，心理压力便会随之产生。

en: When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. (15 words)
cn: 当资源变得匮乏时，人便会转入防御状态，以保存自己所剩不多的资源。

en: In the case of office meetings, where some of employees' most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover. (33 words)
cn: 就办公室会议而言，员工最宝贵的资源莫过于专注力、警觉性和积极性，一旦这些资源被消耗殆尽，生产力便可能骤然停滞，直到他们花时间恢复过来。

en: F) As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job — say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work — it takes an effortful cognitive switch. (32 words)
cn: F) 作为人类，当我们在工作中从一项任务切换到另一项任务时——比如从坐在会议室里切换到处理日常工作——这需要付出一次颇为费力的认知转换。

en: We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. (16 words)
cn: 我们必须先从之前的任务中抽离出来，再花费大量的心理能量，才能继续投入新的工作。

en: If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. (20 words)
cn: 如果我们的精力已经被消耗到危险的程度，那么要完成这种心理上的切换，就会变得格外困难。

en: It's common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on. (26 words)
cn: 一场令人沮丧的会议结束后，人们常常会“摸鱼”上网、跑去倒杯咖啡，或是打断同事、跟他们抱怨一番刚才的会议内容，诸如此类。

en: G) Each person's ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. (11 words)
cn: G) 每个人从一场糟糕的会议中恢复过来的能力，也各不相同。

en: Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. (16 words)
cn: 有些人能很快调整过来，而另一些人则会把这种疲惫感一直带到下班时分。

en: Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee's lag time. (22 words)
cn: 尽管目前尚无正式的“会议恢复综合征”研究在进行，但人们大致还是可以推测出普通员工恢复所需的时间。

en: Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. (12 words)
cn: 在不存在“会议恢复综合征”的情况下，切换任务大约需要10到15分钟。

en: With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. (12 words)
cn: 而在“会议恢复综合征”的影响下，这一时间平均可能长达45分钟。

en: It's even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. (15 words)
cn: 如果一名员工连续参加的几场会议之间只间隔30分钟，情况则会更加糟糕。

en: 'Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting,' says researcher Joseph Allen. (32 words)
cn: 研究员约瑟夫·艾伦说：“在没有‘会议恢复综合征’的情况下，这点时间本就不够用来完成什么事情；而一旦出现这种综合征，留给下一场会议做恢复准备的时间，就更加捉襟见肘了。”

en: 'Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands.' (17 words)
cn: “再加上一场接一场糟糕会议的叠加效应，我们很可能正面临着一场‘流行病’。”

en: H) In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. (47 words)
cn: H) 为了应对“会议恢复综合征”所带来的负面影响，艾伦与研究员约瑟夫·姆罗兹以及内布拉斯加大学奥马哈分校的同事们，联合发表了一项研究，详细阐述了规避常见陷阱的最佳方法，其中还包括一份适用于任何职场的、简明扼要的注意事项清单。

en: Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS. (26 words)
cn: 姆罗兹和他的团队参考了约200篇论文，汇编出这份内容全面的清单，如今，他们或许已经掌握了应对这一此前一直定义模糊的“会议恢复综合征”问题的良方。

en: I) Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. (21 words)
cn: I) 姆罗兹表示，一个不错的切入点，是先问问自己：这场会议究竟是否真的有必要召开。

en: If all that's on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. (27 words)
cn: 如果会议议程上仅仅是简单的进度同步，或者一些并不紧急的信息共享，那么改用邮件的方式，或许更适合整个团队。

en: 'The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible,' says Mroz. (17 words)
cn: 姆罗兹说：“我一直建议的第二点，是尽量让会议规模保持精简。”

en: 'If they don't actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later.' (16 words)
cn: “如果与会者实际上并没有什么即时的意见需要输入，那么他们完全可以事后再跟进了解情况。”

en: 'They don't need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting.' (10 words)
cn: “他们根本不需要一直坐在这场长达一小时的会议里。”

en: Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS. (26 words)
cn: 减少开会的时间，最终会让员工在真正参加的会议中投入更多的参与度，而专家们一致认为，这正是应对“会议恢复综合征”行之有效的良方。

en: J) Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don't inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. (23 words)
cn: J) 组织科学教授克利夫·斯科特表示，当员工被召集去参加那些无法激发参与感的会议时，他们同样会感到身心俱疲。

en: It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting --one of the main traps of MRS. (27 words)
cn: 在一场毫无意义的会议结束后，他们需要花费宝贵的时间来宣泄情绪、发发牢骚，并努力重新集中注意力——这正是“会议恢复综合征”的主要陷阱之一。

en: Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings — and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS — the waste of workday hours can feel insulting. (33 words)
cn: 久而久之，随着员工发现自己被越来越多不必要的会议所束缚，也因此需要应对越来越长的“会议恢复综合征”恢复时间，工作时间就这样被白白浪费掉，这种感觉甚至会让人觉得受到了某种冒犯。

en: K) Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. (38 words)
cn: K) 尽管围绕这一主题的研究相对匮乏，但哈特曼已经自行摸索出许多与姆罗兹研究中所建议的相似的技巧，与当年被困在无休止的无谓会议中的自己相比，她已经取得了长足的进步。

en: The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. (29 words)
cn: 如今，她邀请参加会议的人员，不再局限于必要的核心员工，还包括来自各个可能与议题相关的部门的代表。

en: Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says. (24 words)
cn: 她表示，像她这样的管理者，即便是从非专业人士那里，也愿意寻求意见来辅助自己做决策，反而能够从员工队伍中获得更多的支持与配合。

en: L) If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen's findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. (35 words)
cn: L) 姆罗兹表示，如果一个组织能够采纳姆罗兹和艾伦研究成果中提出的全部22条建议，最明显的变化，将是日程表上会议总数的大幅减少。

en: Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. (19 words)
cn: 减少开会时间，最终将带来生产力的提升——而这正是召开会议本应实现的根本目的。

en: While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. (32 words)
cn: 尽管目前还没有任何一种应对“会议恢复综合征”的方法经过实证检验，但艾伦表示，一个颇有前景的小技巧，是让员工找出那些能够迅速把自己的情绪从消极转为积极的事物。

en: As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery. (25 words)
cn: 说起来虽然简单，但找到一个属于自己的“快乐角落”，去那里待一会儿，再直接回到工作状态中，或许正是促进恢复的关键所在。

en: M) Leaders should see also themselves as 'stewards of everyone else's valuable time', adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. (23 words)
cn: M) 《会议的惊人科学》一书的作者史蒂文·罗格尔伯格补充道，领导者也应当把自己视为“他人宝贵时间的管理者”。

en: Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees' endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS. (22 words)
cn: 具备预见潜在陷阱、并悉心照顾员工承受能力的能力，能够让领导者为应对“会议恢复综合征”提供切实有效的短期防范措施。

en: N) Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. (18 words)
cn: N) 然而，艾伦表示，最重要的一点，是各个组织需要真正认识到，会议本应是灵活多变的。

en: By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks. (19 words)
cn: 通过重新调整对待员工时间的优先次序，企业便能够从源头上彻底消除“会议恢复综合征”产生的根源。

en: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. (15 words)
cn: 讽刺和爵士乐之间，有一点出人意料的共同之处：你一听便知，无需多加解释。

en: Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. (19 words)
cn: 讽刺主要是通过语气来传达的，其语气所要表达的，往往正是字面意思的反面。

en: For example, when someone says, 'Well, that's exactly what I need right now,' their tone can tell you it's not what they need at all. (25 words)
cn: 比如，当有人说“哦，这正是我现在最需要的”时，他们的语气会告诉你，这其实根本不是他们想要的东西。

en: Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean. (11 words)
cn: 讽刺最常见的作用，要么是凸显某种恼怒，要么，说白了，就只是刻薄而已。

en: If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm. (13 words)
cn: 如果你想让自己更快乐、也让人际关系更融洽，那就该戒掉讽刺。

en: Why? (1 words)
cn: 为什么呢？

en: Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor. (8 words)
cn: 因为讽刺，本质上其实是伪装成幽默的敌意。

en: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. (22 words)
cn: 尽管表面上带着微笑，许多接收到讽刺言语的人，内心其实感到被贬低，也常常会觉得说这话的人既无礼又令人不齿。

en: Indeed, it's not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word 'sarkazein' which literally means 'to tear or strip the flesh off.' (27 words)
cn: 事实上，“sarcasm”（讽刺）一词源于希腊语“sarkazein”，其字面意思是“撕裂或剥去皮肉”，这一点也就不足为奇了。

en: Hence, it's no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word 'cutting' and that it hurts. (17 words)
cn: 因此，讽刺常常被冠以“尖刻”一词，且确实会伤人，这也就毫不奇怪了。

en: What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. (26 words)
cn: 此外，由于行为在很大程度上决定着一个人的想法和感受，一个人如果总是习惯性地表现出讽刺的态度，这种行为本身，反倒可能会进一步加深他内心潜藏的敌意与不安全感。

en: After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly. (26 words)
cn: 说到底，讽刺其实可以被用作一种隐蔽的霸凌形式——而大多数施加霸凌的人，本身往往就带着愤怒、不安全感，或是懦弱。

en: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. (21 words)
cn: 反过来说，当一个人不再随口说出负面言论、尤其是讽刺性的话语时，他很快就可能会变得更加快乐、也更加自信。

en: Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm. (22 words)
cn: 与此同时，他生活中的其他人，获益或许会更多——因为他们再也不必去承受那些带有情感伤害性的讽刺言语了。

en: Now, I'm not saying all sarcasm is bad. (8 words)
cn: 当然，我并不是说所有的讽刺都是不好的。

en: It may just be better used sparingly--like a potent spice in cooking. (12 words)
cn: 只是，它或许最好像烹饪中一味劲道十足的香料那样，适量使用。

en: Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it. (13 words)
cn: 一旦放得太多，整道菜的味道就会被它完全盖过。

en: Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it. (20 words)
cn: 同样，偶尔来一点带着讽刺意味的机智，也能为一场对话增添一丝风味，添上一份幽默的色彩。

en: But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient. (24 words)
cn: 但如果讽刺的分量下得太重、或是持续不断地出现，就会把整场对话的情感基调彻底盖过，让接收者尝到一种十分苦涩的滋味。

en: So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you're communicating with. (26 words)
cn: 所以，不妨把讽刺的分量降低一些，转而努力培养机智风趣的表达方式——这种表达通常不带任何敌意，因而也更容易得到交流对象的欣赏。

en: In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent. (11 words)
cn: 从本质上说，讽刺人人都能轻易做到，而真正无害的机智风趣，却需要天分和技巧。

en: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. (20 words)
cn: 因此，机智与讽刺之间的主要区别，正如前文所言，在于讽刺往往是伪装成幽默的敌意。

en: It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. (12 words)
cn: 它可能带有伤害对方的意图，语气也常常尖酸刻薄。

en: Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. (26 words)
cn: 而机智的言辞，通常是对他人无益的言行所做出的回应，其目的是通过凸显问题的荒谬之处，来厘清并阐明事情的本质。

en: Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor. (17 words)
cn: 讽刺性的话语，往往以尖刻的方式表达出来；而机智风趣的言辞，则带着毫不掩饰、也毫无恶意的幽默感。

en: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. (8 words)
cn: 多样性对于学习新技能而言，至关重要。

en: Consider learning how to serve in tennis. (7 words)
cn: 不妨以学习网球发球为例。

en: Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? (18 words)
cn: 你是否应该总是在球场上同一个位置发球、瞄准同一个落点进行练习呢？

en: Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. (23 words)
cn: 尽管在条件更加多样的情况下进行练习，起初进步会显得更慢一些，但从长远来看，这样做很可能会让你成为一名更出色的网球选手。

en: This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned. (12 words)
cn: 这是因为，多样性能够让所学的内容更好地泛化、应用到更广泛的情境之中。

en: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. (13 words)
cn: 这一原理，在许多领域中都能观察到，包括言语感知和类别学习等。

en: For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category 'dog' if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs. (24 words)
cn: 例如，如果婴儿接触到的只有吉娃娃，而没有接触过其他各种品种的狗，他们就很难学会“狗”这一类别概念。

en: 'There are over ten different names for this basic principle,' says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. (20 words)
cn: 一项最新研究的高级研究员利莫尔·拉维夫说：“这一基本原理，目前已经有超过十种不同的名称。”

en: 'Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli.' (16 words)
cn: “从变化较少的输入中学习，往往速度更快，但却可能难以泛化应用到新的刺激情境之中。”

en: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education. (36 words)
cn: 为了找出关键规律、理解多样性效应背后的原理，拉维夫和她的同事们回顾梳理了150多项与多样性和泛化相关的研究，这些研究横跨计算机科学、语言学、类别学习、视觉感知以及正规教育等多个领域。

en: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. (25 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，在这些研究中，“多样性”一词至少可以指代四种不同类型的多样性，例如样本集大小和安排方式等。

en: 'These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared - which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning,' says Raviv. (26 words)
cn: 拉维夫说：“这四种类型的多样性，此前从未被直接放在一起比较过——这意味着，我们目前尚不清楚，究竟哪一种对学习最为有效。”

en: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. (15 words)
cn: 多样性所带来的影响，取决于它是否与当前所要完成的任务相关。

en: But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills. (18 words)
cn: 但根据“宫城先生原理”，练习那些看似毫不相关的技能，实际上可能反而有助于其他技能的学习。

en: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? (8 words)
cn: 但多样性究竟为何会对学习和泛化产生影响呢？

en: One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not. (20 words)
cn: 一种理论认为，更多样化的输入，能够凸显出一项任务中哪些方面才是相关的、哪些则并不相关。

en: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. (10 words)
cn: 另一种理论则认为，更强的多样性能够带来更广泛的泛化能力。

en: This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical (非典型的) examples. (14 words)
cn: 这是因为，多样性能够更好地反映真实世界的样貌，其中也包括那些非典型的例子。

en: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories. (23 words)
cn: 第三个原因，则与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练内容具有多样性时，学习者便不得不主动地对自己的记忆进行重构。

en: 'Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives,' explains Raviv. (37 words)
cn: 拉维夫解释道：“理解多样性所带来的影响，对我们日常生活的方方面面而言，可以说都至关重要。它不仅会影响我们学习语言、运动技能和各种类别概念的方式，甚至还会对我们的社交生活产生影响。”

en: 'For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.' (20 words)
cn: “举例来说，一个人是在小社区还是大社区中长大，会影响他们的人脸识别能力。”

en: 'Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory.' (12 words)
cn: “童年时期接触的面孔数量较少，往往与成年后人脸记忆能力的减弱有关。”

en: 'We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic,' concludes Raviv. (17 words)
cn: 拉维夫总结道：“我们希望这项研究，能够激发人们的好奇心，并推动围绕这一主题展开更多的研究工作。”

en: 'Our paper raises a lot of open questions.' (8 words)
cn: “我们的论文提出了许多尚未解答的问题。”

en: 'Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?' (16 words)
cn: “我们是否能够在大脑之外的领域，比如免疫系统中，发现类似的多样性效应呢？”

en: It's quite remarkable how different genres of music can spark unique feelings, emotions, and memories. (15 words)
cn: 不同风格的音乐，竟能激发出如此独特的感受、情绪和回忆，这实在令人惊叹。

en: Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries and we are all attracted toward our own unique life soundtrack. (23 words)
cn: 研究表明，音乐能够缓解手术前的压力和焦虑，而我们每个人，也都会被属于自己人生的那份独特“配乐”所吸引。

en: If you're looking to alleviate stress, you might want to give classical music a try. (15 words)
cn: 如果你正想缓解压力，不妨试试古典音乐。

en: The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting loose pleasure-inducing dopamine (多巴胺) in the brain that helps control attention, learning and emotional responses. (25 words)
cn: 古典音乐的声音能够产生一种镇静的效果，促使大脑释放出令人愉悦的多巴胺，帮助调节专注力、学习能力以及情绪反应。

en: It can also turn down the body's stress response, resulting in an overall happier mood. (15 words)
cn: 它还能降低身体的压力反应，从而带来整体上更愉悦的心情。

en: It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to clarity in a person's thinking. (14 words)
cn: 事实证明，愉悦的心情，能够让一个人的思维变得更加清晰。
