en: Although there are many great composers of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel, none of these artists' music seem to have the same health effects as Mozart's does. (29 words)
cn: 尽管古典音乐界不乏巴赫、贝多芬、亨德尔这样伟大的作曲家，但这些艺术家的音乐，似乎都不像莫扎特的音乐那样，具备同等程度的健康功效。

en: According to researchers, listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve cognitive function. (15 words)
cn: 研究人员表示，聆听莫扎特的音乐能够提升脑电波活动，改善认知功能。

en: Another study found that the distinctive features of Mozart's music trigger parts of the brain that are responsible for high-level mental functions. (22 words)
cn: 另一项研究发现，莫扎特音乐所独有的特征，能够激活大脑中负责高级心智功能的区域。

en: Even maternity wards use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother's belly. (17 words)
cn: 甚至连产科病房，也会播放莫扎特的音乐，帮助新生儿适应离开母体后的外部生活。

en: It has been found that listening to classical music significantly reduces a person's blood pressure. (15 words)
cn: 研究还发现，聆听古典音乐能够显著降低一个人的血压。

en: Researchers believe that the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart recover from stress. (16 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，古典音乐那份令人平静的声音，或许有助于让你的心脏从压力状态中恢复过来。

en: Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping. (15 words)
cn: 古典音乐也可以是一种帮助失眠人群的有效工具。

en: One study found that students who had trouble sleeping slept better while they were listening to classical music. (18 words)
cn: 一项研究发现，那些原本睡眠不佳的学生，在聆听古典音乐时，睡眠质量得到了改善。

en: Whether classical music is something that you listen to on a regular basis or not, it wouldn't hurt to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find soothing. (33 words)
cn: 无论你是否经常聆听古典音乐，每天抽出一点时间，去听一听那些能让你感到舒缓平静的音乐，总归不会有什么坏处。

en: You will be surprised at how good it makes you feel and the potentially positive change in your health. (19 words)
cn: 你会惊讶地发现，这样做能让你感觉有多好，也可能会为你的健康带来一些积极的变化。

en: A) In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark-- a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. (26 words)
cn: A) 在美国佐治亚州雅典市，坐落着一处颇为奇特的当地地标——一棵巨大的白橡树，几乎人人都说它“拥有自己”。

en: Because of this, it is considered one of the more famous trees in the world. (15 words)
cn: 正因如此，它被视为世界上颇为著名的树木之一。

en: So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it? (14 words)
cn: 那么，这棵树究竟是如何“拥有”了自己以及周围那片土地的呢？

en: B) Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. (27 words)
cn: B) 据说，19世纪的某个时期，一位名叫威廉·杰克逊上校的佐治亚人，对这棵树情有独钟，并竭力想要保护它免受任何伤害。

en: As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. (31 words)
cn: 至于他为何如此钟爱这棵树，关于这个故事最早的文字记载，是一篇1890年8月12日发表在《雅典周报》头版、作者匿名的文章。

en: It states, 'Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human.' (23 words)
cn: 文章写道：“杰克逊上校自幼便看着这棵树长大，对它的喜爱之情，几乎不亚于对待一个人。”

en: 'Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers.' (32 words)
cn: “它繁茂的枝叶和粗壮的枝干，常常为他遮挡暴雨，而他也曾无数次爬上它最高的枝头，去掏取鸣禽的鸟蛋。”

en: 'He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it.' (41 words)
cn: “他看着这棵树一天天长大，直到自己年事已高，望着眼前这棵枝繁叶茂、气势恢宏的大树，他不禁痛心地想到，自己去世之后，这棵树恐怕会落入那些可能会毁掉它的人手中。”

en: C) Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. (25 words)
cn: C) 为此，杰克逊通过一份契约，将这棵树以及它周围一小片土地的所有权，转让给了这棵树本身。

en: The deed read, 'W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides.' (51 words)
cn: 这份契约写道：“威廉·H·杰克逊出于对这棵橡树的深厚感情，以及希望它能得到保护的殷切愿望，特将这棵橡树自身及其四周八英尺以内的全部土地，完全转让给它自己所有。”

en: D) In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. (20 words)
cn: D) 随着时间推移，这棵树逐渐成为了一处小小的旅游景点，被人们称为“拥有自己的树”。

en: However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. (23 words)
cn: 然而，进入20世纪初，这棵树开始显现出缓慢死亡的迹象，人们对此也无能为力。

en: Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians (守护者) of Earth. (20 words)
cn: 时间终究会追上我们所有人，即便是像树木这样通常寿命悠长、高大葱郁、堪称地球“守护者”的存在，也不例外。

en: Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted. (35 words)
cn: 据传，1942年10月9日，这棵高逾30米、树龄200至400年的大树，最终因一场猛烈的暴风雨、以及（或）此前早已死亡、根系腐烂而轰然倒下。

en: E) About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from an acorn taken from the original tree. (35 words)
cn: E) 大约四年后，“少女园艺俱乐部”（曾在这棵树不幸倒下之前一直悉心照料它）的成员们，找到了一棵由这棵原树的橡子培育而成的小树苗。

en: And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. (37 words)
cn: 就这样，1946年10月9日，在佐治亚大学农学院罗伊·鲍登教授的指导下，这棵小树苗被移植到了它“先祖”曾经矗立的地方。

en: A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion. (25 words)
cn: 几个月后，雅典市市长罗伯特·L·麦克沃特亲自出席，举行了一场正式的纪念仪式，以庆祝这一时刻。

en: F) This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. (33 words)
cn: F) 这棵新树后来被称为“自己拥有之树之子”，人们默认，作为原树的“继承者”，它自然而然地继承了自己所立之地的土地所有权。

en: Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. (29 words)
cn: 当然，据了解，由这棵原树的种子培育而来、如今仍存活的其他树木还有好几十棵，因为总会有人取走它的果实、种到别处去。

en: That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. (26 words)
cn: 不过话说回来，到目前为止，原树的其他“子女”都还没有向法院提出过分得这片土地的诉求，所以看起来一切相安无事。

en: In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though is often referred to as simply The Tree That Own Itself. (26 words)
cn: 无论如何，“自己拥有之树之子”至今依然屹立不倒，尽管人们通常还是简单地称它为“拥有自己的树”。

en: G) This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding. (31 words)
cn: G) 说到这里，问题便自然而然地回到了：杰克逊当初究竟是否真的将这棵树的法律所有权转让给了它自己，而这样一份契约又是否具备法律效力。

en: H) Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. (63 words)
cn: H) 首先，事实证明，杰克逊一生中只在雅典生活过大约三年时间——从43岁那年，即1829年到1832年，这在一定程度上，就已经推翻了他自幼便在这棵树下度过童年、看着它长大、并在临终前为它的命运忧心忡忡这一说法。

en: Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on. (24 words)
cn: 此外，对雅典地区土地所有权记录的全面查证也显示，并没有证据表明杰克逊曾经拥有这棵树所在的那片土地。

en: I) He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear. (27 words)
cn: I) 在那三年里，他确实是住在紧邻这棵树的一片土地上，但他是否真正拥有那片土地，却并不清楚。

en: Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. (34 words)
cn: 无论如何，1832年，一块四英亩的地产——其中就包括这棵树所在的土地，以及杰克逊居住的那片相邻土地在内——被出售给了大学教授马尔萨斯·A·沃德。

en: In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31,000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. (33 words)
cn: 在这笔交易中，沃德需要向杰克逊支付1200美元（相当于今天约3.1万美元），这笔钱要么是用于购买地产本身，要么只是对杰克逊此前在这片土地上所做改良的一种补偿。

en: In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand. (45 words)
cn: 说到底，不管他当初是真的拥有那片相邻的土地，还是仅仅因为据传曾在大学任职而被允许使用它，有一点是确定的：他从未拥有过这棵树真正生长的那块土地——而这，恰恰才是探讨这个问题时最关键的一点。

en: J) After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. (23 words)
cn: J) 沃德教授购得那片土地后，杰克逊一家便在几英里外购置了一块655英亩的土地，并搬去了那里。

en: Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seems to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. (32 words)
cn: 十年后，也就是1844年，杰克逊似乎陷入了财务困境，他名下那片小小的种植园被克拉克县治安官办公室查封，并被拍卖以偿还抵押贷款。

en: Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well. (32 words)
cn: 由此推断，倘若他当初真的在雅典本地拥有一些土地——包括这棵树所在的那块地在内——他很可能早就会将其变卖以筹措资金，否则，这块地恐怕也难逃被一并没收的命运。

en: K) And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. (30 words)
cn: K) 而且，不管实际情况如何，杰克逊本应清楚，要想让这棵树的未来真正得到保障，就必须为那片已被“转让”出去的土地缴纳财产税。

en: Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this. (17 words)
cn: 然而，却没有任何文献或记录表明，曾有人为此专门设立过信托之类的机制来加以落实。

en: L) On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it. (59 words)
cn: L) 除此之外，也根本没有确凿证据能够证明，这样一份契约确实曾经存在过——尽管雅典地区的契约记录，早在杰克逊1876年去世之前几十年便已开始留存，而据那位声称曾亲眼见过这份契约、身份不明的原始报道记者所说，它在1890年时理应还保存在档案之中。

en: M) As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. (18 words)
cn: M) 从以上种种来看，你大概也能猜到，几乎没有多少人真正相信这个故事的这一面。

en: So how did all of this come about then? (9 words)
cn: 那么，这一切究竟又是从何而来的呢？

en: N) It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled 'Deeded to Itself', which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. (47 words)
cn: N) 有人推测，这个故事其实是《雅典周报》那位匿名作者凭空杜撰出来的，出自前文提到的那篇1890年头版文章《转让给自己》，而这篇文章中，还包含着好几处更容易被证明纯属子虚乌有的内容。

en: As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not. (41 words)
cn: 至于这位作者为何要这样做，人们推测，这或许是19世纪版本的一种“标题党”式思想实验——探讨的是，一个人能否合法地把这样一件没有意识的生命体“转让”给它自己。

en: O) Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owned Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of the that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. (32 words)
cn: O) 不管真相如何，下一次已知提及“拥有自己的树”的记载，要等到1901年，同样是刊登在《雅典周报》的百年纪念特刊上。

en: This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. (19 words)
cn: 这篇报道显然只是照搬了约十年前发表的那篇原始文章，只是措辞上略作了改动。

en: The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original. (36 words)
cn: 再下一次报道则是在1906年，同样刊登在《雅典周报》上，同样明显是在照搬原始报道、只是略微改写了措辞——这大概就是19世纪版本的“旧闻重发”，专门用来对付那些早已淡忘原始报道的读者。

en: It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. (12 words)
cn: 员工能够分辨是非对错，这一点毋庸置疑。

en: So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace? (16 words)
cn: 那么，当他们在职场中看到有人表现出危险行为时，为什么更多的员工却选择不加干预呢？

en: There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. (11 words)
cn: 有若干因素会影响一个人是否会出面干预。

en: First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. (14 words)
cn: 首先，他们得能够察觉到一个危险局面正在逐渐显现。

en: Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. (13 words)
cn: 其次，公司的文化氛围需要让他们感到，站出来发声是安全的。

en: And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively. (13 words)
cn: 第三，他们还需要具备有效沟通的能力，才能把话说清楚、说到位。

en: This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. (15 words)
cn: 这并不仅仅是一个职场问题；在工作之外，这同样是一个日益凸显的问题。

en: Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. (14 words)
cn: 人们每天都会在街头目睹各种事情，却往往选择袖手旁观。

en: This is known as the bystander effect—the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. (25 words)
cn: 这种现象被称为“旁观者效应”——目睹某一事件的人越多，这群人中愿意出手帮助受害者的可能性反而越低。

en: The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. (9 words)
cn: 这一现象背后的心理学原理，被称为“责任分散”。

en: Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need. (28 words)
cn: 简单来说，围观的人越多，人们就越倾向于认为会有别人来处理——结果就是，在真正需要有人出手的关键时刻，却没有任何人真正采取行动或加以干预。

en: This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. (13 words)
cn: 这种从众心理的力量之强，甚至足以让人们逃避自己本应承担的责任。

en: But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. (14 words)
cn: 但在职场中，不出手进行安全干预的，并不只是一线员工。

en: There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either. (10 words)
cn: 也确实存在主管同样选择不加干预的情况。

en: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone. (35 words)
cn: 当一群员工看到不安全行为在领导层面都没有得到处理时，这便树立了一种先例——仿佛这类情况本就该如此应对，从而为所有人定义了整个团队的安全文化。

en: Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. (22 words)
cn: 尽管公司鼓励员工在发现不安全操作时挺身而出、加以干预，但实际这样做的比例却不到一半。

en: Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. (8 words)
cn: 恐惧，是导致人们不愿干预的根本因素。

en: There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. (18 words)
cn: 他们既害怕受到处罚，也担心一旦出手干预，自己反而要承担更多的工作。

en: Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations. (29 words)
cn: 过去干预未能奏效的经历，是另一个促使人们不愿干预的重要因素——这会让他们在此后遇到类似情况时，更倾向于把行动的责任推给别人。

en: On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. (8 words)
cn: 在许多工作场所，都必须指定专门的“胜任人员”。

en: Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. (22 words)
cn: 他们的部分职责，就是在员工没有配备恰当设备、或作业条件不安全时，及时出面干预。

en: Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger. (14 words)
cn: 一旦出现危险情况，这些“胜任人员”还必须要求立即停止作业。

en: Supervisors also play a critical role. (6 words)
cn: 主管同样扮演着至关重要的角色。

en: Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them. (39 words)
cn: 即便某个岗位并不硬性要求配备“胜任人员”，主管也需要具备一整套广泛的技能，不仅要能够识别并化解职场中的各类隐患，还要在自己的团队内部营造出一种鼓励主动干预、支持坦诚沟通的安全氛围。

en: Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker. (38 words)
cn: 除了“胜任人员”和主管之外，同样重要的是，要让组织内的每一个人都明白：无论你是被指定的“胜任人员”、主管，还是一线员工，只要目睹可能存在的不安全行为，就都有责任及时加以干预。

en: The term 'environmentalist' can mean different things. (7 words)
cn: “环保主义者”这个词，可以有着不同的含义。

en: It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. (13 words)
cn: 过去，它指的是那些致力于保护野生动物和自然生态系统的人。

en: In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change. (17 words)
cn: 进入21世纪后，这一术语的含义逐渐演变，开始涵盖应对人为气候变化这一迫切需求。

en: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy. (21 words)
cn: 环保主义这两条脉络之间的差异，正是科学界围绕核能问题产生分歧的根源所在。

en: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. (24 words)
cn: 一方是纯粹主义者，他们认为核能带来的风险得不偿失，应对气候危机的唯一出路，就是可再生能源。

en: The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. (32 words)
cn: 另一方则同样认同可再生能源至关重要，但同时指出，社会仍需要具备一定的可用电力储备，以便在阳光不足、风力不够的时候，满足消费者的基本用电需求。

en: Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited. (20 words)
cn: 核能远比石油、天然气和煤炭更为清洁，因此自然而然地成为了一个可行的选项，尤其是在水电资源有限的地区。

en: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality. (36 words)
cn: 曾参与联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）报告撰写工作的利昂·克拉克，虽然并非毫无保留地支持核能，但他表示，如果我们真的认真对待碳中和这一目标，核能就是一个颇有价值的选项。

en: 'Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables,' he said. (23 words)
cn: 他说：“这一切的核心，在于你究竟认为我们能在多大程度上，仅靠百分之百的可再生能源，就实现既定的气候目标。”

en: 'If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear.' (23 words)
cn: “如果你不相信我们能够单靠可再生能源做到这一点，同时你又真正关心气候问题，那你就不得不去认真考虑核能这类选项了。”

en: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. (9 words)
cn: 全球范围内实现百分之百可再生能源这一目标是否真正可行，同样也存在争议。

en: Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been '100% renewable' for years. (11 words)
cn: 像佛蒙特州伯灵顿这样的城市，多年来一直宣称自己已实现“百分之百可再生能源”。

en: But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. (23 words)
cn: 但这些城市往往人口规模较小，有时仍需依赖化石能源，而且本身就拥有大量唾手可得的可再生资源。

en: Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，那些真正能够完全依靠可再生能源运转的国家，通常也是得益于其得天独厚的水电资源。

en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. (16 words)
cn: 德国堪称大型工业化国家大力推行绿色能源的最佳案例。

en: Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. (21 words)
cn: 2011年，时任德国总理安格拉·默克尔宣布推行“能源转型”（Energiewende）计划，旨在逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时逐步引入可再生能源。

en: Wind and solar power generation are has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019. (22 words)
cn: 自2010年以来，德国的风能和太阳能发电量增长了超过400%，到2019年，可再生能源已占该国电力供应总量的46%。

en: But progress has halted in recent years. (7 words)
cn: 但近年来，这一进程却陷入了停滞。

en: The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. (36 words)
cn: 可再生能源本身的不稳定性，不仅意味着夜间往往难以产生足够的电力，也意味着白天太阳能和风能有时会“供过于求”，甚至给电网造成过大负荷，逼得电力公司不得不倒贴钱、鼓励用户多用电。

en: Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. (27 words)
cn: 由于电网基础设施建设进展滞后，难以将德国北部过剩的绿色电力，源源不断地输送到南部的工业地区，导致许多工厂至今仍在依靠煤炭和天然气运转。

en: The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests. (22 words)
cn: 在一些地方，政治层面的容忍度也已达到极限，当地居民纷纷以强烈抗议，回应新建风力发电机组的计划。

en: The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%. (21 words)
cn: 最终结果是，自2010年以来，德国的温室气体排放量大约下降了11.5%——这一降幅，甚至低于欧盟13.5%的平均水平。

en: The Sun is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny. (17 words)
cn: 《太阳也是一颗星》是一个关于爱情、浪漫、命运与宿命的、真正动人的故事。

en: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living illegally in America, not by choice exactly. (13 words)
cn: 娜塔莎是一名出生于牙买加的移民，如今在美国过着非法居留的生活，而这其实并非她自己的选择。

en: Her parents brought her over and created the situation she strives to be out of. (15 words)
cn: 是她的父母把她带到了美国，也正是他们，把她推入了如今这个她一心想要摆脱的处境。

en: Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. (8 words)
cn: 丹尼尔是一名美国人，父母是韩国移民。

en: He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha dismisses through scientific reasoning. (17 words)
cn: 他相信真爱、命运，以及娜塔莎用科学理性一概加以否定的种种“无稽之谈”。

en: Daniel and Natasha meet by coincidence on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be deported. (21 words)
cn: 丹尼尔和娜塔莎在纽约街头偶然相遇，而这一天，恰好正是她即将被驱逐出境的日子。

en: She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day. (31 words)
cn: 她没有把这件事告诉他，却还是允许他整天陪伴在自己身边——尽管他其实是想借这一天的时间，努力让她爱上自己。

en: Natasha is me. (3 words)
cn: 娜塔莎，就是我。

en: I found her so similar to myself. (7 words)
cn: 我发现她和我自己是如此相似。

en: She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always skeptical. (8 words)
cn: 她思维缜密、讲求科学，做事务实，还带着几分愤世嫉俗，也始终保持着怀疑的态度。

en: Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I adore Daniel seeing that too. (18 words)
cn: 她那种透过科学视角、痴迷于宇宙万物的劲头，极具感染力，而我也很喜欢看到丹尼尔同样为之着迷。

en: Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even cracks Natasha's tough outer shell. (18 words)
cn: 丹尼尔为人迷人而又充满激情，他的言辞总能打动人心，甚至连娜塔莎那层坚硬的外壳，也被他一点点敲开了裂缝。

en: By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them. (14 words)
cn: 读完这本书，我已经爱上了这两个人物。

en: I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. (12 words)
cn: 我曾经总觉得，爱情故事既廉价又可笑。

en: I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. (16 words)
cn: 但现在我想，我终于能够体会到，沉浸在一个纯粹乐观的故事里，究竟有着怎样的价值。

en: I got lost in The Sun is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. (19 words)
cn: 我完全沉浸在了《太阳也是一颗星》之中，一个周末，就把整本书从头到尾读完了。

en: I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending. (14 words)
cn: 我迫不及待地想知道结局——我多么希望它会是一个幸福的结局。

en: It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic. (12 words)
cn: 偶尔向魔法屈服一次，感觉真好。

en: It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. (27 words)
cn: 它不必是一部带着真正咒语的硬核奇幻小说，它也可以只是两个彼此拥有那份特殊感觉的人之间所迸发出的“魔力”。

en: That chemistry that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other. (14 words)
cn: 那种化学反应，会让他们只要靠近彼此，便产生反应，擦出火花。

en: A) According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. (13 words)
cn: A) 根据最近的研究，行为的改变，其实伴随着大脑内部的生理变化。

en: In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. (28 words)
cn: 过去十年间，研究人员已经证明，要让一种新行为真正内化为根深蒂固的习惯，所需的时间并没有一个简单划一的答案。

en: Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. (27 words)
cn: 即便是我们当中效率最高、最有自律精神的人，要摆脱一件早已成为我们身份自动组成部分的事情，也绝非一朝一夕之功。

en: Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself. (33 words)
cn: 一旦我们成功实现了这种改变，接下来还必须对生活做出其他相应的调整，才能确保这种改变得以持续维持——而这本身，往往又是另一项全新的挑战。

en: B) At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. (21 words)
cn: B) 从根本上说，若不引入某种行之有效的系统，想要成功改变并维持一种行为，几乎是不可能的。

en: When there isn't the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. (18 words)
cn: 一旦缺乏正确的框架作为支撑，我们辛苦取得的进步，就更有可能功亏一篑。

en: To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits. (17 words)
cn: 为了确保能够成功改变并维持某种行为，我们应当避开一些有害的习惯做法。

en: C) The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. (10 words)
cn: C) 第一个应当避免的做法，是单纯依赖意志力。

en: Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. (11 words)
cn: 回想一下，你上一次发誓要抵御某种诱惑，是什么时候。

en: Perhaps you didn't want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p.m. (25 words)
cn: 或许你曾下定决心不再每隔15分钟就看一次手机，又或者，你曾发誓下午三点绝不再伸手去拿一块巧克力。

en: Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit. (32 words)
cn: 想想看，当手机近在咫尺时，要忍住不去瞄一眼，又或者，当午后倦意袭来时，要忍住不走向自动售货机，这该有多么困难。

en: D) The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. (33 words)
cn: D) 关于人类意志力究竟是有限的还是无限的，相关研究目前尚无定论，但专家们大体上都认同一点：如果只依靠意志力，是无法真正改变并维持一种习惯的。

en: The old military saying 'You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training' also applies to behavior change. (23 words)
cn: 一句古老的军事格言——“临场发挥不会超越水平，只会跌落到训练水平”——同样适用于行为改变。

en: The idea is simple—you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic. (13 words)
cn: 这个道理很简单——只要把某件事重复足够多次，它便会成为一种自动化的行为。

en: E) Think about what else you can change about your surrounding that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. (25 words)
cn: E) 想一想，你还可以对周围环境做出哪些改变，好让自己每天更容易坚持完成这种行为改变。

en: It is called your 'cue.' (5 words)
cn: 这就是所谓的“提示物”。

en: Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit. (9 words)
cn: 从本质上说，它是触发你去执行某个特定习惯的一个开关。

en: If you don't want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p.m., have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. (23 words)
cn: 如果你不想在下午三点伸手去拿含糖零食，那就在办公桌上备好一盒草本茶。

en: When 3 p.m. comes around, that's your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine. (27 words)
cn: 等到下午三点一到，这就成了你的提示信号，提醒你去倒一杯热水、泡上那杯茶，而不是走向自动售货机。

en: F) The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. (11 words)
cn: F) 第二个应当避免的做法，是把目标设定为消极的“不做什么”。

en: Sometimes, it's not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. (21 words)
cn: 有时候，让你半途而废的，并不是你所采用的方法本身，而是你最初想要改变的那个习惯的设定方式。

en: For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. (26 words)
cn: 举例来说，“不吃巧克力来对抗午后倦意”，就是一个比“到点用草本茶替代巧克力”更难达成的目标。

en: Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. (30 words)
cn: 你的大脑，总是倾向于找出以往行之有效的固定套路，让你无需刻意思考，就能在未来不断重复这些行为。

en: However, that this habit-learning system isn't so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. (17 words)
cn: 然而，这套习惯养成机制，在应对“学会不去做某件事”这类目标时，效果却并不理想。

en: That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. (14 words)
cn: 这正是为什么，与其一味地放弃某种行为，不如考虑用另一种行为去取代它。

en: Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. (19 words)
cn: 把注意力放在你即将采取的、最终会与你想要戒除的行为产生冲突的具体行动上。

en: When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate. (17 words)
cn: 当你把注意力集中在做一件新事情上时，你也就为自己的习惯养成系统，创造了运转的机会。

en: G) The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. (14 words)
cn: G) 第三个应当避免的做法，是在不同情境下，一味套用同一种策略。

en: Because we are creatures of habit, it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. (35 words)
cn: 由于我们本就是习惯的产物，很自然地，我们会以为，既然某种策略成功帮我们养成并维持了一种理想行为，那么当我们想要改变另一种行为时，同样的策略也理应奏效。

en: But that's not always the case. (6 words)
cn: 但事实并非总是如此。

en: Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another. (15 words)
cn: 有时候，帮助你成功改变一种行为的那套系统，换到另一种行为上，可能就完全不管用了。

en: H) Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. (15 words)
cn: H) 有时候，我们习惯了在做决策时，仅仅依靠自己的直觉。

en: This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. (29 words)
cn: 这种做法在某些情境下确实行之有效，但在另一些情境下，却可能反而成为一种阻碍——尤其是当我们本该权衡各种指标和数据、而不是任由直觉主导一切的时候。

en: For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. (25 words)
cn: 举例来说，如果你想戒掉早上一睁眼就查看邮件的习惯，你或许可以决定用另一项活动来取代它。

en: But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. (23 words)
cn: 但如果你想戒掉沉迷电子游戏的习惯，仅仅决定“我要去跑步”，效果可能就没那么理想了。

en: You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together. (18 words)
cn: 这时候，你或许需要引入另一重强化机制，比如约朋友一起预订一节健身课程。

en: I) The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. (13 words)
cn: I) 第四个应当避免的做法，是在自己出现失误、状态“翻车”时，不肯原谅自己。

en: Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. (8 words)
cn: 当然，即便是最周密的计划，有时也难免会落空。

en: You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you founded yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. (35 words)
cn: 你或许已经坚持了整整五天“睡前不碰屏幕”的作息习惯，结果一个紧急的大项目突然砸到你桌上，睡前你又不由自主地抱着笔记本电脑窝在了床上。

en: Or you prepared meals on Sundays and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. (28 words)
cn: 又或者，你每逢周日都会提前备好一周的健康晚餐，结果到了周五，你已经累得筋疲力尽，最终还是点了一份油腻的外卖。

en: Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. (32 words)
cn: 生活总会横生变数，即便你所要做的行为改变本身很小，每一天的坚持也可能变得相当不易，而运气总有用尽的时候，哪怕只是某一天而已。

en: The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. (21 words)
cn: 你内心那个追求完美的自己，或许正忍不住想要彻底放弃所有目标，但请试着从更宏观的角度去看待这件事。

en: Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn't mean you can't start afresh the next day. (18 words)
cn: 只是暂时偏离了原本的轨道，并不意味着你不能在第二天重新开始。

en: J) The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. (10 words)
cn: J) 最后一个应当避免的做法，是轻视自己所取得的微小进步。

en: There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. (18 words)
cn: 许多追求完美的人，在努力实现某种行为改变时，都容易陷入这样一种习惯性误区。

en: They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. (23 words)
cn: 他们往往过于专注于宏大的最终目标，却不愿花时间去庆祝自己在这一过程中取得的点滴进步。

en: Your brain responds to rewards. (5 words)
cn: 你的大脑，是会对奖励做出回应的。

en: The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cued, and at the end, when it's rewarded. (33 words)
cn: 基底神经节——这一与我们习惯执行密切相关的脑区——在一种行为刚刚被触发、以及最终获得奖励这两个节点上，活跃程度最高。

en: Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. (24 words)
cn: 比如说，假设你的目标是每周跑三次、每次五英里，而这周你只在周一、周三、周五各跑了一英里。

en: Rather than focusing on how far you've gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you've made. (23 words)
cn: 与其一味盯着自己距离目标还有多远，不如想想看，该如何为自己已经取得的这份进步，给予一些奖励。

en: It doesn't have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. (23 words)
cn: 这份奖励不必宏大昂贵，它可以简单到，只是在跑步结束后，为自己榨一杯最爱的果汁。

en: Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going. (17 words)
cn: 但无论奖励是什么，它都必须超越这项活动本身，才能真正推动你继续坚持下去。

en: K) Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. (16 words)
cn: K) 启动一项新行为，往往看起来是整个改变过程中最艰难的部分。

en: However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. (10 words)
cn: 然而，人们却常常没能为如何维持这项改变，做好足够充分的准备。

en: One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. (29 words)
cn: 造成这种情况的原因之一，是我们误以为，当初用来启动这一改变的那些策略，同样也能有效地帮助我们把这种改变坚持下去。

en: But they won't. (3 words)
cn: 但事实并非如此。

en: Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. (30 words)
cn: 改变一种根深蒂固的习惯，需要我们改变自己对这一习惯所持有的、早已深深渗透进生活各个层面的信念，而要让这份认知能够持续地体现在行动中，就需要我们始终保持一种积极乐观的心态。

en: If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. (23 words)
cn: 一旦情绪低落，那种想要改变行为方式的智慧，似乎便会随之消失，我们也会重新回到多吃少动的老路上去。

en: The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! (11 words)
cn: 因此，维持新行为的关键，其实就在于：保持快乐！

en: Which is why it's so hard to maintain new behaviors. (10 words)
cn: 这也正是为什么，维持一种新的行为，会如此困难。

en: L) Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. (35 words)
cn: L) 请记住，克服那种阻碍我们推行诸如健康饮食、坚持锻炼等新改变的行为惯性，从长远来看，能够让我们受益良多，也有助于改善我们的身心健康。

en: No one was born with habits. (6 words)
cn: 没有人生来就带着习惯。

en: They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. (10 words)
cn: 所有的习惯，都是后天习得的，因此，它们也都可以被“卸载”。

en: The question is: how badly do you really want to change? (11 words)
cn: 问题在于：你到底有多么迫切地想要做出改变？

en: The 'American Dream' promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. (25 words)
cn: “美国梦”所承诺的，是在这片“机遇之地”，任何人只需凭借辛勤工作和雄心壮志，便能实现阶层跃升、走向富足。

en: And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations. (33 words)
cn: 然而，如今的美国年轻人，想要挣得比同龄时期的父母更多，却举步维艰；而美国的向上流动性，实际上也不及其他工业化国家。

en: So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? (10 words)
cn: 那么，“美国梦”这一理念，为何至今依然经久不衰？

en: A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV. (22 words)
cn: 《美国政治科学杂志》上的一项新研究，指出了一个此前一直被忽视的因素：真人秀电视节目的影响。

en: Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. (19 words)
cn: 范德堡大学的金恩智指出，在过去20年间，真人秀节目已经逐渐主导了美国电视荧屏。

en: And the overwhelming majority of these have a 'rags-to-riches' storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. (22 words)
cn: 而这些节目中，绝大多数都采用了“白手起家、逆袭致富”的叙事套路：讲述普通美国人通过努力工作，最终取得巨大经济成功的故事。

en: And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts — which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans — get a much smaller proportion of the viewership. (37 words)
cn: 尽管这类节目常年位列收视率最高的节目之列，但新闻节目——它们所呈现的，是数百万美国人所面临的经济困境更为真实的一面——所获得的收视份额，却要小得多。

en: Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous (无处不在的) on TV — but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? (22 words)
cn: “白手起家、逆袭致富”式的故事，在电视上可谓无处不在——但观看这类节目，是否真的会让人相信，经济地位的跃升是轻而易举的呢？

en: To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. (19 words)
cn: 为了弄清这一点，金恩智的团队让参与者观看了一段5分钟的、带有“逆袭致富”情节的真人秀节目片段。

en: Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. (15 words)
cn: 作为对照，另一组参与者观看的，则是一段不含“逆袭致富”情节的真人秀节目片段。

en: After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream. (18 words)
cn: 观看结束后，参与者需要对与“美国梦”相关的四条陈述，分别评定自己的认同程度。

en: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. (21 words)
cn: 结果显示，观看过“逆袭致富”片段的参与者，对“美国梦”的信念，确实显著更强。

en: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs. (35 words)
cn: 有趣的是，当研究人员按党派归属对参与者进行区分后发现，这一效应在共和党支持者中十分显著，但在民主党支持者中却并不明显——这似乎说明，这类电视节目中所暗含的信息，或许恰恰迎合了人们既有的社会经济观念。

en: Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. (9 words)
cn: 金恩智还对3000名美国居民展开了一项调查。

en: They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). (28 words)
cn: 参与者还需要评定，自己认为人生的成功，在多大程度上与诸如雄心壮志之类的内在因素、以及诸如家庭财富之类的外在因素相关。

en: Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched. (14 words)
cn: 最后，他们还会看到一份电视节目清单，并勾选出自己经常收看的节目。

en: Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows. (26 words)
cn: 那些经常收看、或大量观看“逆袭致富”类节目的参与者，相比从不收看此类节目的人，对“美国梦”的信念也更为强烈。

en: Kim concludes that 'rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility'. (19 words)
cn: 金恩智总结道：“‘逆袭致富’类娱乐媒体，是推动并延续人们对向上流动性之信念的一股重要文化力量。”

en: And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality. (37 words)
cn: 而问题恰恰就出在这里：如果人们错误地认为，只要努力工作，就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们对那些真正能够对抗不平等的政策，支持力度就可能会随之减弱。

en: 'In this era of choice, entertainment media are what captures hearts and minds,' Kim writes. (15 words)
cn: 金恩智写道：“在这个选择多元的时代，真正能够俘获人心的，正是娱乐媒体。”

en: 'Its political consequences are anything but trivial'. (7 words)
cn: “它所带来的政治影响，绝非无足轻重。”

en: When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. (15 words)
cn: 每当有人问起“你是做什么的？”，我们几乎总是会用自己的职业来回答。

en: Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. (11 words)
cn: 对我们许多人来说，工作的意义，远不止是一份差事那么简单。

en: It is the defining aspect of our identity. (8 words)
cn: 它，是定义我们身份的核心要素。

en: For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves. (14 words)
cn: 对我们许多人来说，正是通过自己的工作，我们才得以定义自我。

en: 'Without my job I don't know who I am,' is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. (27 words)
cn: “如果没有了这份工作，我都不知道自己是谁了”——这句话，我在自己的诊室里，已经不止一次听来访者说起过。

en: Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. (25 words)
cn: 事实上，对于那些失去工作、或被迫更换工作的来访者，这往往是我在陪伴他们时最棘手的议题之一。

en: This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. (15 words)
cn: 这种失去所引发的身份危机，其严重程度，远远超过了失去这份工作本身。

en: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. (24 words)
cn: 然而，我逐渐领悟到的一点是，我们的身份认同，远比乍看之下要复杂得多。

en: If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. (40 words)
cn: 如果我们愿意花时间静下心来反思，就会发现，除了工作身份之外，我们同样可以将自己定义为朋友、配偶、子女、父母，或是某支运动队、某个宗教团体中的一员。

en: We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. (19 words)
cn: 我们或许会意识到，在这些不同的角色和关系中，自己的感受和行为方式，与在职场中截然不同。

en: The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. (9 words)
cn: 那个在家中总是被动顺从的女儿，到了职场上，或许会摇身一变，成为一位果断有力的领导者。

en: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. (8 words)
cn: 此外，我们在职场中的身份，也并非一成不变。

en: They change over time. (4 words)
cn: 它们会随着时间的推移而不断演变。

en: I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. (17 words)
cn: 就拿我自己来说，我曾做过店员、女服务员、学生、应届毕业生，如今则是一名临床心理学家。

en: At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. (19 words)
cn: 在每一个人生阶段，我能否成功适应并发展出与之相符的职业身份，都对我的身心健康至关重要。

en: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market. (25 words)
cn: 尽管我们都希望能在某种程度上消除生活中的不确定性，但我们终究还是必须学会与不确定性共处，尤其是在当今这样一个瞬息万变的就业市场之中。

en: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. (12 words)
cn: 我们如何看待自己，是身份认同问题的核心所在。

en: When we tell ourselves 'I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through' it can become part of our belief system. (25 words)
cn: 当我们对自己说“我擅长启动一个项目，却不太擅长把它坚持完成”时，这句话便可能逐渐内化为我们信念体系的一部分。

en: But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. (27 words)
cn: 但如果你不幸经历了一次被迫的职业变动，你就有必要去审视这些信念，看看它们究竟在多大程度上是站得住脚的。

en: You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. (16 words)
cn: 你需要问问自己，这些信念对你究竟有多大帮助，并认真考虑做出个人层面的改变。

en: We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. (18 words)
cn: 通过不断尝试、反复练习，以及有意识的自我约束，我们可以在人生的任何阶段，改变自己的信念、行为方式以及情感体验。

en: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. (50 words)
cn: 在这样一个职业发展可能把我们带入全新领域的时代，去质疑自己既有的自我认知、并探索能否通过改变自己对自身的信念来重塑身份体验，从而拓展自己的职业选择，就显得愈发重要。

en: Ultimately it is you who define who you are. (9 words)
cn: 说到底，真正定义“你是谁”的人，只有你自己。

en: You are only your job if you let it be so. (11 words)
cn: 只有当你自己允许它如此时，你才等同于你的工作。

en: With the rapid progress in the economy, it is natural that people's ideology is bound for change. (17 words)
cn: 随着经济的快速发展，人们的观念注定会发生变化，这是很自然的事情。

en: Being thrifty is no longer a virtue to some people, and they are not alone in holding this view. (19 words)
cn: 对一些人来说，节俭已不再是一种美德，而且持这种看法的人不止他们一个。

en: Each might have different viewpoints on how to lead one's lifestyle: some prefer simplicity, some love luxuries, some spend extravagantly, some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse. (31 words)
cn: 每个人对该如何过自己的生活方式，可能都有不同的看法：有人偏爱简朴，有人钟情奢华，有人挥金如土，也有人像乡下老鼠那样，尽可能多地囤积财富。

en: As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its appeal to me, but as my station changes, I have an opportunity to mingle with the newly rich, an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle. (43 words)
cn: 由于我出身贫寒、又生长在农村，简朴的乡村生活对我来说，几乎从未失去过它的吸引力；但随着我社会地位的变化，我有机会与新贵们打成一片，这段经历彻底颠覆了我对生活方式的看法。

en: It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much, an idea only recently being revealed to me. (20 words)
cn: 花得少、攒得多是一种罪恶或邪恶的行为——这个观点，是我最近才意识到的。

en: Actually the whole world is in a rage to borrow and to spend, with the USA leading the trend. (19 words)
cn: 事实上，整个世界都陷入了一股借贷消费的狂热之中，而美国正是引领这一潮流的国家。

en: The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world, but the irony is that they borrow money from us. (23 words)
cn: 美国依然是世界上最富有、最强大的国家，但颇具讽刺意味的是，他们却在向我们借钱。

en: Though a layman of economics, at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into the predator rather than the decent and kind lender. (28 words)
cn: 尽管我只是个经济学的门外汉，但至少我明白，用借来的钱去投资，会让借款人变成“掠食者”，而不是那位正派、善良的出借人。

en: An apparent case is real estate. (6 words)
cn: 房地产就是一个显而易见的例子。

en: Those who are shrewd and have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. (25 words)
cn: 那些精明地从银行贷到款的人，通过以高出购入价好几倍的价格出售自己购置的房产，相对而言变得富有起来。

en: Even education is not immune from this theory. (8 words)
cn: 就连教育也无法幸免于这一理论。

en: Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this investment, even though they have to scrape a living. (28 words)
cn: 许多有远见、送孩子上大学的贫困父母，都从这项投资中获益，尽管他们自己不得不省吃俭用、艰难度日。

en: It is reasonable to conclude that spending is praiseworthy, supposing it is not beyond your means. (16 words)
cn: 由此可以合理地得出结论：只要不超出自己的经济能力，消费就是一件值得称道的事情。

en: On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles (腌菜) and salads. (33 words)
cn: 在马六甲海峡附近的一座小型果园里，林国安只剩下一棵种植“九王果”的树——这是一种口感爽脆、味道酸涩的浆果，马来西亚人多用它来腌制泡菜和拌沙拉。

en: "It's not very well-known," says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan (龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. (20 words)
cn: 这位45岁的果农说：“这种果子不太出名。”他如今转而专注于种植市场更大的龙眼和菠萝。

en: "We have to grow what is profitable," he says. (9 words)
cn: 他说：“我们必须种植能赚钱的作物。”

en: But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. (24 words)
cn: 但在不到一小时车程之外的马来西亚乡间，三座巨大的银色穹顶建筑内，科学家们正努力改变食品的未来。

en: They're pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called 'alternative' crops—such as kedondong. (17 words)
cn: 他们正在通过种植和加工所谓的“替代”作物——比如九王果——来拓展人类饮食的边界。

en: At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. (34 words)
cn: 在全球研究中心“未来作物”（CFF）的总部，这种被大大低估的水果，已被加工成一款无糖果汁，富含维生素C，在感官评测中获得了极高的评分。

en: "Anything you see here is a forgotten crop," says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur. (26 words)
cn: 赛义德·阿扎姆－阿里指着穿插在CFF位于马来西亚首都吉隆坡郊外的花园中随处可见的各种植物说：“你在这里看到的任何一种作物，都是一种被遗忘的作物。”

en: Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. (17 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里教授解释道，仅仅四种作物——小麦、玉米、水稻和大豆——就提供了全世界三分之二的粮食供应。

en: "We're dependent on these four," he says. (7 words)
cn: 他说：“我们依赖着这四种作物。”

en: "But actually there's 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." (17 words)
cn: “但事实上，还有7000种我们已经种植了数千年的作物，我们却将它们全都忽视了。”

en: Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops—plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or 'alternative' as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops. (34 words)
cn: 研究人员正试图挖掘这些被忽视的作物的潜力——他们将这些植物称为“被遗忘的”“未被充分利用的”或“替代性”作物，因为它们正被由主要作物加工成分推动的、日益趋同的饮食结构所取代。

en: It's a timely quest. (4 words)
cn: 这是一项适逢其时的探索。

en: The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. (15 words)
cn: 食品行业目前已经占到了全球温室气体排放量的近三分之一。

en: By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. (20 words)
cn: 据估计，到2050年，为了养活预计将达到100亿的全球人口，世界必须多生产50%的粮食。

en: Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions. (12 words)
cn: 要在不加剧气候变化的前提下满足这一需求，亟需找到解决方案。

en: Forgotten crops hold key answers. (5 words)
cn: 被遗忘的作物，掌握着关键的答案。

en: By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. (19 words)
cn: 通过对本地被忽视的植物进行投资，各国可以减少对进口作物及其高碳供应链的依赖。

en: Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. (21 words)
cn: 在气候变暖威胁着现有作物的当下，重新引入人类曾经食用过的多种作物，也有助于提升粮食安全。

en: On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient (气候韧性较强的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. (15 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里还指出，被遗忘的作物往往也是气候韧性最强、营养价值最高的作物之一。

en: His summary is plain: "Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity." (13 words)
cn: 他的总结简明扼要：“饮食多样化，对人类的未来至关重要。”

en: Food security experts agree. (4 words)
cn: 粮食安全专家们对此表示认同。

en: "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. (31 words)
cn: 新加坡国立大学水政策研究所高级研究员塞西莉亚·托尔塔哈达说：“这个世界上不存在真正的粮食不安全，只存在对粮食的无知。”

en: "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds. (21 words)
cn: 她补充道：“每当我们拥有本地作物时，我们总倾向于忽视它们，仿佛它们毫无价值——但事实并非如此。”

en: Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. (5 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里对这种怀疑态度有着切身的体会。

en: He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. (18 words)
cn: 早在20世纪80年代，他就通过在尼日尔结识的女农民们所从事的工作，接触到了替代性作物。

en: The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. (27 words)
cn: 当时还是博士生的他回忆道，自己曾对这些女农民在没有任何技术支持的情况下、在自家后院种植的作物赞叹不已——每当主要作物歉收时，正是这些作物养活了她们的家人。

en: He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. (10 words)
cn: 他从中看到了构建替代性食品体系的巨大机遇。

en: But "the resistance was enormous," he recalls. (7 words)
cn: 但他回忆道：“当时遭遇的阻力是巨大的。”

en: Undeterred, he ploughed on. (4 words)
cn: 没有被吓退，他继续坚持推进这项事业。

en: Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. (18 words)
cn: 一个又一个项目，逐渐证明了这些作物在不同环境下作为主要作物替代品的可行性。

en: But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. (11 words)
cn: 但这些作物能否具备市场竞争力，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

en: "That's the critical thing," he says. (6 words)
cn: 他说：“这才是关键所在。”

en: In one of the centre's domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa (辣木) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten (麸质) and higher in nutrients. (31 words)
cn: 在该中心的其中一座穹顶建筑内，食品技术专家陈欣琳用辣木叶粉替代部分小麦粉，烘焙出一款麸质含量更低、营养更丰富的蛋糕。

en: Tan's job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. (19 words)
cn: 陈欣琳的工作，是用这些人们仍不太熟悉的食材，研发出既能吸引本地口味、也能吸引国际口味的食谱。

en: In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. (29 words)
cn: 近年来，她利用CFF种植的一些被遗忘的作物——比如辣木和班巴拉花生——制作出了从速食汤到印度小吃在内的各式食品。

en: "I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes," says Tan, who is also a trained chef. (19 words)
cn: 身兼受过专业训练的厨师身份的陈欣琳说：“我努力对这些被遗忘的作物进行现代化改造，而不是照搬老旧的食谱。”

en: It's a strategy to appeal to the world's growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. (22 words)
cn: 这是一种策略，旨在吸引那些日益转向快餐和加工食品行业的、正在不断壮大的全球中产阶级。

en: It's also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as "old or poor people's food" or as inferior "women's crops", adds Tan. (24 words)
cn: 陈欣琳补充道，这也是一种有助于扭转人们对本地作物的看法的方式——不再将它们视为“老年人或穷人的食物”，或是低人一等的“女人的作物”。

en: The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. (11 words)
cn: 人们对本地食物的这些负面观念，其根源可能相当深远。

en: The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. (26 words)
cn: 班巴拉花生是撒哈拉以南非洲一种富含蛋白质的本地作物，在东南亚部分地区也有种植，它被边缘化的根源，可以追溯到殖民统治时期。

en: "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. (14 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里说：“种植班巴拉花生的非洲女性，实际上曾因种植这种作物而受到惩罚。”

en: "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." (18 words)
cn: “殖民统治者宣称，你们不能种这个，因为它没有油脂可榨，我们也找不到市场来销售它。”

en: But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. (33 words)
cn: 但如今，班巴拉“murukku”（一种油炸小吃）已成为CFF评价最好的食品之一，他们的目标是让它进驻各大超市，并向潜在投资者列举藜麦等作物的成功案例，作为有力的佐证。

en: Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. (17 words)
cn: 大约30年前，藜麦除了在其原产地玻利维亚和秘鲁的山区之外，几乎无人知晓。

en: Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world. (15 words)
cn: 如今，这种富有营养的谷物，已经出现在世界各地高档餐厅的菜单上。

en: Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. (16 words)
cn: 以营养而非产量来衡量作物价值，正是“被遗忘食物”这项事业的核心所在。

en: Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. (14 words)
cn: 自20世纪60年代的“绿色革命”以来，高产作物就一直主导着现代农业。

en: That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. (22 words)
cn: 在当年那个世界迫切需要增加粮食供应的年代，这在一定程度上是应对毁灭性饥荒的关键举措。

en: Today "nutrition is becoming a time bomb", says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. (19 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里说，如今，随着二氧化碳浓度不断上升、导致作物矿物质流失，“营养问题正在成为一颗定时炸弹”。

en: Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts. (20 words)
cn: 他主张，与其对主要作物进行生物强化，不如把投资投向那些本身就更具营养价值、却已被遗忘的作物。

en: In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre's "crown jewels", revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. (30 words)
cn: 在CFF第三座穹顶建筑的深处，实验室经理戈马蒂·塞图拉曼打开了一扇窗，让人得以一窥该中心的“镇馆之宝”——只见在明亮的黄色灯光下，四棱豆的藤蔓正茁壮生长。

en: It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. (25 words)
cn: 这是科学家们研究更高温度和二氧化碳浓度对替代作物营养成分影响的多个实验舱之一。

en: This research is "the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that 'future crops' are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates. (20 words)
cn: 阿扎姆－阿里说，这项研究是“真正的游戏规则改变者”，它将确保“未来作物”在气候变暖的环境下，同样也是最健康的作物。

en: There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. (20 words)
cn: 美国智库“食物坦克”（Food Tank）的主席丹尼尔·尼伦伯格表示，围绕“被遗忘的食物”，一股日益增长的全球性势头正在形成。

en: Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. (34 words)
cn: 除了自称是全球首个专门致力于未被充分利用作物研究的CFF之外，还有其他一些重要机构也在倡导农业多样性，包括“作物信托”（Crop Trust）、“慢食运动”（Slow Food）、国际半干旱热带作物研究所（Icrisat）以及“生物多样性国际组织”（Bioversity International）。

en: Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says. (24 words)
cn: 她还提到，与此同时，越来越多的中等收入消费者正在寻找富有营养的食物，还有一些人则渴望尝试祖辈曾经食用过的那些未加工食品。

en: But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others. (28 words)
cn: 但在某些地区人们对“被遗忘的食物”兴趣渐增的同时，在另一些地区，这种兴趣却被富含糖分、脂肪和加工食品的西式饮食的全球蔓延所压过。

en: A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is "the obsession with imported products", says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. (36 words)
cn: 以马来西亚为例，推广日渐式微的本地作物所面临的一大关键障碍，是“人们对进口产品的痴迷”——这是Sitka餐厅联合创始人詹妮弗·关的说法，该餐厅位于吉隆坡一处富裕郊区，致力于推广本地食材。

en: Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a "status symbol", she says. (24 words)
cn: 她说，Sitka被视为马来西亚小型“从农场到餐桌”餐饮潮流的先驱，但即便如此，该餐厅的顾客仍然把追求进口食材，当作一种“身份的象征”。

en: The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. (7 words)
cn: 支持“被遗忘的食物”这一主张，让人觉得颇为直观、合乎情理。

en: Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. (8 words)
cn: 一些分析人士则表示，这事实上是不可避免的。

en: "Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change," says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City University of London. (28 words)
cn: 伦敦城市大学食品政策学教授蒂姆·朗说：“气候变化几乎可以肯定地意味着，人们的口味将被迫发生改变。”

en: We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says. (17 words)
cn: 他说，随着主要粮食作物产量的下降，我们“必须逐渐习惯食用其他作物”。

en: Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. (17 words)
cn: 想象一下，你是一个被派往地球、负责记录这颗星球上哺乳动物行为的外星人。

en: You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film. (13 words)
cn: 你误打误撞地走进了一家正在放映好莱坞最新恐怖电影的影院。

en: Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. (11 words)
cn: 几十个人聚集在一间黑暗、没有任何装饰的房间里。

en: They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly. (14 words)
cn: 他们全都盯着一块矩形区域，那上面的光影图案正在飞速变化。

en: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. (9 words)
cn: 他们显然处于一种高度亢奋的状态。

en: Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls. (23 words)
cn: 他们的心率有所加快，时不时紧张地环顾四周，还会时而在座位上集体惊跳起来，并发出高亢的警示叫声。

en: Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. (11 words)
cn: 最终，灯光亮起，那块矩形屏幕也随之熄灭。

en: The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure. (16 words)
cn: 这些人站起身，边聊天边说笑地离开了房间，脸上流露出愉悦的神情。

en: Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? (16 words)
cn: 为什么这些人类要自愿让自己经历这种看似极度令人不快的体验呢？

en: And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen? (15 words)
cn: 他们又为何会对屏幕上那些光影图案，产生如此强烈的反应呢？

en: I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment. (17 words)
cn: 我一直对“恐怖的悖论”着迷不已——即许多人竟主动去寻求令人恐惧的娱乐体验，这一奇特的事实。

en: I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature. (11 words)
cn: 我认为，这个谜题的答案就藏在人性之中。

en: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. (23 words)
cn: 我的研究表明，人类在进化过程中，逐渐学会了从那些能让我们在安全环境下体验负面情绪的情境中获得愉悦感。

en: You can see these elements of horror in Children's games. (10 words)
cn: 在儿童游戏中，你就能看到这些恐怖元素的影子。

en: Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. (12 words)
cn: 以捉迷藏为例，这其实是一种对捕食者与猎物互动关系的模拟。

en: The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast. (21 words)
cn: 孩子躲藏起来，成年人则假扮成捕食者，一边像危险的野兽那样吼叫，一边寻找孩子。

en: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario. (37 words)
cn: 这种模拟为孩子提供了关于如何避免沦为猎物的关键信息，孩子们往往会觉得这类活动令他们深感满足，这大概是因为，它让他们得以在安全的环境中，体验一种潜在的灾难性情境。

en: They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour. (15 words)
cn: 他们从中感受到愉悦，而愉悦感正是进化用来激励我们做出适应性行为的方式。

en: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. (18 words)
cn: 恐怖之所以能给许多人带来愉悦感，是因为它让我们得以“把玩”负面情绪，并发展出应对这些情绪的策略。

en: We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion. (18 words)
cn: 我们由此学会了真正恐惧的感觉是什么样的，也学会了该如何应对负面情绪。

en: How, then, does horror work? (5 words)
cn: 那么，恐怖究竟是如何发挥作用的呢？

en: My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. (24 words)
cn: 我的研究表明，恐怖的运作机制，是利用了一整套古老的生物防御机制——一种经过进化而来的恐惧系统，这一系统是我们与其他动物所共有的。

en: But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger. (21 words)
cn: 但人类拥有独一无二的想象力，我们利用这种进化而来的想象力，去“游历”那些充满危险的虚拟世界。

en: There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. (17 words)
cn: 即便你并非恐怖片的忠实粉丝，观看恐怖电影也确实有其充分的理由。

en: If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. (31 words)
cn: 如果你能完整地看完整部电影而毫发无损，你很可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感——一种自己成功挺过了一段极其可怕的经历的感觉。

en: Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant? (22 words)
cn: 不管怎样，观看恐怖电影能让你更擅长应对自己的恐惧，而谁又知道，这种能力何时会在关键时刻真正派上用场呢？

en: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. (22 words)
cn: 在现实世界中，一场针对多年来被强加给我们的审美模式的觉醒运动，正在悄然兴起。

en: But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful. (12 words)
cn: 但在数字领域，社交媒体却决定着什么才算是美的。

en: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. (9 words)
cn: 这两场方向相反的斗争，正在同步展开。

en: In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. (21 words)
cn: 在现实世界中，这场斗争所对抗的，是强加在女性身上、要求她们迎合一种不切实际的审美理想的内在压力。

en: As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. (19 words)
cn: 作为这场斗争的一部分，多家媒体开始呈现那些身材并不符合所谓“理想标准”的女性形象。

en: All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate." (22 words)
cn: 所有那些此前一直被排除在杂志封面、电视剧和公共议程之外的女性，如今都获得了“正当性”。

en: At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws. (29 words)
cn: 与此同时，一批网络红人也开始在社交媒体上上传自己素颜的照片，甚至是刻意突出所谓“缺陷”的照片。

en: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. (18 words)
cn: 科技已经重塑了我们的审美理想，并且十分有效地将这一信息传递给了大众。

en: One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look," which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050. (25 words)
cn: 过去十年留下的一项奇特“遗产”，便是“赛博格容貌”的流行，它描绘出美国人在2050年可能呈现的容貌样貌。

en: The cyborg look spread rapidly. (5 words)
cn: “赛博格容貌”曾迅速走红、广泛传播。

en: Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal. (11 words)
cn: 但如今，“Instagram脸”已经取而代之，成为新的审美理想。

en: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. (19 words)
cn: 当学习过程中存在主动参与时，人们对既定审美规范的内化会变得更加有效。

en: The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified (游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share. (25 words)
cn: 用户的这种主动参与，体现在社交媒体平台所提供的游戏化互动之中——点赞、发表评论、进行比较、分享内容的种种功能，皆是如此。

en: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background. (36 words)
cn: 一旦这种理想化的审美标准被内化，用户就会获得各种工具或功能，来改变自己的外貌以迎合这一被广泛接受的审美理想——比如修图、选择理想的滤镜、搭配合适的背景等等。

en: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. (18 words)
cn: 一项在美国开展的调查显示，超过50%的人在发布照片之前，都会先对图片进行滤镜处理。

en: And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. (15 words)
cn: 而你听到这其中大多数人都是女性，想必也不会感到意外。

en: One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side. (35 words)
cn: 过度沉迷于滤镜处理所带来的一项重大后果，便是一种正在兴起的倾向：人们开始像旁观者那样审视和评判自己，把自己当作一件供人观察和评估价值的物品来看待。

en: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. (11 words)
cn: 滤镜所产生的影响，早已远远超出了单纯的娱乐消遣范畴。

en: The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. (17 words)
cn: 滤镜以及网络上进行的整套“游戏”，都在影响着用户的心理健康。

en: According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines. (26 words)
cn: 一项研究显示，Instagram、Snapchat和FaceTune等应用程序，让用户得以达到此前只有在美容杂志上才能见到的那种完美程度。

en: Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. (20 words)
cn: 尽管人类向来珍视美，但在过去十年间，我们对外貌的痴迷，已经达到了前所未有的顶峰。

en: The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care. (33 words)
cn: 在社交媒体上耗费的时间，会催生出一种想要实现根本不可能实现的完美容貌的冲动，而这种冲动是如此强烈，以至于唯一能够真正解决它的，并非美容整形手段，而是心理健康层面的干预。

en: Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? (19 words)
cn: 你是否曾与自己在乎的人谈论重要的事情，却发现谈话令人沮丧而非富有成效？

en: Negative energy can then cast a shadow (Q26: L) over your efforts to build a shared understanding. (17 words)
cn: 负面情绪随后可能会为你们建立共识的努力蒙上一层阴影。

en: In fact, collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. (7 words)
cn: 事实上，协作式解决问题的对话是需要技巧的。

en: Strong listening skills are essential. (5 words)
cn: 良好的倾听能力至关重要。

en: Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, affectionate (Q27: A) smiles, and warm comments helps. (13 words)
cn: 通过表达欣赏、报以亲切的微笑和温暖的话语来注入积极情绪，会很有帮助。

en: So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. (14 words)
cn: 将自己的情绪基调保持在平和区间的能力，同样至关重要。

en: If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue flips (Q28: F) from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate halt (Q29: G). (32 words)
cn: 如果对话的语气变得激烈、怒火爆发，对话就会从协作型瞬间转变为对抗型，进展也很可能随即戛然而止。

en: In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry. (10 words)
cn: 此外，有效的对话通常还具备另一个重要特征：对称性。

en: Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. (13 words)
cn: 对话中的对称性，指的是双方发言量之间的平衡。

en: Are you each getting equal airtime? (6 words)
cn: 你们双方获得的“发言时间”是否对等？

en: When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to become annoying to one or both of you. (24 words)
cn: 当一方说得多，这种不对称或失衡往往会让一方或双方都感到厌烦。

en: The silent partner typically (Q30: N) tires of only listening, while the talker can feel overburdened (Q31: H). (18 words)
cn: 沉默的一方通常会厌倦只能一味倾听，而说话的一方则可能感到不堪重负。

en: Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take. (9 words)
cn: 通常，双方都更愿意有更均等的交流与回应。

en: Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can erode (Q32: D) symmetry as well. (16 words)
cn: 说话速度和音量的高低差异，同样也会削弱对话的对称性。

en: The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. (12 words)
cn: 语速更快或声音更大的一方，很容易开始占据更多的发言时间。

en: The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor. (11 words)
cn: 语速较慢或声音较轻的一方，则可能难以获得发言的机会。

en: Conversations also lose balance when one partner's opinions count more than the other's. (13 words)
cn: 当一方的观点比另一方的观点更受重视时，对话也会失去平衡。

en: One person's input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more vigorous (Q33: O). (17 words)
cn: 一个人的意见之所以更具分量，可能是因为其表达方式更为强势有力。

en: One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more tentatively (Q34: M). (15 words)
cn: 而另一种观点则可能因为表达得更为试探、犹豫，而容易被忽视。

en: If either partner fairly consistently predominates (Q35: I) or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. (16 words)
cn: 如果任何一方总是相当稳定地占据主导，或者总是趋于消失，那么调整这种模式将大有帮助。

en: The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive. (20 words)
cn: 这样一来，对话会让人感觉更富成效，同时整体关系也更可能让人感觉更加积极。

en: A) Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. (6 words)
cn: A) 蓝月亮、玫瑰月亮、超级月亮。

en: For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. (18 words)
cn: 不知为何，各大网站似乎都认定你非常想要了解关于这些月亮的一切。

en: "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. (9 words)
cn: “快来看本周末这场惊艳的超级月亮！”一则标题这样宣称。

en: "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain. (15 words)
cn: “超级月亮其实没什么大不了的，你们都在毁掉天文学。”另一则标题则如此抱怨。

en: B) The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse, which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur in January. (44 words)
cn: B) 最近的一个例子，就是“超级血狼月”月食——这名字听起来就像是我上九年级时会为之编排一支充满深情的现代舞的歌曲名，但实际上，它是一桩预计将在一月发生的天文事件。

en: As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. (33 words)
cn: 正如我们下文将要解释的那样，这次月亮其实并没有什么真正神秘或特别之处，它在天空中也不会像血淋淋的狼头，或是任何类似的诡异景象。

en: We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic. (38 words)
cn: 之所以会出现这些“超级”月亮事件，是因为我们把历史上用来标记全年满月的各种修饰语一股脑地叠加在了一起，而在互联网时代，我们有时未免会为此过度兴奋。

en: C) Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. (10 words)
cn: C) 不妨把这篇文章当作你了解一切赏月资讯的首选指南。

en: Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event. (11 words)
cn: 以下就是你需要了解的、关于这次最新天文事件的信息。

en: D) Look, it's okay if you don't know. (8 words)
cn: D) 说实话，不知道也没关系。

en: There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not. (33 words)
cn: 或许有大批人整天装作对天上那玩意儿为何会按一定周期忽大忽小了如指掌，但实际上他们根本一无所知。

en: E) The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. (25 words)
cn: E) 月球绕地球运行，并且处于潮汐锁定状态——这意味着它始终以同一面朝向我们，而不像我们所在的地球那样自转。

en: That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. (26 words)
cn: 这也是为什么，即便月球绕着我们旋转，你也总能看到“月亮上的人影”（或者依你的文化偏好，也可以说是“月亮上的兔子”）。

en: But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. (23 words)
cn: 但当月亮满月、在天空中又大又亮时，那只是因为它反射了太阳的光。

en: But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. (15 words)
cn: 不过月亮始终处于运动之中，因此它被阳光照射的角度也在不断变化。

en: It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. (41 words)
cn: 新月时我们看不见月亮，是因为月球恰好位于我们和太阳之间；所谓的月球“黑暗面”其实亮如拉斯维加斯的灯火，而我们能看到的那一面，却正处于阴影之中。

en: A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. (23 words)
cn: 满月出现时，地球恰好位于太阳和月球之间，因此阳光正好照亮了我们能看到的那一面。

en: And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other. (17 words)
cn: 而其余所有的月相，不过是这两个极端状态之间的过渡而已。

en: F) The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. (17 words)
cn: F) 月球与地球之间的距离并非始终恒定，因为它的运行轨道并非一个完美的正圆。

en: We call the closest point perigee (近地点), and the most distant point is apogee (远地点). (15 words)
cn: 我们把距离地球最近的点称为“近地点”，最远的点称为“远地点”。

en: 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles. (18 words)
cn: 2018年最近的近地点和最远的远地点恰好都出现在一月，两者之间的距离差约为3万英里。

en: G) The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. (18 words)
cn: G) 你之所以需要关心这一距离上的寻常变化，是因为正是它，让一轮月亮变成了“超级月亮”。

en: When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. (15 words)
cn: 当满月出现的时间接近近地点时，月亮看起来就会稍微大一些。

en: Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. (32 words)
cn: 老实说，这种差异其实并不算特别显著，但如果你能把超级月亮和某个可以体现出这种“略微增大”的参照物一同拍摄下来，效果看起来还是相当酷炫的。

en: January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over. (48 words)
cn: 一月的“超级血狼月”月食之所以“超级”，是因为它发生的日期恰好与月球在一月最接近我们的时刻重合；不过，月球在全年中真正距离我们最近的时刻，其实要等到二月的超级月亮才会出现——到时候，想必又会引来一番不必要的过度兴奋。

en: H) Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). (21 words)
cn: H) “血月”只会在月全食期间出现（对于任何一个特定地点而言，这种现象一年中都可能发生数次）。

en: When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. (13 words)
cn: 当月亮悄然滑入地球的阴影之中时，我们便赋予了它一层泛红的色泽。

en: The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. (40 words)
cn: 月亮在升起或落下时，也可能会呈现出橙色，如果它整夜都低悬在地平线附近，也会是这样——因为它反射的光线在那个位置需要穿过更厚的大气层，从而散射掉更多的蓝光。

en: But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse. (12 words)
cn: 但那种深沉而略带诡异的红色，你大概只有在月食期间才能看到。

en: I) A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods. (70 words)
cn: I) 很多关于月亮的新闻标题实在有些荒谬（比如你完全没必要对“蓝月亮”特别激动，它看起来其实和普通满月没什么两样），但如果你所在的地区能够看到血月，那你倒是真该从床上爬起来看一看——尽管它们说到底不过是月食现象，绝非什么天神之间血腥战斗的证据。

en: J) In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. (17 words)
cn: J) 2018年3月，我们迎来了当年的第二次“蓝月亮”，一时广受赞誉。

en: And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. (49 words)
cn: 虽然这种现象算不上那种“哇快出去看啊”式的特别，但它确实有其特别之处：所谓“蓝月亮”，指的是同一个日历月份内出现两次满月的现象，而自1999年以来，我们此前一直未曾在同一年里出现过两次“蓝月亮”，下一次要等到2037年才会再次发生。

en: Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. (41 words)
cn: 天文学家戴维·查普曼解释道，这其实只是我们历法体系中的一个特殊现象；自从人类不再按照月亮的周期、转而依照太阳和四季来安排事务以来，我们便不再拥有“每月固定出现一次满月”这种规律了。

en: The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. (27 words)
cn: 月相周期平均为29.53天，因此在大多数月份里，我们通常还是只会出现一次新月和一次满月。

en: But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. (14 words)
cn: 但偶尔也会出现某个月份“偷走”了另一个月份满月的情况。

en: In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark. (30 words)
cn: 在2018年（以及1999年，还有即将到来的2037年），一月和三月都恰好在月初和月末各出现了一次满月，唯独把二月晾在了一边，没有满月。

en: K) Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. (18 words)
cn: K) 一年中出现两次“蓝月亮”实属罕见，但每隔几年，我们还是会遇到一次单独的“蓝月亮”。

en: Also, fun fact: not actually blue. (6 words)
cn: 另外说个有趣的事实：它其实并不是真的蓝色。

en: A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue." (36 words)
cn: 月亮确实可能会呈现出一种略带忧郁感的蓝色，但这种情况，只有在大小恰到好处的微粒弥漫在空气中时才会发生——这与月亮是否属于所谓的“蓝月亮”毫无关系。

en: Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once. (35 words)
cn: 火山喷发或大火产生的大片烟灰云，倒是能造成这种效果，但这种情况并不常见，而要让这两种罕见现象同时发生，可以说是真的需要“天时地利”齐聚才行。

en: L) You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. (19 words)
cn: L) 你或许曾听说过，2018年那次格外特别的第二次“蓝月亮”，同时也是一次“逾越节月”。

en: This is true! (3 words)
cn: 这是真的！

en: That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. (22 words)
cn: 这只是意味着，它是春季的第一次满月，而这一满月常被用来确定复活节星期日的具体日期。

en: All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further. (15 words)
cn: 不过这一切说到底都只是历法上的琐碎讲究，我们不打算在此深入展开。

en: M) Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. (19 words)
cn: M) 有时候，你会看到某个标题堆砌了一大堆形容月亮的修饰语，多到让人头晕目眩。

en: A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? (13 words)
cn: 什么“超级蓝血虫月”，又或者是“超级血狼月”？

en: Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the U.S. alone today, not to mention historically. (51 words)
cn: 不少网站会告诉你，“狼月”是“美洲原住民”文化中对一年首次满月的传统称呼，但这种说法其实颇为奇怪——因为仅在今天的美国，就登记在册着573个部落联盟，更不用说历史上曾存在过的更多部落了。

en: The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical. (34 words)
cn: 认为饥饿嚎叫的狼群，在一月是如此普遍的存在，以至于整个北美——无论文化、地理还是语言各不相同——竟会不约而同地想出同一个昵称，这种说法本身就并不合乎逻辑。

en: N) Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. (40 words)
cn: N) 许多文化都有自己对某个特定月份或季节满月的传统称呼，因此，如果你想为一次只是稍微比平常大那么一点点的月亮，编出一个更加吸引眼球的故事，倒确实有不少现成的名字可供选用。

en: But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so. (30 words)
cn: 但这些名称说到底都是基于人类的历法、生活习俗和民间传说而来的；即便到了四月，你走出门外，也并不会看到一轮真正的粉色月亮——尽管我倒是挺希望它是真的。

en: With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside. (26 words)
cn: 随着人口不断增长、全球城市化进程持续加速，人们的大量关注都聚焦在了城市的可持续发展上，而乡村地区所获得的关注却少之又少。

en: Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. (15 words)
cn: 乡村生活总是与紧密联结的社区、归属感以及简单宁静的生活方式联系在一起。

en: Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. (21 words)
cn: 然而，尽管乡村确实具备部分甚至全部这些特质，保守观念和就业机会匮乏的问题同样也存在于乡村之中。

en: And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. (13 words)
cn: 而正是由于后者，乡村社区才正在遭受着困境。

en: Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation. (30 words)
cn: 受到城市地区经济条件不断改善的吸引，世界各地的乡村居民纷纷外迁，这一方面加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，另一方面也让乡村日渐凋敝、走向荒芜。

en: So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes, or should it at all? (16 words)
cn: 那么，在这些变化之中，乡村究竟该如何确保自身得以延续下去，抑或它根本就不该被保留？

en: Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. (23 words)
cn: 由于居所与各类设施之间距离较远，加之公共交通往往时断时续，乡村居民对汽车的依赖程度也更高。

en: Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. (11 words)
cn: 乡村居民维护自己那些大多独门独户的住宅，也需要消耗更多的能源。

en: We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. (20 words)
