cn: 在我看来，无论是选择动物蛋白，还是选择素食，都各有其充分的理由。

en: However, abandoning meat and meat products is not the environmental panacea (万灵药) many would have us believe. (16 words)
cn: 然而，摒弃肉类及其制品，并不是许多人所以为的那种能包治百病的环保灵丹妙药。

en: And if taken to an extreme, it also could have harmful nutritional consequences. (13 words)
cn: 而且，如果走向极端，这样做还可能给营养摄入带来有害的后果。

en: A healthy portion of meat's negative reputation centers on the assertion that livestock is the largest source of greenhouse gases worldwide. (21 words)
cn: 肉类之所以名声不佳，相当大一部分原因，就在于“畜牧业是全球最大的温室气体排放源”这一说法。

en: For example, an analysis published in 2009 by the World Watch Institute based in Washington, D. C. asserted that 51 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions come from rearing and processing livestock. (32 words)
cn: 例如，总部位于华盛顿特区的“世界观察研究所”在2009年发表的一项分析就断言，全球51%的温室气体排放来自牲畜的饲养与加工。

en: According to the U. S. Environmental Protection Agency, the largest sources of U. S. greenhouse gas emissions in 2016 were electricity production (28 percent of total emissions), transportation (28 percent) and industry (22 percent). (34 words)
cn: 根据美国环境保护署的数据，2016年美国温室气体排放的最大来源依次是电力生产（占排放总量的28%）、交通运输（28%）以及工业（22%）。

en: All of agriculture accounted for a total of 9 percent, but all of animal agriculture contributes less than half of this amount, representing 3.9 percent of the total greenhouse emission in the U. S. (34 words)
cn: 整个农业总共占了9%，但其中畜牧业的贡献还不到这一数字的一半，只占美国温室气体排放总量的3.9%。

en: That is very different from claiming that livestock represents as much as or more than transportation. (16 words)
cn: 这与“畜牧业的排放量与交通运输相当、甚至更高”这种说法，相去甚远。

en: Why is there such a misconception? (6 words)
cn: 为什么会存在这样的误解呢？

en: In 2006 the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) published a study titled "Livestock's Long Shadow," which received widespread international attention. (22 words)
cn: 2006年，联合国粮食及农业组织（FAO）发布了一项名为《牲畜的巨大阴影》的研究，该研究引发了国际社会的广泛关注。

en: It stated that livestock produced a staggering 18 percent of the world's greenhouse gas emissions. (15 words)
cn: 该研究称，畜牧业产生了高达全球温室气体排放总量18%这一惊人的比例。

en: The agency drew a startling conclusion that livestock was doing more to harm the climate than all models of transportation combined. (21 words)
cn: 该机构由此得出了一个令人震惊的结论：畜牧业对气候的损害，超过了所有交通运输方式加在一起的总和。

en: This latter claim was wrong, and has since been corrected by Henning Stenfeld, the report's senior author. (17 words)
cn: 但后面这一说法其实是错误的，此后该报告的资深作者亨宁·斯滕菲尔德已对其做出了更正。

en: The problem was that analysts from the FAO used a comprehensive life-cycle assessment to study the climate impact of livestock, but a different method when they analyzed transportation. (28 words)
cn: 问题在于，粮农组织的分析人员在研究畜牧业对气候的影响时，采用的是一种全面的生命周期评估方法，但在分析交通运输时，却采用了另一种不同的方法。

en: For livestock, they considered every factor associated with producing meat. (10 words)
cn: 在评估畜牧业时，他们考虑了与生产肉类相关的每一个因素。

en: This included emissions from fertilizer production, converting land from forests to pastures, growing feed, and direct emissions from animals (manure as well as expelling of gas from the stomach) from birth to death. (33 words)
cn: 这其中包括化肥生产所产生的排放、森林转变为牧场的排放、饲料种植的排放，以及动物从出生到死亡整个过程中的直接排放（既包括粪便，也包括胃部排出的气体）。

en: However, when they looked at transportation's carbon footprint, they ignored impacts on the climate from manufacturing vehicle materials and parts, assembling vehicles and maintaining roads, bridges and airports. (28 words)
cn: 然而，在考察交通运输的碳足迹时，他们却忽略了制造车辆材料与零部件、组装车辆，以及维护道路、桥梁和机场等环节对气候造成的影响。

en: Instead, they only considered the exhaust smoke emitted by finished cars, trucks, trains and planes. (15 words)
cn: 相反，他们只考虑了成品汽车、卡车、火车和飞机所排放的尾气。

en: As a result, the FAO's comparison of greenhouse gas emissions from livestock to those from transportation was greatly distorted. (19 words)
cn: 结果，粮农组织在畜牧业与交通运输温室气体排放量之间所做的对比，出现了严重的失真。

en: I pointed out this flaw during a speech to fellow scientists in San Francisco on March 22, 2010, which led to a flood of media coverage. (26 words)
cn: 2010年3月22日，我在旧金山向同行科学家们发表演讲时指出了这一缺陷，此事随即引发了媒体的大量报道。

en: To its credit, the FAO immediately owned up to its error. (11 words)
cn: 值得肯定的是，粮农组织当即承认了自己的错误。

en: Unfortunately, the agency's initial claim that livestock was responsible for the lion's share of world greenhouse gas emissions had already received wide coverage. (23 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，该机构最初关于“畜牧业是全球温室气体排放最大来源”的说法，早已被广泛传播报道。

en: To this day, we struggle to "unring" the bell. (9 words)
cn: 直到今天，我们仍在努力挽回这一已经造成的负面影响，却收效甚微。

en: In its most recent assessment report, the FAO estimated that livestock produces 14.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. (22 words)
cn: 在最新的评估报告中，粮农组织估计，畜牧业产生的排放，占人类活动所产生全球温室气体排放总量的14.5%。

en: There is no comparable full life-cycle assessment for transportation. (9 words)
cn: 目前尚不存在针对交通运输、可与之相比较的完整生命周期评估。

en: However, as Stenfeld has pointed out, direct emissions from transportation versus livestock can be compared and amount to 14 versus 5 percent, respectively. (23 words)
cn: 不过，正如斯滕菲尔德所指出的那样，交通运输与畜牧业的直接排放量是可以相互比较的，二者分别约占14%和5%。

en: Many people continue to think that avoiding meat as infrequently as once a week will make a significant difference to the climate. (22 words)
cn: 许多人仍然认为，哪怕只是每周有一天不吃肉，也能对气候产生显著的积极影响。

en: But according to one recent study, even if Americans eliminated all animal protein from their diets, they would reduce greenhouse gas emissions by only 2.6 percent. (26 words)
cn: 但根据一项近期的研究，即便美国人从饮食中彻底剔除所有动物蛋白，其温室气体排放量也仅会减少2.6%。

en: According to our research at the University of California, Davis, if the practice of Meatless Monday were to be adopted by all Americans, we'd see a reduction of only 0.5 percent. (31 words)
cn: 根据我们在加州大学戴维斯分校所做的研究，如果全体美国人都践行“无肉星期一”，我们所能看到的减排幅度也仅有0.5%。

en: Moreover, technological, genetic and management changes that have taken place in U. S. agriculture over the past 70 years have made livestock production more efficient and less greenhouse gas-intensive. (29 words)
cn: 此外，过去70年间美国农业在技术、育种和管理方面所发生的种种变革，使得畜牧业生产变得更加高效，温室气体排放强度也随之降低。

en: According to the FAO's statistical database, total direct greenhouse gas emissions from U. S. livestock have declined by 11.3 percent since 1961, while production of livestock meat has more than doubled. (31 words)
cn: 根据粮农组织的统计数据库，自1961年以来，美国畜牧业的直接温室气体排放总量已下降了11.3%，而畜肉产量却增长了一倍以上。

en: Demand for meat is rising in developing and emerging economies, especially in the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia. (20 words)
cn: 在发展中经济体和新兴经济体中，对肉类的需求正在不断增长，尤其是在中东、北非和东南亚地区。

en: For example, raising livestock such as goats in Kenya is an important source of food and income for many small-scale farmers and herders. (23 words)
cn: 例如，在肯尼亚，饲养山羊等牲畜，是许多小农户和牧民重要的食物与收入来源。

en: But meat consumption per person in these regions still lags that of developed countries. (14 words)
cn: 但这些地区的人均肉类消费量，仍然落后于发达国家。

en: In 2015, average annual meat consumption per person in developed countries was 92 kilograms, compared to 24 kilograms in the Middle East and North Africa and 18 kilograms in Southeast Asia. (31 words)
cn: 2015年，发达国家的人均年肉类消费量为92公斤，而中东和北非地区仅为24公斤，东南亚地区更是只有18公斤。

en: Still, given projected population growth in the developing world, there will certainly be an opportunity for countries such as the United States to bring their sustainable livestock rearing practices to the table. (32 words)
cn: 尽管如此，考虑到发展中国家预计将出现的人口增长，像美国这样的国家无疑将迎来一个机会，把自己可持续的畜牧养殖实践带到国际舞台上来。

en: Removing animals from U. S. agriculture would lower national greenhouse gas emissions to a small degree, but it would also make it harder to meet people's nutritional requirements. (28 words)
cn: 将畜牧业从美国农业中剔除，虽能在小幅度上降低全国的温室气体排放，但也会让满足人们的营养需求变得更加困难。

en: Many critics of animal agriculture are quick to point out that if farmers raised only plants, they could produce more pounds of food and more calories per person. (28 words)
cn: 许多批评畜牧业的人往往会迅速指出，如果农民只种植农作物，那么每个人所能生产的食物重量和卡路里都会更多。

en: But humans also need many essential micro- and macro-nutrients for good health. (12 words)
cn: 但人类要维持健康，同样需要许多必不可少的微量与宏量营养素。

en: It's hard to make a compelling argument that the United States has a calorie deficit, given its high national rates of adult and child obesity. (25 words)
cn: 鉴于美国全国成人和儿童的肥胖率都居高不下，很难有说服力地论证美国存在卡路里摄入不足的问题。

en: Moreover, not all plant parts are edible or desirable. (9 words)
cn: 此外，并非所有的植物部位都是可食用的、或是人们所需要的。

en: Raising livestock is a way to add nutritional and economic value to plant agriculture. (14 words)
cn: 饲养牲畜，正是为植物性农业增添营养价值和经济价值的一种方式。

en: As one example, the energy in plants that livestock consume is most often contained in cellulose (纤维素), which is indigestible for humans and many other mammals. (26 words)
cn: 举一个例子：牲畜所摄取的植物中所蕴含的能量，大多储存于纤维素之中，而纤维素是人类以及许多其他哺乳动物都无法消化的。

en: But cows, sheep and other ruminant (反刍的) animals can break cellulose down and release the solar energy contained in this vast resource. (21 words)
cn: 但牛、羊等反刍动物却能够分解纤维素，释放出蕴藏在这一庞大资源中的太阳能。

en: According to the FAO, as much as 70 percent of all agricultural land globally is range land that can only be utilized as grazing land for ruminant livestock. (28 words)
cn: 根据粮农组织的数据，全球所有农业用地中，多达70%属于牧场用地，而这类土地只能被用作反刍牲畜的放牧用地。

en: The world population is currently projected to reach 9.8 billion by 2050. (12 words)
cn: 目前预计，到2050年，世界人口将达到98亿。

en: Feeding this many people will raise immense challenges. (8 words)
cn: 养活如此庞大数量的人口，将带来巨大的挑战。

en: Meat is more calorie-dense per serving than vegetarian options, and ruminant animals largely thrive on feed that is not suitable for humans. (22 words)
cn: 就每份食物所含的卡路里而言，肉类的能量密度要高于素食选项，而反刍动物大多以人类不适宜食用的饲料为生，也能茁壮成长。

en: Raising livestock also offers much-needed income for small-scale farmers in developing nations. (12 words)
cn: 饲养牲畜还为发展中国家的小农户提供了亟需的收入来源。

en: Worldwide, livestock provides a livelihood for 1 billion people. (9 words)
cn: 在全世界范围内，畜牧业为10亿人提供了生计。

en: Climate change demands urgent attention, and the livestock industry has a large overall environmental footprint that affects air, water and land. (21 words)
cn: 气候变化需要我们予以紧急关注，而畜牧业整体上也确实对空气、水资源和土地带来了不小的环境足迹影响。

en: These, combined with a rapidly rising world population, give us plenty of compelling reasons to continue to work for greater efficiencies in animal agriculture. (24 words)
cn: 这些因素，再加上迅速增长的世界人口，都给了我们充分且有说服力的理由，去继续努力提升畜牧业的效率。

en: I believe the place to start is with science-based facts. (10 words)
cn: 我认为，我们应当从基于科学的事实出发，作为这一切努力的起点。

en: Why are we so worried about our careers? (8 words)
cn: 为什么我们会如此担忧自己的职业生涯？

en: Partly it's to do with money, but there's a psychological aspect to our fears as well. (16 words)
cn: 部分原因与金钱有关，但我们的这种恐惧，同样也存在心理层面的因素。

en: We worry because we suspect—not wrongly—that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob. (30 words)
cn: 我们之所以感到担忧，是因为我们怀疑——而且这种怀疑并非毫无道理——这个世界上到处都是一种令人畏惧的人，他们随时准备无情而迅速地对我们做出评判：我们可以把这种人称为“势利眼”。

en: A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve. (29 words)
cn: 所谓“势利眼”，指的就是那种仅凭我们身上相对微小的某一部分，就断然得出结论、判定我们值得他们付出多少关注的人。

en: In the past, that might be your ancestry and royal connections. (11 words)
cn: 在过去，这一部分或许是你的家世出身和与皇室的关系。

en: Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living. (14 words)
cn: 而如今，势利眼所在意的只有一件事：你是靠什么谋生的。

en: This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is 'What do you do?' and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold. (40 words)
cn: 这就解释了，为什么在任何新的社交场合中，我们被问到的第一个问题往往是“你是做什么工作的？”——而根据我们的回答，势利眼要么会以灿烂的笑容欢迎我们，要么会把我们晾在一边、置之不理。

en: And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress. (17 words)
cn: 而这正是我们内心那种迫切渴望取得成就、给人留下深刻印象的冲动被点燃的原因所在。

en: Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this. (15 words)
cn: 有时，我们的这种行为会被误解为贪婪和虚荣，但它的成因远不止于此。

en: A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. (17 words)
cn: 我们对豪华轿车、体面工作和大房子的许多兴趣，其实与物质主义并没有太大关系。

en: It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods. (25 words)
cn: 它与一种对尊重和敬意的渴求有关——而在我们的社会中，这种尊重和敬意，唯有通过获取物质财富才能获得。

en: It isn't the goods themselves we seek, it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them. (20 words)
cn: 我们所追求的并非这些物品本身，而是通过拥有它们所能赢得的那份被爱的感觉。

en: The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn't condemn them for their greed, we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world. (31 words)
cn: 下次当我们看到有人开着法拉利时，不应因其贪婪而加以谴责，而应对他们那种对世界之爱如此强烈的渴求，抱以怜悯之心。

en: At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable. (22 words)
cn: 势利心态的根源，在于人们缺乏想象力，也缺乏足够的自信，去判断这个世界上究竟谁才是真正有价值的人。

en: The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified. (18 words)
cn: 势利眼在如何辨别出色个体这一问题上，其信念既严重误入歧途，又盲目地墨守成规。

en: For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect. (18 words)
cn: 对势利眼来说，唯有那些早已备受赞誉、早已功成名就的人，才值得他们尊重。

en: There is no room in their timid regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good—and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil, and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet. (43 words)
cn: 在他们那胆怯而墨守成规的头脑中，根本容不下这样一种想象：某个人或许聪慧、善良、品行优良——却不知为何被社会彻底忽视了，他们的这些品质隐藏在一层不为人知的面纱之下，至今还没有找到显露自身的明确渠道。

en: The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction. (42 words)
cn: 应对势利心态真正的良方，并不在于宣称世上根本不存在孰优孰劣之分，而在于坚持认为，优劣之别常常存在于意想不到之处，且往往不带有任何外在的、可供辨识的标志。

en: And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path. (32 words)
cn: 而正因为我们如此不擅长判断他人的真正价值，我们最终的责任，仍然是对几乎每一个与我们擦肩而过的人，都保持善意、友善、好奇与丰富的想象力。

en: Women have historically been paid less. (6 words)
cn: 从历史上看，女性的薪酬一直低于男性。

en: But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up—fast. (12 words)
cn: 但在20世纪80年代的美国，这种差距开始迅速缩小。

en: During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year. (15 words)
cn: 在那十年间，性别薪酬差距每年大约缩小一个百分点。

en: Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017. (14 words)
cn: 如果这一趋势持续下去，性别薪酬差距原本会在2017年彻底消失。

en: But the trend didn't continue, and the gap remains yawning. (10 words)
cn: 但这一趋势并没有延续下去，性别薪酬差距至今依然十分悬殊。

en: According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counter intuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies. (28 words)
cn: 根据哈佛大学学者的一项新研究，这种停滞不前的状况，或许有些出人意料地，可以归因于各州及联邦层面家庭休假政策的推行。

en: The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them. (23 words)
cn: 这些学者指出，在20世纪90年代，随着各级政府开始推行休假政策，主要是女性在享受这些政策所带来的便利。

en: Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace—instead of dropping out to have families—those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men. (33 words)
cn: 尽管这些休假政策或许确实帮助这些女性留在了职场——而不是为了生育、组建家庭而彻底退出职场——但那些休假后重返岗位的女性，其薪资增长速度却低于男性。

en: After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since. (30 words)
cn: 事实上，自美国推行家庭休假政策之后，性别薪酬差距的年均收敛速度骤降至仅0.03个百分点，并且此后一直维持在这一水平。

en: Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world. (21 words)
cn: 长期以来，那些追踪职场薪酬平等进程的人士，眼看着这一进程在世界许多国家都逐渐放缓。

en: In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic (大流行病). (11 words)
cn: 事实上，在此次大流行病期间，这一进程甚至开始出现了倒退。

en: The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity (平等), and still exists just about everywhere. (23 words)
cn: 性别薪酬差距，正是这种“不平等”最为突出的例证之一，且如今几乎在世界各地都依然存在。

en: The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years. (28 words)
cn: “母职惩罚”一词，已经成为解释这一现象的简称：在许多地方——尤其是富裕国家——女性在进入育龄阶段之前，薪酬水平与男性是相当的。

en: Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counterparts. (14 words)
cn: 而一旦生育了子女，女性的薪资便开始逐渐落后于男性同事。

en: Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement. (28 words)
cn: 造成这一现象的部分原因，是女性承担了更多家中无偿的劳动，这会侵占她们本可用于工作、以及推进职业发展的时间和精力。

en: But it's also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy. (36 words)
cn: 但这也是因为，身为母亲的女性在加薪和晋升方面往往被忽视，而且即便离开职场的这段时间是自愿选择的、并得到了公司或政府政策的支持，这段“脱离职场”的经历也依然会让女性的职业发展因此受挫、落于人后。

en: What would have happened if leave policies hadn't been introduced? (10 words)
cn: 如果当初没有推行休假政策，情况又会是怎样呢？

en: The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now. (25 words)
cn: 这项研究并未深入探讨这一问题，只是指出，如果20世纪80年代的趋势得以延续，我们如今本应已经实现了薪酬平等。

en: It's possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way. (14 words)
cn: 然而，也有一种可能：无论如何，通往薪酬平等的这条道路，最终都会停滞下来。

en: If women's gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated. (68 words)
cn: 如果说女性在20世纪80年代所取得的进步，是通过消除偏见等相对而言更易被控制的问题而实现的，那么一旦这些问题得到解决，女性仍将面临一个问题——由于哺乳等生理因素，她们是在孩子出生后最初几周里承担生育和照料责任的一方，这就迫使她们不得不休假，无论这些休假是否属于强制性规定。

en: By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. (24 words)
cn: 如今，人们普遍认为，坚持长期规律运动能为人们带来一系列健康益处。

en: But is it ever too late to start? (8 words)
cn: 但开始运动，会不会有为时已晚的时候呢？

en: New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early mortality which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. (45 words)
cn: 一项新研究考察了那些在40多岁以后将运动量提高到超过年轻时水平的人群，结果发现，这些人早逝风险的下降幅度，与那些一生坚持规律运动的人相近。

en: This was a drop of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. (15 words)
cn: 与不运动的人相比，这一风险下降了32%至35%。

en: Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of chronic diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers. (29 words)
cn: 那些在中年才开始运动的人，其心脏病、癌症等慢性疾病的发病率也有所下降，降幅与长期坚持运动者相近。

en: So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? (8 words)
cn: 那么，为什么还要费心坚持一生规律运动呢？

en: The authors of the study concede that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. (29 words)
cn: 该研究的作者承认，有些人可能会把这项研究的结论理解为：自己可以推迟开始运动计划，但这种理解是错误的。

en: There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not disregard. (17 words)
cn: 持续保持运动活跃状态，还有其他一些身心方面的益处，是我们不应忽视的。

en: These real health benefits include better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. (14 words)
cn: 这些切实的健康益处包括更好的认知功能，以及更低的体重增加风险。

en: The latter is particularly important given the global obesity epidemic. (10 words)
cn: 鉴于全球肥胖问题日益严重，后者显得尤为重要。

en: In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those patterns later in life. (33 words)
cn: 此外，专家们指出，越早开始运动越好，因为如果你在年轻时就养成运动的习惯，那么日后也更有可能延续这些运动模式。

en: It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or adolescents, and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. (31 words)
cn: 因此，理想的情况是，人们在儿童或青少年时期就开始运动，并且无论年龄多大，始终保持积极活跃的生活方式都是有益的。

en: However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s. (26 words)
cn: 不过，这项研究也确实表明，即便此前并不爱运动，若能在四五十岁时开始变得活跃起来，依然能够从中受益。

en: Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. (10 words)
cn: 和大多数厨师一样，“飞比”（Flippy）也不惧怕辛苦的工作。

en: Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. (30 words)
cn: 自去年夏天以来，这意味着它要在加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的加州汉堡（Caliburger）从上午11点一直工作到下午7点，此外还要在洛杉矶道奇体育场的Chick-N-Tots餐厅做一些短期工作。

en: These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. (13 words)
cn: 这些都是漫长而重复的工作时段，老板要求它必须做到绝对的一致性。

en: But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. (11 words)
cn: 但事实上，你永远不会听到“飞比”抱怨半句，或是说出任何话来。

en: For Flippy is a robot—a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes—that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards. (33 words)
cn: 因为“飞比”是一台机器人——一条连接云端、以3D热成像扫描仪为“眼睛”的机械臂——它每小时能翻烤汉堡肉饼或油炸80篮食物，还能监测食物状态，甚至在事后清理厨房。

en: Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers." (28 words)
cn: “飞比”由米索机器人公司（Miso Robotics）研发，该公司隶属于加州集团（Cali Group）。加州集团首席执行官约翰·米勒将其形容为“一家碰巧在卖芝士汉堡的科技公司”。

en: Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. (22 words)
cn: 加州集团研发新设备后，会在其遍布全球的加州汉堡门店中进行实地测试，“飞比”也将于今年被部署到这些门店中。

en: And Flippy is not alone. (5 words)
cn: 而“飞比”并非唯一的一台机器人。

en: Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners. (18 words)
cn: 同样在加利福尼亚州，熊机器人公司（Bear Robotics）也研发出了一款能自主导航的机器人“佩妮”（Penny），迄今已为4万名顾客提供过服务。

en: Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. (10 words)
cn: 十年前，机器人大厨和服务员还纯属科幻情节。

en: Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. (14 words)
cn: 如今，它们已成为现实，而且价格也让它们成为一项颇具可行性的投资。

en: "From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. (23 words)
cn: 熊机器人公司首席运营官胡安·伊格罗斯表示，从5月起，“佩妮”将采用订阅制方式交付使用，能带来“立竿见影的回报”。

en: Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. (8 words)
cn: 据报道，“飞比”的售价在6万至10万美元之间。

en: Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight—where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots—are now a possibility. (26 words)
cn: 如今，完全自动化、几乎无需人工监管的汉堡餐厅已成为可能——在这样的餐厅里，顾客通过屏幕点餐、电子支付，所吃的食物则由机器人烹制并送达。

en: The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. (16 words)
cn: 相关技术其实已经存在，眼下需要的只是以具备成本效益、且顾客愿意接受的方式，将其整合到一起。

en: In an industry keen to slash labour costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. (15 words)
cn: 在一个渴望削减人力成本、提高利润的行业中，进一步的自动化似乎已在所难免。

en: After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. (22 words)
cn: 在加利福尼亚州的“江南豆腐屋”餐厅经过八个月的试用后，熊机器人公司称，“佩妮”帮助该店销售额提升了28%。

en: Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values. (25 words)
cn: 与此同时，在美国的试点中，麦当劳目前正在其英国1300家门店安装的自助点餐屏幕，据报道使订单金额提升了30%。

en: Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. (26 words)
cn: 个性化被视为这项技术吸引力的关键所在，此外，它还能稳定地向顾客推送所谓的“加购推荐”（如套餐优惠、加点小食、加大饮品等）。

en: Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you—factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood. (44 words)
cn: 不久之后，当你登录某个餐厅应用程序时，它将能够利用你的数据和购买记录来为你推荐菜品——所考虑的因素五花八门，从天气状况，到（如果你是在一块能识别人脸的屏幕前点餐）你当下的心情，都可能被纳入考量。

en: "Right now people compromise on choice. (6 words)
cn: “眼下，人们在选择上其实是有所将就的。”

en: We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. (6 words)
cn: “摆在我们面前的，是一份‘一刀切’的菜单。”

en: Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. (9 words)
cn: “但归根结底，技术能让我们做出个性化的选择。”

en: You love spicy food and chicken? Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. (24 words)
cn: 餐饮科技公司Flyt的首席执行官汤姆·韦弗说：“你喜欢辣味食物和鸡肉？这是像你这样的顾客最常点的菜。”

en: He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. (20 words)
cn: 他还兴致勃勃地谈起赫尔辛基的快闪餐厅Take-In——一家全服务型餐厅，顾客可以在店内从各类外卖平台点餐。

en: "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants." (19 words)
cn: “这是几百年来头一次，数字技术让我们得以创造出全新形态的餐厅。”

en: If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. (18 words)
cn: 如果说街头快餐已经为自动化做好了准备，那么自动化对高端餐厅的影响，可能会更为微妙，也更为缓慢。

en: "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. (26 words)
cn: 谢菲尔德大学人工智能与机器人学教授诺埃尔·夏基说：“恐怕还要过很长很长时间，我们才能见到五星级的机器人大厨。”

en: "Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. (24 words)
cn: “除了人工智能在创造力上的差距之外，出色的烹饪还需要对食材有细腻入微的理解，以及精细的烹调技艺，这对机器人而言将是极为艰巨的挑战。”

en: Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow." (9 words)
cn: “把易碎的食物摆放到盘子上，机器人的动作也会慢得令人难以忍受。”

en: Currently, robots have limited functionality. (5 words)
cn: 目前，机器人的功能还相当有限。

en: A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. (13 words)
cn: 工作人员需要把餐盘装到Penny（一款送餐机器人）身上，而顾客则需要自己把餐盘取下来。

en: At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. (20 words)
cn: 在采用机器人技术的美国比萨外送公司Zume，诸如给比萨铺料这类难度较高的工作，仍由人工完成。

en: But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. (14 words)
cn: 但即将推出的Moley机器人，则让人得以一窥未来技术的精密程度。

en: Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. (27 words)
cn: 该机器人的动作是以《顶级大厨》（MasterChef）比赛冠军蒂姆·安德森的烹饪动作为模板设计的，其机械臂被固定安装在炉灶上方，经编程后可用生食材烹制菜肴。

en: It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks. (26 words)
cn: 它目前是为家庭使用而设计的，但研发方计划推出商用版本，这将使餐厅厨房实现自动化处理高难度技术任务成为可能。

en: For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous. (19 words)
cn: 就目前而言，QSR Automations公司为米切尔斯与巴特勒斯（Mitchells & Butlers）连锁酒吧以及肯德基所提供的厨房技术，则没有那么“炫酷”。

en: Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. (18 words)
cn: 该系统并不需要厨师大声喊出顾客的点单，而是通过屏幕自动分发这些订单。

en: The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time. (27 words)
cn: 厨房屏幕会随后告知厨师何时开始烹制每道菜，从而确保你那盘炸鱼、薯条和豌豆能在恰当的时间一起上桌。

en: The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs—a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. (22 words)
cn: 餐饮业目前正面临严重的熟练厨师短缺问题——据技能服务机构People 1st统计，缺口高达11,000人。

en: "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine. (23 words)
cn: 《Restaurant》杂志主编斯特凡·乔姆卡说：“那些旨在让流程变得更为‘傻瓜化’的自动化系统，正试图弥补这一缺口。”

en: In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. (21 words)
cn: 就简化或提升顾客体验而言，在线餐厅预订可以说是互联网时代轻松取得的一项成功。

en: Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. (11 words)
cn: 自动化的桌边点餐与支付，则被视为下一个具有里程碑意义的进展。

en: Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance. (32 words)
cn: 在那之前，像曼彻斯特“33奥尔德姆街”酒吧老板安迪·史密斯这样的早期采用者——他在自己的店里使用了Ordoo应用程序——很可能会发现，顾客的接受度虽在增长，却“低于预期”。

en: Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. (9 words)
cn: 餐饮科技领域令人尴尬的失败案例，屡屡登上新闻头条。

en: The TGI Fridays drone (无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. (25 words)
cn: 比如，TGI星期五餐厅的一架无人机曾致使《布鲁克林日报》一名摄影师受伤；美国汉堡连锁品牌Shake Shack也不得不放弃了全面推行无现金点餐点的计划。

en: But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist". (20 words)
cn: 但乔姆卡表示，如果这类技术仅仅是在为“并不真实存在的问题提供解决方案”，那么它就可能偏离了正确的方向。

en: "Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds. (8 words)
cn: 他补充道，“自动化支付”或许是有用的。

en: But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?" (13 words)
cn: 但在一家高档餐厅里，“你真的需要那么快就把晚餐吃完吗？”

en: That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. (21 words)
cn: 这种对人性化待客艺术的坚持，对于那些把自动化视为工作威胁的员工来说，会是一件令人欣慰的事。

en: "Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. (25 words)
cn: 工会“联合工会”（Unite）伦敦地区负责人戴夫·特恩布尔说：“联合工会担心，如果没有相应的保障机制，自动化带来的任何益处，都会绕过服务员等低薪岗位的工作者。”

en: "We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions." (19 words)
cn: “我们正在敦促国会议员们确保，自动化不会像以往历次工业革命那样，仅仅让少数富人获益。”

en: The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. (14 words)
cn: 行业内的一个共识是：自动化将使企业能够更有效地重新调配员工。

en: Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. (9 words)
cn: 工作岗位会发生变化，即便岗位数量不会立即减少。

en: "Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. (8 words)
cn: “自助点餐屏幕意味着前厅岗位的用人需求会增加。”

en: Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark. (12 words)
cn: 麦当劳首席运营官杰森·克拉克说：“去年，我们新招聘了1000名经理。”

en: Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs". (13 words)
cn: 加州汉堡（Caliburger）则设有一项培训计划，将员工重新培养为机器人工程师，或称“厨房技术员”。

en: But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads (管理费用) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. (23 words)
cn: 但归根结底，通过雇用更少的人手或以更低的薪酬水平来削减管理费用的机会，才是真正吸引各大品牌拥抱这项技术的原因。

en: Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. (24 words)
cn: 毫无疑问，在未来十年里，传统实体餐厅中的工作岗位将不可避免地减少，尤其是因为自动化将助推它们那个正在迅速崛起的对手——外卖配送行业。

en: Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. (22 words)
cn: 达美乐（Domino）和Just Eat等公司都已尝试过机器人和无人机配送，这类配送方式在冰岛雷克雅未克已经合法。

en: "Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey. (9 words)
cn: 诺埃尔·夏基说：“机器人送餐是未来的趋势。”

en: "Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day." (14 words)
cn: “这些时速4英里的小型地面机器人既安全，又能全天24小时工作。”

en: Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. (26 words)
cn: 只要将预期订单量的机器学习分析，与QSR等系统所生成的逐分钟烹饪数据结合起来，这支机器人配送队伍便几乎可以做到即时送达。

en: "Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. (17 words)
cn: Just Eat工程总监丹尼尔·理查森预测道：“餐厅将会在订单送达之前，就提前把食物准备好。”

en: "I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door." (27 words)
cn: “我只需要对家人说一句‘我们吃比萨吧’，我的智能助手就会听到这句话，十分钟后食物就会送到我家门口。”

en: No one is putting an exact date on it yet. (10 words)
cn: 目前还没有人能给出一个确切的实现日期。

en: But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming. (13 words)
cn: 但无论是在餐厅的用餐区，还是在你家门口，机器人的到来，已是大势所趋。

en: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. (18 words)
cn: 许多人把友谊看作一床能带来慰藉的毯子：一个可以依靠哭泣的肩膀，一个值得信赖、可以倾诉衷肠的灵魂伴侣。

en: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process. (26 words)
cn: 然而，更多时候，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，却会在途中失去朋友，而这已成为这一过程中习以为常的一部分。

en: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. (19 words)
cn: 伴随日常生活而来的混乱与永无止境的动荡，是维系稳定友谊道路上一个极具破坏性的障碍。

en: As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones. (19 words)
cn: 身为学生，我们常常用这个借口，来轻描淡写地打发掉那些曾经被自己视为挚爱之人的离去。

en: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. (32 words)
cn: 与其把人生看作一场竞赛——每个人都在自己通往某种成功的赛道上奔跑——我们必须重新学会珍视自己在这条路上所建立的种种联结。

en: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom. (9 words)
cn: 我们必须重新审视极端个人自由所带来的危害。

en: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. (11 words)
cn: 极端个人主义将个人自由置于集体之上。

en: It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans. (17 words)
cn: 举例来说，它主张，全民医保作为集体主义的一个例证，威胁到了许多美国人的梦想。

en: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. (10 words)
cn: 我们当中许多人都已沦为个人主义文化的牺牲品。

en: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person. (27 words)
cn: 社会往往推崇个人成就，并基于这样一种假设来加以褒扬：胜出或成功，是比别人更努力工作的结果。

en: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success." (15 words)
cn: 作为一个社会整体，我们将“在通往成功的路上失去朋友”这一观念奉为圭臬。

en: I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. (19 words)
cn: 我记得在高中时曾听人说过：“不用担心失去友谊，只管专心学习、考上大学。”

en: That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. (18 words)
cn: “从长远来看，这才是唯一重要的事。”这种想法并非我一个人独有的经历。

en: It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. (15 words)
cn: 许多成功故事都在宣扬这种观念，它也已深深嵌入我们看待成长的方式之中。

en: Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. (16 words)
cn: 励志演说家们会促使听众坦然接受“失去朋友是不可避免的结局”这一说法。

en: Spend too much time with friends? (6 words)
cn: 跟朋友花了太多时间？

en: You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. (8 words)
cn: 那你正在浪费本该用来成就自己的宝贵时间。

en: Invest time in your relationships? (5 words)
cn: 把时间投入到人际关系中？

en: Invest time in your work instead. (6 words)
cn: 还不如把时间投入到工作中去。

en: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. (20 words)
cn: 这种对成功持续不断的渴求，蒙蔽了我们的双眼，使我们看不清伴随日常生活而来的种种变化旋涡。

en: We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. (14 words)
cn: 我们被期待要取得实实在在的成功——获得奖项、晋升更高的职位、取得更好的成绩。

en: In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized. (13 words)
cn: 为了取得成功，我们失去了朋友，而这一现象可悲地已被视为常态。

en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. (12 words)
cn: 我们不能对失去友谊安之若素，因为友谊正是我们人生的锚点。

en: Yes, pursue success. (3 words)
cn: 没错，去追求成功吧。

en: Challenge yourself. (2 words)
cn: 去挑战自我吧。

en: Push limits. (2 words)
cn: 去突破极限吧。

en: But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others. (30 words)
cn: 但与所有那些自诩为成功专家的人所宣扬的相反，独自奋斗并不会让你比那些借助他人帮助而取得成就的人更成功、更出色。

en: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. (23 words)
cn: 要努力去培养健康的人际关系，并在看似忙得抽不出时间给任何人的日程中，坚持维系这些关系。

en: Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result. (33 words)
cn: 尽管我们或许生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中，但一路上有人支持你、爱护你，远比任何最终的结果都更为重要。

en: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality." (29 words)
cn: 马丁·路德·金在接受诺贝尔和平奖的获奖演说中说道：“我相信，赤手空拳的真理与无条件的爱，终将在现实中获得最后的胜利。”

en: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. (18 words)
cn: 五十多年过去了，我们的社会依然在艰难地分辨真相与幻想、事实与虚构。

en: From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. (18 words)
cn: 从围绕气候变化的争议，到关于奴隶制该如何被讲授的辩论，美国正站在一个十字路口。

en: And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations. (13 words)
cn: 而围绕公平的斗争，正是这些至关重要的对话的核心所在。

en: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. (10 words)
cn: 一项又一项研究表明，不公平已带来了令人震惊的后果。

en: A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades. (33 words)
cn: 花旗银行2020年的一份报告指出，如果过去二十年间与高等教育相关的公平问题能够得到妥善解决，“黑人学生原本可以将其终身收入总额提高1130亿美元”。

en: This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. (14 words)
cn: 这一数据背后，折射出我们这个国家未能正视的大量问题。

en: It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. (18 words)
cn: 它同时也揭示了一个事实：我们正在错失弥合彼此分歧的宝贵机会。

en: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity. (17 words)
cn: 然而，通过传承马丁·路德·金的精神遗产，我们能够让国家重新走上通往真正公平的道路。

en: Students—and adults for that matter—simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. (21 words)
cn: 学生——就此而言，成年人也一样——若不了解当今种种冲突最初的成因，就根本无法真正理解这些冲突。

en: That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. (17 words)
cn: 这意味着，我们有责任帮助他们在美国历史与当下时事之间建立起联系。

en: It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. (18 words)
cn: 这也意味着，要为他们提供应对自身生活中不公与偏见所需要的工具。

en: Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel. (32 words)
cn: 秉持这些原则，并致力于展开真诚的对话，能够帮助每一位学生更好地领悟我们已经走过了多远的路，也更清楚地看清前方尚待跋涉的旅程。

en: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country. (26 words)
cn: 通过更为真实地分析对更多合格、多元化教育工作者的需求，我们就能改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训与人才留用策略。

en: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. (9 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，我们社会中根深蒂固的分歧，正在拖慢这些进展的步伐。

en: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". (18 words)
cn: 一项近期调查发现，77%的美国人认为，这个国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。

en: But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. (14 words)
cn: 但有关两极分化加剧的报道，不应说服我们对彼此视而不见。

en: Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on. (11 words)
cn: 恰恰相反，它们应当促使我们正面直视彼此共同面临的问题。

en: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". (12 words)
cn: 正如一些人所主张的那样，我们并非生活在一个“后种族社会”之中。

en: We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. (18 words)
cn: 在种族不平等问题上，我们根本承担不起继续掩耳盗铃的后果。

en: Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. (25 words)
cn: 除非我们诚实地正视不宽容、偏见，以及这些社会痼疾如何影响着我们彼此相待的方式，否则不公正将继续困扰着我们。

en: But our children and our grandchildren deserve better. (8 words)
cn: 但我们的子孙后代理应得到更好的未来。

en: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. (18 words)
cn: 值此马丁·路德·金纪念日，以及在未来的日子里，让我们承诺齐心协力，去打破现状。

en: Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience." (32 words)
cn: 让我们继续携手建设一个更美好、更具包容性的国家；正如马丁·路德·金所言：“一个与自身和平相处的社会，一个能够与自己良知共存的社会。”

en: We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. (18 words)
cn: 我们人类总喜欢相信自己是特殊的，但科学和技术却一再证明，这种看法是错误的。

en: People once thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things. (31 words)
cn: 人们曾经认为，人类是唯一会使用工具、组建团队、传播文化的动物，但科学已经证明，其他动物也同样具备这些能力。

en: Meanwhile, technology has quashed (使无效), one by one, claims that cognitive tasks require a human brain. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，科技正逐一击破那些认为认知任务必须依靠人类大脑才能完成的说法。

en: The first adding machine was invented in 1623. (8 words)
cn: 第一台加法计算器发明于1623年。

en: This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. (10 words)
cn: 就在过去这一年里，一件由计算机生成的作品赢得了一场艺术比赛的奖项。

en: I believe the moment when computers meet and surpass human intelligence is on the horizon. (15 words)
cn: 我相信，计算机智能赶上并超越人类智能的那一刻，已经近在眼前。

en: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? (19 words)
cn: 当机器变得比最聪明的人类更智能、更富创造力时，人类的智慧与创造力又将如何被评判其价值呢？

en: There will likely be a spectrum. (6 words)
cn: 答案很可能会呈现出一个从此端到彼端的连续光谱。

en: In some domains, people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. (17 words)
cn: 在某些领域，即便计算机能做得更好，人们依然更看重由人类亲自去完成这件事。

en: It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away. (21 words)
cn: 距离计算机击败世界棋王加里·卡斯帕罗夫已经过去了整整二十五年，但人类的国际象棋并未因此消失。

en: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and redundant. (10 words)
cn: 而在另一些领域，人类的技能则会显得既昂贵又多余。

en: Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic accompanying a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer—they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps entertaining. (33 words)
cn: 以插画为例：大多数读者并不在意配在杂志文章旁边的那幅图，究竟是由人绘制还是由计算机生成——他们只是希望这幅图与内容相关、有新意，或许还带点趣味性。

en: And, of course, this question isn't black or white. (9 words)
cn: 当然，这个问题并非非黑即白。

en: Many fields will be a hybrid, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where, much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to oversee the machines. (45 words)
cn: 许多领域将呈现出一种混合形态：一些人能幸运地找到自己的一席之地，但大部分工作将由计算机完成——就像今天的制造业一样，绝大多数工作由机器人完成，但仍需要一些人在场监督这些机器。

en: If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to vanish, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich. (43 words)
cn: 如果历史可以作为借鉴，那么几乎可以肯定，人工智能的发展将导致更多工作岗位消失，拥有纯人类技能的创意工作者将变得更加富有，但人数会越来越少，而那些掌握创意技术所有权的人，则将成为新一代的超级富豪。

en: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned—and it's not always clear when to give up. (18 words)
cn: 项目、感情和工作，并不总能如我们计划的那样顺利进行——而且，何时该放弃，往往也并不总是那么清晰明了。

en: We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win," but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses. (20 words)
cn: 我们都曾无数次听人说过“半途而废者永远不会成功”这句话，但有时候，及时止损才是最明智的决定。

en: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. (27 words)
cn: 想一想那段早已走到尽头、你却仍不肯放手的感情，或是那份明明让你痛苦不堪、你却依然坚守的工作。

en: Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. (21 words)
cn: 我们当中许多人都会努力抓住最后一丝希望，认为自己能让“它”——无论这个“它”指的是什么——重新变好。

en: And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea. (24 words)
cn: 虽然坚持通常是一种十分可贵的品质，但它也可能让你在一件早已不再明智的事情上，投入过多。

en: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit." (17 words)
cn: 身为一名高管教练，我曾与许多充满热忱、勤奋努力、不愿轻言“放弃”的领导者共事过。

en: But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't. (20 words)
cn: 但最有智慧的领导者，懂得分辨“过早放弃”与“不该坚持却仍在坚持”之间的区别。

en: We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into—even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. (35 words)
cn: 我们都容易受到“沉没成本谬误”的影响——这是一种不自觉的认知偏差，会让我们执着于已经投入了时间、精力或金钱的事情，哪怕放弃才是更有利的选择。

en: We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere—investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. (47 words)
cn: 我们清楚地知道，已经付出的资源是无法收回的，于是便选择继续坚持——继续投入一个本该终止的项目，继续维系一段本该结束的感情，或是把一本自己早已不喜欢、本该放下的书读完，只因为已经读了一半。

en: If quitting is "not your thing," you may be especially susceptible to this bias. (14 words)
cn: 如果“放弃”从来不是你的作风，那你可能格外容易受到这种偏差的影响。

en: The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. (27 words)
cn: 沉没成本谬误会让我们过度担忧一旦选择放手将会失去什么，却对“不放手”所要付出的代价想得远远不够。

en: To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. (19 words)
cn: 为了抵消这种偏差，你可以有意识地把注意力重新聚焦到“收益”上，从而更客观地权衡各种选择。

en: Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? (11 words)
cn: 问问自己：如果现在及时止损，我能获得什么？

en: Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? (11 words)
cn: 我会因此变得更快乐吗？会不会因此腾出时间，去抓住另一个（更好的）机会？

en: Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? (11 words)
cn: 接着再问问自己：如果继续硬撑下去，我将要付出怎样的代价？

en: For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? (17 words)
cn: 举例来说，你是否可能会在已经损失的基础上，继续投入更多本可以用在别处的资源？

en: Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities? (13 words)
cn: 又或者，你是否会因此再也没有精力去把握其他有前景的可能性？

en: The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. (25 words)
cn: “控制幻觉”同样可能干扰我们的正确判断，让我们高估自己掌控事态、促成良好结果的能力。

en: This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. (13 words)
cn: 这种偏差会给我们带来一种“掌控感”，在一定程度上有益于心理健康。

en: However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. (15 words)
cn: 但与此同时，这种偏差也可能导致我们在一条注定失败的道路上，投入越来越多。

en: Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out. (36 words)
cn: 尤其是当它与“我绝不是个半途而废的人”这种心态相结合时，我们对某件事或某个人所拥有的掌控感一旦被高估，就会让我们在本该抽身而退时，反而选择加倍投入。

en: To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. (21 words)
cn: 要抵消这种偏差，你可以审视自己所处的情况，制作一张简单的两栏清单，分别列出哪些是你能掌控的、哪些是你无法掌控的。

en: Think rigorously. (2 words)
cn: 要严谨地进行思考。

en: While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way. (22 words)
cn: 虽然你或许能够影响他人和各种局面，但你无法强迫他们按照你的意愿去改变或行事。

en: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. (26 words)
cn: 厘清哪些事在你的掌控之中、哪些不在，对于就“放弃还是坚持”做出高质量的决策至关重要。

en: With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. (27 words)
cn: 手握一份写下来的清单，你就能确保自己把注意力集中在可掌控的事情上，也能更好地判断继续投入是否值得。

en: Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering. (15 words)
cn: 把精力和情感耗费在自己无法掌控的事情上，既会让人身心俱疲，也会削弱个人的掌控感与力量。

en: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. (13 words)
cn: 研究表明，人们往往会把自我身份认同和社会地位，与自己所做出的承诺紧密联系在一起。

en: And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status. (20 words)
cn: 而正因为我们把自己等同于自己所作的承诺，一旦从某项承诺中抽身，便可能被感知为对自身身份或地位的一种威胁。

en: Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. (10 words)
cn: 就拿我的客户瑞安来说吧，她是一家科技公司的一名领导者。

en: Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. (36 words)
cn: 瑞安已经在一个设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但该项目一直未能取得所需的成果；然而，一想到自己付出了这么多，却要将项目放弃，她就难以承受。

en: As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." (27 words)
cn: 在我和瑞安一起探讨她究竟该取消这个由她主导的项目、还是继续坚持下去时，她说道：“问题是，我从来不是一个半途而废的人。”

en: This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action. (16 words)
cn: 这种单一而僵化的自我认知，蒙蔽了她的判断力，也限制了她可以采取的行动选择。

en: Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. (11 words)
cn: 我们的自我概念与身份认同，都是会影响我们行为的心理构念。

en: If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. (27 words)
cn: 如果你强烈地认定自己“绝不是半途而废的人”，那么这种狭隘而僵化的自我概念，可能会让你在某条既定的道路上一直停滞不前。

en: To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. (15 words)
cn: 要克服这种内在的障碍，可以回想一下自己身上其他一些积极的特质与性格特点。

en: Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? (19 words)
cn: 问问自己：我还拥有（或希望拥有）哪些其他优势，是可以运用到当下这个处境中的？

en: For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery." (25 words)
cn: 举例来说，当我问瑞安，在做这个决定时，她的性格中还有哪些积极品质是她需要好好运用的，她回答道：“洞察力和勇气。”

en: Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. (14 words)
cn: 接下来，不妨透过自己身上每一个这样的特质，重新审视一下自己所处的境况。

en: What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? (11 words)
cn: 你身上那个善于洞察的部分会怎么说？那个勇敢的部分呢？

en: Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. (17 words)
cn: 从这些不同的性格特质出发去思考自己的决定，能让你意识到，自己其实拥有更多的选择。

en: It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. (18 words)
cn: 此外，寻求外部的信息来源也会有所帮助，而不是仅仅依赖自己的思考和直觉。

en: But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit. (10 words)
cn: 但重要的是，要仔细想清楚，自己究竟该征求谁的意见。

en: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. (14 words)
cn: 理想情况下，应该去寻求那些在这件事上投入比你少、利害关系不如你深的人的意见。

en: If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. (24 words)
cn: 比如说，如果你正在考虑是否要关闭自己创办的企业，不妨去请教其他创业者，而不只是询问自己的合伙人。

en: Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. (26 words)
cn: 同样地，如果你想寻求感情方面的建议，最好去问一个不曾亲历你这段感情起起伏伏的人，而不是只依赖自己最好的朋友。

en: In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?" (21 words)
cn: 无论哪种情况，我都建议你先描述清楚自己的处境，然后追问一句类似“如果是你，你会怎么处理这种情况？”这样的问题。

en: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. (21 words)
cn: 另一种做法是，去寻找确凿的数据，来揭示你正在考虑的这件事，真实的成功几率究竟有多大。

en: Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. (13 words)
cn: 继续沿用创业的例子来说，数字才是你最好的朋友。

en: Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. (32 words)
cn: 利用这些数字，让自己暂时跳出对这个创意的偏爱，去审视你的资金消耗速度相对于增长计划、行业整体增速，以及其他能预测创业成功与否的各项因素。

en: External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered. (16 words)
cn: 来自外部的信息来源，能帮助你看到那些自己此前或许未曾考虑过的视角和可能性。

en: When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. (21 words)
cn: 当一件事最初看起来大有希望，结果却没有按照我们所设想的那样发展时，我们很容易变得过度自我苛责。

en: Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. (23 words)
cn: 没有人喜欢那种“自己做出了错误决定”的感觉，尤其是当“做出明智的决定”这项品质，本身就是你十分看重的东西时。

en: The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. (11 words)
cn: 此时，最有效的应对策略，便是放过自己一次。

en: Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience (韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset. (25 words)
cn: 练习自我关怀，能够增强你的心理韧性、情商和对他人的同理心，还能提升你的表现，帮助你培养出一种成长型思维。

en: Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. (16 words)
cn: 与其反复纠结、苛责自己，不如把注意力转向：自己能从这次经历中学到些什么。

en: For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. (18 words)
cn: 比如，瑞安就意识到，自己在主导这个设计项目的过程中，锻炼出了多项新技能和领导能力。

en: And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her. (22 words)
cn: 尽管她最终还是决定放弃这个项目，但她依然庆幸自己曾经努力尝试过，也对这段经历教会她的一切心怀感激。

en: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. (6 words)
cn: 不可否认，坚持不懈确实能够帮助我们走向成功。

en: But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. (22 words)
cn: 但为了自身的幸福感，学会分辨“过早放弃”与“执着于一条注定失败的道路”，同样十分重要。

en: While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities. (24 words)
cn: 尽管放手可能并不容易，但它能为你腾出时间、精力与心理空间，去构想新的可能性、追寻新的机会。

en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. (9 words)
cn: 作为彼此依存的存在，我们无法脱离他人而独自蓬勃发展。

en: We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. (27 words)
cn: 我们喜欢与志同道合的人共事——那些与我们有着共同兴趣，或同样信奉我们所看重的某项事业的人。

en: This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families. (21 words)
cn: 这一点，从我们把自己组织成国家、地区、社区、机构和家庭等各种集体形式中，便可见一斑。

en: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? (14 words)
cn: 你所归属的群体，是否拥有强烈的集体意识或共同的信念？

en: Is there interdependence among its members? (6 words)
cn: 其成员之间是否存在相互依存的关系？

en: Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? (11 words)
cn: 你是否认为这个群体，是自己存在意义中重要的一部分？

en: If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity. (14 words)
cn: 如果你对以上问题的回答都是肯定的，那么你正在体验的，正是一种微观形式的团结。

en: What is solidarity? (3 words)
cn: 什么是“团结”？

en: Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "... a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people." (20 words)
cn: 词典中对它最简单的定义是：“……一群人之间共有的、能将彼此凝聚在一起的观点、情感、目标或利益。”

en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labour. (38 words)
cn: 在我们所生活的这个日益多元化的社会中，“团结”呈现出复杂而多面的特质——它在身处快速变化的环境、处于复杂分工体系之中的一个个独特个体之间，编织出相互依存的纽带。

en: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社群主义). (12 words)
cn: “团结”的一个面向，与社群主义的原则十分契合。

en: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. (14 words)
cn: 在这种情境下，个人会放弃自身利益，去服务于集体的共同利益。

en: However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. (18 words)
cn: 然而，这种对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格坚持，也限制了个体差异与个人偏好的表达与实践。

en: Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group. (13 words)
cn: 结果，个体性与自主性便被牺牲，以维持群体的统一。

en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. (17 words)
cn: “团结”也被视为是对个人主义与选择自由被过度强调这一现象的一种反拨。

en: It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others. (38 words)
cn: 它与自由主义的理念背道而驰——后者主张个人不应受到约束，将社会视为妨碍自己自由选择、按照对自身有利的方式行事的障碍，而不去顾及这些行为会如何影响他人。

en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. (22 words)
cn: 但尽管“团结”具有诸多面向，社会理论家们仍将其视为促成社会秩序与进步的一个关键因素。

en: They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. (24 words)
cn: 他们认为，随着人类社会变得日益多元，要想生存下去，就需要基于种种差异建立起更多新的纽带。

en: In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. (20 words)
cn: 有鉴于此，他们认为，真正的团结，不仅仅是建立在共同利益基础上的一种肤浅关系。

en: Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. (17 words)
cn: 团结并非仅仅是权衡“对自己有多少好处”这种策略性计算的产物。

en: It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. (11 words)
cn: 它也不是一个建立在“你我联手对抗全世界”这种原则之上的排他性小圈子。

en: Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. (8 words)
cn: 恰恰相反，它是包容的，且并非出于强迫。

en: Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other—in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. (23 words)
cn: 出于团结而行动，意味着彼此支持、相互声援——因为人们认识到，一个人的命运与另一个人的命运是紧密相连的。

en: It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. (22 words)
cn: 这是一种以合作实践为特征的纽带，并因对他人福祉或共同利益的关切而得到不断加强。

en: It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable. (20 words)
cn: 它为捍卫人的尊严而奋斗，也倾听并回应着最弱势群体的呼声。

en: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. (14 words)
cn: 那些屡屡给出不请自来的建议的人，可能确实是出于好意，真心想要提供帮助。

en: Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. (16 words)
cn: 另一些人这样做，则可能是出于一种源自“能够影响他人”这一能力的自我价值感。

en: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency. (24 words)
cn: 一项研究发现，相较于权力欲较低的人，那些权力欲较强的人更倾向于给别人提建议。

en: Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. (23 words)
cn: 在无私的外表之下，人们之所以会不请自来地给你提建议，或许是因为这样做能让他们感到自己更有权力、更能掌控局面。

en: They may not be fully aware of this drive, however. (10 words)
cn: 不过，他们自己可能并未完全意识到这种驱动力的存在。

en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. (23 words)
cn: 这类人还可能表现出一种成问题的情绪脆弱性——他们很容易情绪激动，而且需要很长时间才能平复下来。

en: It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations. (30 words)
cn: 这或许是因为，在他们的童年时期，只有当情绪反应最为强烈时，他们的感受才会得到认可，这也使得他们养成了在面对不适时反应过度的习惯，而这种习惯在大多数情况下都显得不太恰当。

en: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. (28 words)
cn: 当一个人给建议是为了让自己感到更有权力时，他们行为背后潜藏的焦虑，往往会被建议的接收者察觉到。

en: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesirable result. (29 words)
cn: 在这种情况下，人们很容易忍不住对提建议的人做出强烈反应，指责对方是在操控自己，但这种做法可能会带来不理想的后果。

en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict. (43 words)
cn: 如果“给建议”这一行为本身正积极地维系着某人的自我价值感，那么直截了当的拒绝，就可能被他们视为一种威胁，从而激活其“战斗或逃跑”的应激反应，导致他们在寻求认可的行为上变本加厉，甚至引发更大的冲突。

en: The key is to validate without over-identifying. (7 words)
cn: 关键在于，既要认可对方，又不能过度认同对方的说法。

en: You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. (34 words)
cn: 你可以让对方知道，你已经听到了他们的想法，也理解他们的出发点，但同时不必接受“没有他们的帮助你就无法应付”这种可能带有伤害性的说法。

en: You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?" (42 words)
cn: 你不妨这样说：“谢谢你的想法。我自己已经有了应对这件事的计划，不过我真的很感激你的看法，也会把它纳入考虑。以后如果我需要帮助，可以再告诉你吗？”

en: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. (15 words)
cn: 如果你很难得体地设立界限，那么应优先着力提升自己的自我调节能力。

en: As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster. (24 words)
cn: 尽管不断收到不请自来的建议，会让你感到不适，但如果你能以宽容的态度去回应，局面往往能更快地得到缓解。

en: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. (26 words)
cn: 尽管这通常并非提建议者的本意，但许多接收到这些不请自来的建议的人，往往会因此感到有压力、被冒犯，或者单纯地感到心烦。

en: Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety. (24 words)
cn: 如果你觉得有必要，在这方面设立一道界限，是完全合理的，也能为你带来更多的情感安全感。

en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress. (30 words)
cn: 设立界限时，最好能考虑到对方这样做背后的深层原因，以此来避免不必要的冲突和更多的压力。

en: It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. (16 words)
cn: 最好把口音理解为一种独特的、成体系的、受规则支配的说话方式。

en: Accent is not a synonym for dialect, but it's related. (10 words)
cn: 口音并不是方言的同义词，但两者确实相关。

en: Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only. (24 words)
cn: 方言是一个统括性的术语，涵盖了某一社群发音、造词、排词的整套方式；而口音仅仅指其中发音这一部分。

en: Many laymen presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is inherently the best form of speech, but linguists (语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a reality. (54 words)
cn: 许多外行人都想当然地认为，每个国家都存在唯一的标准说话方式和唯一的标准口音，并认为这种被感知为标准的说话方式本质上就是最好的言语形式；但语言学家却常常指出，“标准口音”这一概念，与其说是一种客观现实，不如理解为一种理想化的设想。

en: In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books. (25 words)
cn: 换句话说，根本没有人真正说着“标准英语”；它只是一种存在于语法书和文体手册中的、想象出来的语言使用方式。

en: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been multiple supposed standards, depending on time and place. (26 words)
cn: 语言学家一致认为并不存在唯一真正标准的原因之一在于：多年来，根据时代和地域的不同，一直存在着多种所谓的“标准”。

en: The standard for English in British newsreels (新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. (24 words)
cn: 举例来说，20世纪50年代英国新闻片中的英语标准，与今天美国全国新闻广播中的标准就大相径庭。

en: In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon—and broadcast outlets across the spectrum have never consistently held to those standards anyway. (27 words)
cn: 事实上，从来就不存在一个得到全体一致认可的单一标准——而且，各类广播媒体也从未始终如一地恪守过这些所谓的标准。

en: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is influential and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that deviate from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. (33 words)
cn: 即便如此，“标准口音”这一观念依然颇具影响力，许多职场和教育环境仍在延续着这样一种看法：偏离当前标准的口音不够得体，甚至是不恰当的。

en: Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in domains such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. (27 words)
cn: 学者们发现，美国南方口音的特征，在政府、法律以及服务型行业等领域更容易被接受，但在科技行业中则接受度较低。

en: The acceptability of nonstandard accents may correlate with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace. (26 words)
cn: 非标准口音的可接受程度，可能与阶层和文化上的差异相关——较新兴或声望较高的行业，往往更期望员工在职场中使用较为标准的口音。

en: Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. (17 words)
cn: 定时交通信号灯是按照预先设定的时间表运行的，这些时间表本应与交通高峰时段相协调。

en: Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. (20 words)
cn: 各城市至少需要每两年监测并更新一次信号灯的时间安排，才能确保这些系统持续有效运转。

en: In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize (协调) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. (25 words)
cn: 在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶，一项雄心勃勃、意在更进一步、将全市每一盏红绿灯都实现同步协调的项目，耗资超过4亿美元。

en: Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. (22 words)
cn: 如果你去问一位当地居民，他们多半会认同：在路上节省下来的时间，完全值得这笔投入。

en: If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion (拥堵) and 20% off air pollution. (15 words)
cn: 如果在全国范围内推行信号同步，交通拥堵有望减少10%，空气污染也有望减少20%。

en: Congestion costs time, money, and lives. (6 words)
cn: 交通拥堵会耗费时间、金钱，甚至生命。

en: Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. (13 words)
cn: 大数据能够帮助改善数以百万计的人们安全共享道路的方式。

en: However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light! (11 words)
cn: 然而，若没有交通信号灯，这一切都将无从谈起！

en: The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable—or effective. (17 words)
cn: 世界上第一盏交通信号灯诞生于19世纪60年代的伦敦，但它几乎难以辨认，效果也十分有限。

en: It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. (18 words)
cn: 1868年，铁路经理约翰·皮克·奈特将其从铁路信号系统改造而来。

en: The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. (18 words)
cn: 铁路系统在夜间使用红色煤气灯表示停车信号，白天则使用绿色煤气灯。

en: Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore (臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868. (16 words)
cn: 1868年12月，奈特在伦敦威斯敏斯特桥附近，安装了一套类似的煤气灯臂板信号系统。

en: The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. (10 words)
cn: 第一盏交通信号灯的“寿命”十分短暂。

en: A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed. (22 words)
cn: 安装还不到一个月，一次煤气泄漏就导致其中一盏信号灯在负责操作的警察面前发生了爆炸。

en: Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. (8 words)
cn: 伦敦这次事故之后，交通信号灯的自动化进程一度陷入停滞。

en: Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. (18 words)
cn: 此后又过了四十年，随着汽车不断涌入城市街道，才促使美国开始发展交通信号灯技术。

en: London would not see another traffic light until 1929. (9 words)
cn: 而伦敦，则一直要等到1929年，才重新出现交通信号灯。

en: The United States is a car culture like no other country. (11 words)
cn: 美国是一个独一无二的“汽车文化”国家。

en: Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars. (28 words)
cn: 与大多数欧洲城市不同——那些城市在马匹还是“高科技”交通工具的年代就已开始城市规划——美国的许多城市，则是围绕着城市扩张、郊区地块和汽车来进行设计的。

en: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. (14 words)
cn: 随着交通和城市规模的不断扩大，人们竞相寻找解决日益严峻的交通问题的方案。

en: The first traffic signals were semaphores. (6 words)
cn: 最早的交通信号是臂板信号机。

en: Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. (13 words)
cn: 臂板信号机是一种带有可活动臂杆的塔状装置，用来指示车辆停止或通行。

en: They could be manual or automatic. (6 words)
cn: 它们既可以手动操作，也可以自动运行。

en: There was no consistent design. (5 words)
cn: 当时并没有统一的设计标准。

en: Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose. (14 words)
cn: 各种不同的型号被相继发明出来，并根据各城市的实际需要投入使用。

en: In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. (17 words)
cn: 1912年，莱斯特·怀尔还是一名警察，他被主街与南200街路口的交通状况折腾得筋疲力尽。

en: He developed a manually switched stop light. (7 words)
cn: 于是他研发出了一种需要手动切换的停止信号灯。

en: The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. (19 words)
cn: 这个四面体的箱子被架设在一根十英尺高的杆子上，看起来就像一个鸟舍，需要由警察手动操作。

en: The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights. (15 words)
cn: 警察需要扳动开关，在暗红灯和绿灯之间进行切换。

en: Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. (10 words)
cn: 和1910年的臂板信号机一样，第一代电动信号灯也使用文字来传达信息。

en: However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. (13 words)
cn: 不过，这些文字不再写在会升降的臂杆上。

en: The words "stop" or "move" were on lights. (8 words)
cn: “停止”或“通行”这两个词，被写在了灯光上。

en: The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection (十字路口). (13 words)
cn: 在一个十字路口的四个转角处，各竖起一根灯柱，依次点亮。

en: It was not automated, though. (5 words)
cn: 不过，这套系统并未实现自动化。

en: A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches. (11 words)
cn: 仍需要一个岗亭里的操作员，来手动扳动开关。

en: The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. (16 words)
cn: 这套系统使警察得以从街道中央转移到街角来执勤。

en: From that vantage (有利地位), an officer could oversee the crowd. (10 words)
cn: 站在这一有利位置，警察便能对人群和车流一览无余。

en: If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. (20 words)
cn: 一旦有紧急车辆驶来，警察便可扳动开关，将路口所有方向都切换为红灯，从而清空整个路口。

en: The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. (7 words)
cn: 这样一来，紧急车辆便能毫无阻碍地顺利通过。

en: Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917. (23 words)
cn: 最终，1917年，旧金山推出了第一套既可自动、也可手动操作的红绿电动信号灯系统。

en: In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit—also known as Motor City, USA. (16 words)
cn: 1920年，第一套三色信号灯系统在底特律问世——这座城市素有“美国汽车城”之称。

en: The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. (16 words)
cn: 交通信号灯的演进，恐怕再没有比“汽车城”更合适的诞生地了。

en: Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). (14 words)
cn: 福特汽车公司于1903年在底特律成立（此后其他汽车公司也相继跟进）。

en: Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production. (18 words)
cn: 福特通过更大规模的工厂化生产，让普通民众而非仅仅是富人，也能负担得起汽车。

en: Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. (14 words)
cn: 面对呼啸穿过路口的大量新增车辆，仅有“停”与“行”两种信号已远远不够。

en: Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. (21 words)
cn: 街道上不仅挤满了数量激增的汽车，还有送货马车、熙攘的人群、自行车、马车和有轨电车。

en: The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights. (19 words)
cn: 警示性黄灯的引入，有助于提高驾驶员的安全性，减少了因闯红灯而引发的事故。

en: Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. (9 words)
cn: 在混乱不堪的城市街道上，停止信号灯的作用是极其重要的。

en: Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. (6 words)
cn: 人行横道直到1951年才被引入。

en: The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899. (11 words)
cn: 美国历史上第一起行人死亡事故，发生在1899年。

en: The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. (20 words)
cn: 现代交通信号灯的研发也许始于伦敦，但它却是在美国真正成长起来的。

en: In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. (16 words)
cn: 在克利夫兰，一位名叫加勒特·摩根的非裔美国发明家，研发出了一款价格亲民、并申请了专利的交通信号灯。

en: The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. (13 words)
cn: 黄灯的引入，让路口比过去那种只有“停”与“行”的系统更加安全。

en: The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights. (16 words)
cn: 这种新设计造价低廉，使得更多信号灯得以被安装普及。

en: Morgan sold the patent to General Electric—and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. (16 words)
cn: 摩根把这项专利卖给了通用电气公司——交通信号灯从此得以“一路绿灯”，广泛推广开来。

en: Green means go. (3 words)
cn: 绿灯意味着通行。

en: It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. (26 words)
cn: 道理就是这么简单，但即便如此，最好还是要留意两侧是否有车辆没有注意信号、或正在闯灯驶来。

en: Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. (8 words)
cn: 黄灯意味着减速并准备停车。

en: It does not mean full-throttle (全速) ahead. (6 words)
cn: 它并不意味着可以全速冲过去。

en: While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. (21 words)
cn: 虽然猛踩油门闯过路口有时也能侥幸过关，但闯黄灯仍可能招致罚单，甚至引发危险的事故。

en: Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. (10 words)
cn: 红灯是一种明确而一贯的停车警示。

en: Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. (19 words)
cn: 即便在允许红灯右转的地方，你也必须先完全停稳，才能右转。

en: You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. (14 words)
cn: 你还必须让行于任何直行车辆，因为它们拥有优先通行权。

en: In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. (15 words)
cn: 在美国大多数州和城市，除非另有标示，否则允许红灯右转。

en: New York City does not allow a right on red. (10 words)
cn: 纽约市则不允许红灯右转。

en: Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. (13 words)
cn: 红色箭头信号意味着，在美国大多数州，你都不能在红灯时转弯。

en: The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. (15 words)
cn: 在这些情况下，只有当绿色箭头亮起时，你才能进行转弯。

en: However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming. (35 words)
cn: 不过，在伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、马里兰州、密歇根州、新罕布什尔州、北达科他州、俄勒冈州、南卡罗来纳州、犹他州、华盛顿州以及怀俄明州，只要完全停稳后，仍可以在红色箭头亮起时右转。

en: Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. (19 words)
cn: 闪烁的红灯与停车标志作用相同，通常用于车流量较小的四向交叉路口。

en: When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. (13 words)
cn: 遇到闪烁红灯时，必须完全停稳。

en: Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. (14 words)
cn: 闪烁的红色箭头信号同样意味着先停车，然后再继续转弯。

en: Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. (14 words)
cn: 闪烁的黄灯则意味着让行或提醒谨慎驾驶，比如在消防站外常见这种信号。

en: There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. (15 words)
cn: 美国并不存在所有方向同时闪烁黄灯的情况，因为这种设置是被禁止的。

en: If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic. (14 words)
cn: 如果你遇到的是闪烁黄灯，就应当让行于对向来车。

en: Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. (10 words)
cn: 闪烁黄色箭头信号，是四信号交通灯系统中的一部分。

en: These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. (20 words)
cn: 在一些州，这种信号会出现在受保护的绿色转弯信号（即绿色箭头）之后、常亮黄色箭头之前。

en: When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. (18 words)
cn: 当闪烁黄色箭头亮起时，你可以在让行行人和其他车辆之后进行转弯。

en: Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. (19 words)
cn: 常亮黄色箭头则维持着三色信号灯系统中黄灯所代表的常规警示含义，即停车或准备停车。

en: In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. (23 words)
cn: 在设有闪烁黄色箭头的四信号系统中，常亮黄色箭头则表示让行时段即将结束。

en: The red arrow is about to start. (7 words)
cn: 红色箭头信号即将亮起。

en: Vehicles should stop if safely possible. (6 words)
cn: 在能够安全停车的情况下，车辆应当停车。

en: Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow. (10 words)
cn: 闯常亮黄色箭头信号，是有可能被开具罚单的。

en: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. (12 words)
cn: 总体而言，交通信号灯所代表的含义是相当一致的，只是存在一些细微的差异。

en: Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). (12 words)
cn: 绿灯意味着可以安全通行（不过仍应保持谨慎）。

en: Yellow means caution and yield. (5 words)
cn: 黄灯意味着小心谨慎并让行。

en: Red means danger and stop. (5 words)
cn: 红灯意味着危险，须停车。

en: Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals. (7 words)
cn: 任何时候都应保持防御性驾驶，并遵守交通信号。

en: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits—it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness. (25 words)
cn: 正念已被证明具有诸多切实的健康益处——它有助于缓解焦虑，并促进慢性病患者的康复。

en: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. (28 words)
cn: 这一修行方法所依据的洞见，最早见于古代佛教经典，即：人类具备一种能力，能够观察自身的体验，而不被其裹挟其中。

en: This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events. (48 words)
cn: 简单来说，这意味着我们可以观察自己产生某种渴望、某个愉快的念头，甚至某种令人害怕的情绪，却不必当下就做出反应，让这种感受被放大，或让思绪陷入对往事的回忆、对未来的预想之中而不断打转。

en: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. (30 words)
cn: 正念练习能够帮助我们平静身心，因为我们学会了不再以喜恶或好坏的评判来回应各种体验。

en: It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present. (12 words)
cn: 它并不会使我们变得冷漠或麻木，反而会让我们更充分地活在当下。

en: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. (22 words)
cn: 在当今世界修习正念所面临的挑战之一，是人类注意力已经发生了深刻的转变。

en: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. (24 words)
cn: 艺术家珍妮·奥德尔指出，在我们如今的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已经沦为一种可以被各大企业买卖的商品。

en: This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment. (29 words)
cn: 这种经济模式建立在手机与社交媒体所带来的科技革命之上，使得各类企业得以在每时每刻，用它们的内容精准地捕获我们的注意力。

en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. (13 words)
cn: 大多数人所使用的电子设备，都是让我们持续脱离当下时刻的一种干扰源。

en: The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. (20 words)
cn: 其结果是，我们仿佛感到自己专注和活在当下的能力，被悄悄偷走了。

en: But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love. (24 words)
