cn: 但正念能够帮助我们抵御这种注意力经济，重新去珍视那些让生活变得特别的事物，比如与自己所爱之人相伴的时光。

en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. (30 words)
cn: 大多数关于正念的研究，都聚焦于这种练习给个人带来的益处，但一些学者主张，我们不仅可以为自己修习正念，也可以为他人修习正念。

en: It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships. (8 words)
cn: 这有助于我们建立起更牢固、更健康的人际关系。

en: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. (17 words)
cn: 令人遗憾的事实是，生活在这种注意力经济之中，我们大多数人都已经变成了不擅倾听的人。

en: However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment. (31 words)
cn: 然而，正如我们可以观察自身的体验而不做出反应一样，我们同样也可以去观察他人的体验，而不被条件反射式的反应和评判所裹挟。

en: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. (16 words)
cn: 正念所馈赠的一份礼物，便是怀着悲悯之心，去倾听他人讲述自己的经历。

en: To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. (19 words)
cn: 要给出这份礼物，意味着要放下手机、关掉社交媒体，并搁置其他种种常见的干扰。

en: It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you. (29 words)
cn: 这意味着要练习在他人面前全然在场，全神贯注、不加评判地倾听对方，同时克制住把这场交流变成关于自己的冲动。

en: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one. (26 words)
cn: 如果我们用价格来衡量礼物的价值，这份礼物或许显得一文不值，但在这样一个充满干扰的世界里，它却弥足珍贵。

en: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. (14 words)
cn: 前几天，我需要登录一个自己此前从未使用过的服务。

en: Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine. (36 words)
cn: 由于我是新用户，该网站认定有必要确认我不是机器人，于是给我出了一道验证码测试，用来判断使用者究竟是人还是机器。

en: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. (16 words)
cn: 系统向我展示了一张路边场景的图片，图片上叠加着一个网格。

en: My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. (16 words)
cn: 我的“任务”是点击网格中每一个含有交通标志的方格。

en: I did so, a bit irritated. (6 words)
cn: 我照做了，心里多少有点不耐烦。

en: Then I was presented with another image and another grid—also with a request to identify road signs. (17 words)
cn: 接着，系统又给我出示了另一张图片、另一个网格——同样要求我辨认道路标志。

en: Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input. (12 words)
cn: 我像一头温顺的羔羊一样照做了，网站随后便接受了我提交的答案。

en: And then I realized what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. (23 words)
cn: 随后我才意识到，自己刚才所做的，其实是在为训练自动驾驶汽车所依赖的机器学习软件，不断充实一个数据集。

en: So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labour to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles. (31 words)
cn: 也就是说，为了获得一项将从我的输入中获利的自动化服务的使用权，我首先得付出一份无偿的劳动，来帮助提升自动驾驶汽车的性能。

en: Neat, eh? (2 words)
cn: 是不是很巧妙？

en: But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". (17 words)
cn: 但还有一层更耐人寻味的反讽值得留意：验证码本身被人们称作一种“自动化图灵测试”。

en: The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. (37 words)
cn: 你或许还记得，图灵测试最初的构想，是让人类能够判断一台机器的应答方式，是否能让人分辨不出对方究竟是人类还是机器人。

en: So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans! (20 words)
cn: 而如今，我们竟已置身于这样一个世界：反倒是机器在让我们完成各种“把戏”，来证明我们自己是人类！

en: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. (13 words)
cn: 这场前所未有的转变中最为奇怪的一点，是它竟然一直未能得到充分的讨论。

en: The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. (9 words)
cn: 这不由得让人想起“温水煮青蛙”这一比喻。

en: Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? (18 words)
cn: 我们是否已经被数字技术悄然驯化，以至于看不清自己身上正在发生着什么？

en: Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves? (25 words)
cn: 我们是否已被驯化，从而接受了一个由“智能”科技所主导的世界——为了换取便利，甚至不惜让自己也变得有几分像机器？

en: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars—Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher—argue that the answer to that question is "yes". (26 words)
cn: 在最近一本发人深省、令人震动的著作中，两位学者——法学教授布雷特·弗里施曼与哲学家埃文·塞林格——都认为，这一问题的答案是“是的”。

en: And they're right. (3 words)
cn: 而他们的判断是正确的。

en: There's nothing technophobic (技术恐惧的) about that. (5 words)
cn: 这其中并没有什么“技术恐惧症”的成分。

en: We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. (10 words)
cn: 我们塑造了自己的工具，而后工具又反过来塑造了我们。

en: Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. (10 words)
cn: 按理说，技术应当提供服务于人类目的的工具。

en: But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. (25 words)
cn: 但正如机器学习验证码所展现的那样，如今相当一部分数字技术，已经开始把人类当作实现某种并非我们自身目的的手段来看待（并加以利用）。

en: In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills (踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. (26 words)
cn: 在这一过程中，我们被贬低成了一群在踏车上欢快奔跑的老鼠，而这些踏车，正是由那些根本不把我们的利益放在心上的人所设计的。

en: So back to the frog metaphor. (6 words)
cn: 于是，我们再度回到“青蛙”这个比喻上来。

en: Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? (11 words)
cn: 我们是否足够聪明，能在为时已晚之前及时跳出这锅温水？

en: You don't even have to Google it to know the answer. (11 words)
cn: 这个问题的答案，甚至都不需要你上网搜索，就已心知肚明。
